references.authors: O'Donovan G, Lee IM, Hamer M, et al.
references.title: Association of "Weekend Warrior" and Other Leisure Time Physical Activity Patterns With Risks for All-Cause, Cardiovascular Disease, and Cancer Mortality.
references.finding: Weekend warriors (1-2 sessions/week) had all-cause mortality HR 0.70 versus inactive, similar to regularly active people (HR 0.65).

references.authors: O'Keefe JH, Patil HR, Lavie CJ, et al.
references.title: Potential adverse cardiovascular effects from excessive endurance exercise.
references.finding: Hypothesis review proposing that chronic extreme endurance training may cause atrial fibrosis, coronary calcification and arterial stiffening, while acknowledging inconsistent data and low mortality in lifelong exercisers.

references.authors: Olesen J, Gliemann L, Biensø R, et al.
references.title: Exercise training, but not resveratrol, improves metabolic and inflammatory status in skeletal muscle of aged men.
references.finding: Resveratrol added nothing to training and blunted the exercise-induced fall in muscle protein carbonylation and TNF-alpha.

references.authors: Paluch AE, Bajpai S, Bassett DR, et al.
references.title: Daily steps and all-cause mortality: a meta-analysis of 15 international cohorts.
references.finding: Versus the lowest quartile (~3,550 steps/day), mortality HR was 0.60, 0.55 and 0.47 at ~5,800, ~7,800 and ~10,900 steps/day; benefit levelled off at 6,000-8,000 steps (age 60+) and 8,000-10,000 (under 60). Step rate added little after accounting for volume.

references.authors: Paschalis V, Theodorou AA, Margaritelis NV, et al.
references.title: N-acetylcysteine supplementation increases exercise performance and reduces oxidative stress only in individuals with low levels of glutathione.
references.finding: NAC 1200 mg twice daily for 30 days improved VO2max, time trial and Wingate and lowered F2-isoprostanes only in people with low baseline glutathione; it did nothing or worsened markers in others.

references.authors: Paulsen G, Cumming KT, Holden G, et al.
references.title: Vitamin C and E supplementation hampers cellular adaptation to endurance training in humans: a double-blind, randomised, controlled trial.
references.finding: 1000 mg vitamin C plus 235 mg vitamin E for 11 weeks did not change VO2max gains (8% both groups) but blocked increases in muscle COX4 and PGC-1alpha.

references.authors: Paulsen G, Hamarsland H, Cumming KT, et al.
references.title: Vitamin C and E supplementation alters protein signalling after a strength training session, but not muscle growth during 10 weeks of training.
references.finding: Vitamin C/E blunted hypertrophy signalling after strength sessions and some strength gains (biceps curl) but not muscle growth over 10 weeks.

references.authors: Pelletier DM, Lacerte G, Goulet ED
references.title: Effects of quercetin supplementation on endurance performance and maximal oxygen consumption: a meta-analysis.
references.journal: Int J Sport Nutr Exerc Metab
references.finding: Quercetin improved endurance by 0.74% and VO2max by 1.9%, judged unlikely to be meaningful.

references.authors: Petersen AC, McKenna MJ, Medved I, et al.
references.title: Infusion with the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine attenuates early adaptive responses to exercise in human skeletal muscle.
references.finding: N-acetylcysteine infusion during cycling blocked exercise-induced JNK activation and blunted some adaptive gene responses in muscle.

references.authors: Peterson MD, Rhea MR, Sen A, et al.
references.title: Resistance exercise for muscular strength in older adults: a meta-analysis.
references.finding: Resistance training raised strength by roughly 24-33% in older adults, more with higher intensity.

references.authors: Powers SK, Jackson MJ
references.title: Exercise-induced oxidative stress: cellular mechanisms and impact on muscle force production.
references.finding: Landmark Physiological Reviews synthesis: contracting muscle makes ROS and RNS; low levels are needed for normal force and act as signals for antioxidant, stress-protein and mitochondrial genes, while high levels cause fatigue and contractile dysfunction.

references.authors: Powers SK, Radak Z, Ji LL, et al.
references.title: Reactive oxygen species promote endurance exercise-induced adaptations in skeletal muscles.
references.finding: Updated review arguing redox signalling plays an important role in endurance-training adaptation, while explicitly weighing how strong the evidence is that ROS are essential.

references.authors: Radak Z, Chung HY, Koltai E, et al.
references.title: Exercise, oxidative stress and hormesis.
references.finding: Frames exercise as hormesis: regular moderate ROS exposure up-regulates antioxidant and repair systems along a bell-shaped dose-response.

references.authors: Rahmati M, Lee H, Lee H, et al.
references.title: Associations Between Exercise Training, Physical Activity, Sedentary Behaviour and Mortality: An Umbrella Review of Meta-Analyses.
references.finding: Activity, steps and combined aerobic plus resistance training were linked to lower mortality with 'suggestive' (not convincing) evidence; sedentary-behaviour links were rated weak.

references.authors: Reynolds AN, Mann JI, Williams S, et al.
references.title: Advice to walk after meals is more effective for lowering postprandial glycaemia in type 2 diabetes mellitus than advice that does not specify timing: a randomised crossover study.
references.finding: 10 minutes of walking after each meal lowered postprandial glucose 12% more than one daily 30-minute walk (22% after the evening meal).

references.authors: Rhodes K, Braakhuis A
references.title: Performance and Side Effects of Supplementation with N-Acetylcysteine: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
references.finding: NAC (typical 5.8 g/day) did not significantly improve performance (+0.29%); side effects rose with dose.

references.authors: Ristow M, Zarse K, Oberbach A, et al.
references.title: Antioxidants prevent health-promoting effects of physical exercise in humans.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: 1000 mg vitamin C plus 400 IU vitamin E daily abolished training-induced gains in insulin sensitivity and ROS-responsive gene expression over 4 weeks.

references.authors: Ristow M
references.title: Unraveling the truth about antioxidants: mitohormesis explains ROS-induced health benefits.
references.finding: Mitohormesis commentary: transient mitochondrial ROS induce lasting defences and metabolic health; antioxidants can abolish these benefits.

references.authors: Ross R, de Lannoy L, Stotz PJ
references.title: Separate Effects of Intensity and Amount of Exercise on Interindividual Cardiorespiratory Fitness Response.
references.finding: For a fixed amount of exercise, raising intensity from 50% to 75% of VO2peak eliminated fitness non-response; low-intensity exercise failed to raise fitness in many.

references.authors: Ross R, Blair SN, Arena R, et al.
references.title: Importance of Assessing Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Clinical Practice: A Case for Fitness as a Clinical Vital Sign: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
references.finding: AHA scientific statement proposing cardiorespiratory fitness as a clinical vital sign because it predicts mortality as well as or better than traditional risk factors.

references.authors: Saint-Maurice PF, Troiano RP, Bassett DR Jr, et al.
references.title: Association of Daily Step Count and Step Intensity With Mortality Among US Adults.
references.finding: Versus 4,000 steps/day, 8,000 steps/day had HR 0.49 and 12,000 steps/day HR 0.35 for death; step intensity was not associated after adjusting for steps.

references.authors: Schnohr P, O'Keefe JH, Marott JL, et al.
references.title: Dose of jogging and long-term mortality: the Copenhagen City Heart Study.
references.finding: Light joggers had the lowest mortality (HR 0.22); strenuous joggers' HR was 1.97 with a very wide CI (0.48-8.14), interpreted by the authors as a U-shaped curve.

references.authors: Scribbans TD, Ma JK, Edgett BA, et al.
references.title: Resveratrol supplementation does not augment performance adaptations or fibre-type-specific responses to high-intensity interval training in humans.
references.finding: 150 mg/day resveratrol during 4 weeks of HIIT blunted gains in peak aerobic power and PGC-1alpha, SIRT1 and SOD2 expression.

references.authors: Shailendra P, Baldock KL, Li LSK, et al.
references.title: Resistance Training and Mortality Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
references.finding: Any resistance training was associated with 15% lower all-cause mortality; maximum reduction 27% at about 60 min/week, diminishing at higher volumes.

references.authors: Shailendra P, Baldock KL, Li LSK, et al.
references.title: Weight training and risk of all-cause, cardiovascular disease and cancer mortality among older adults.
references.finding: Any weight training was associated with modestly lower mortality (HR 0.94); more time gave only marginally greater reductions; no association in people doing no aerobic exercise.

references.authors: Smoliga JM, Blanchard OL
references.title: Recent data do not provide evidence that resveratrol causes 'mainly negative' or 'adverse' effects on exercise training in humans.
references.finding: Letter disputing that the Gliemann data show resveratrol is 'mainly negative' or adverse for exercise training in humans.

references.authors: Stamatakis E, Ahmadi MN, Gill JMR, et al.
references.title: Association of wearable device-measured vigorous intermittent lifestyle physical activity with mortality.
references.finding: Three 1-2 minute bursts of vigorous incidental activity a day were associated with 38-40% lower all-cause and cancer mortality and 48-49% lower CVD mortality.

references.authors: Stamatakis E, Ahmadi MN, Friedenreich CM, et al.
references.title: Vigorous Intermittent Lifestyle Physical Activity and Cancer Incidence Among Nonexercising Adults: The UK Biobank Accelerometry Study.
references.finding: Daily vigorous intermittent lifestyle activity was associated with lower cancer incidence in a near-linear way, with most bouts under 1 minute.

references.authors: Stamatakis E, Ahmadi M, Biswas RK, et al.
references.title: Device-measured vigorous intermittent lifestyle physical activity (VILPA) and major adverse cardiovascular events: evidence of sex differences.
references.finding: In women, a median 3.4 min/day of VILPA was associated with 45% lower major cardiovascular events (HR 0.55); associations in men were weaker and less clear.

references.authors: Stensvold D, Viken H, Steinshamn SL, et al.
references.title: Effect of exercise training for five years on all cause mortality in older adults-the Generation 100 study: randomised controlled trial.
references.finding: Five years of supervised exercise did not lower mortality versus guideline advice overall; HIIT showed a non-significant trend (HR 0.63 vs control, 0.51 vs moderate training).

references.authors: Storoschuk KL, Moran-MacDonald A, Gibala MJ, et al.
references.title: Much Ado About Zone 2: A Narrative Review Assessing the Efficacy of Zone 2 Training for Improving Mitochondrial Capacity and Cardiorespiratory Fitness in the General Population.
references.finding: Narrative review concluding current evidence does not support Zone 2 as the optimal intensity for mitochondrial or fat-oxidation capacity in the general public; higher intensities matter more at low volumes.

references.authors: Stunes AK, Syversen U, Berntsen S, et al.
references.title: High doses of vitamin C plus E reduce strength training-induced improvements in areal bone mineral density in elderly men.
references.finding: 1000 mg vitamin C plus 235 mg vitamin E blunted the strength-training-induced rise in hip and spine bone density.

references.authors: Takahashi M, Miyashita M, Park JH, et al.
references.title: Effects of Breaking Sitting by Standing and Acute Exercise on Postprandial Oxidative Stress.
references.finding: After a sitting day, postprandial d-ROMs (a crude oxidative marker) tended to rise, but not after a standing or exercise day.

references.authors: Tari AR, Brissach DE, Ingeström EML, et al.
references.title: Survival of the fittest? Peak oxygen uptake and all-cause mortality among older adults in Norway.
references.finding: Moderately fit older adults had 59-66% lower 5-year mortality than unfit peers, with no further reduction at higher fitness.

references.authors: Tikkanen E, Gustafsson S, Amar D, et al.
references.title: Biological Insights Into Muscular Strength: Genetic Findings in the UK Biobank.
references.finding: Mendelian randomization suggested higher grip strength protects against coronary heart disease (OR 0.69) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.75).

references.authors: Torres-Rojo FI, Enríquez-Del Castillo LA, González-Chávez SA, et al.
references.title: Effect of exercise intensity on redox biomarkers in healthy adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
references.finding: Training raised antioxidant capacity and lowered oxidant markers overall; effects were significant for vigorous protocols and not for non-vigorous ones.

references.authors: Vaamonde D, Da Silva-Grigoletto ME, García-Manso JM, et al.
references.title: Physically active men show better semen parameters and hormone values than sedentary men.
references.finding: Physically active men had better progressive motility and morphology and higher FSH, LH and testosterone than sedentary men.

references.authors: Wahib HR, Afroundeh R, Farzizadeh R, et al.
references.title: Physical activity and oxidative stress biomarkers in humans: a systematic review and quantitative meta-analysis.
references.finding: Physical activity lowered MDA (SMD -1.02) and raised total antioxidant status, without consistent enzyme changes; heterogeneity was very high (I2 ~95%).

references.authors: Weston KS, Wisløff U, Coombes JS
references.title: High-intensity interval training in patients with lifestyle-induced cardiometabolic disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: In lifestyle-related cardiometabolic disease, HIIT raised VO2peak 3.0 mL/kg/min (about 9%) more than moderate continuous training.

references.authors: Wewege M, van den Berg R, Ward RE, et al.
references.title: The effects of high-intensity interval training vs. moderate-intensity continuous training on body composition in overweight and obese adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: HIIT and moderate continuous training gave similar modest reductions in body fat in overweight adults; HIIT took less time.

references.authors: Wise LA, Cramer DW, Hornstein MD, et al.
references.title: Physical activity and semen quality among men attending an infertility clinic.
references.finding: Regular exercise was not associated with semen quality overall, but cycling 5+ h/week was linked to low sperm concentration (OR 1.92).

references.authors: Wise LA, Rothman KJ, Mikkelsen EM, et al.
references.title: A prospective cohort study of physical activity and time to pregnancy.
references.finding: Vigorous activity of 5+ h/week was associated with lower fecundability (FR 0.68) in lean women; moderate activity with slightly higher fecundability (FR 1.18).

references.authors: Wise LA, Wang TR, Ulrichsen SP, et al.
references.title: A prospective study of male physical activity and fecundability.
references.finding: Male vigorous, moderate or total activity was not consistently associated with couples' fecundability.

references.authors: Yfanti C, Akerström T, Nielsen S, et al.
references.title: Antioxidant supplementation does not alter endurance training adaptation.
references.finding: Vitamin C plus E for 12 weeks of strenuous cycling did not change gains in VO2max, power output or lactate threshold.

references.authors: Yfanti C, Nielsen AR, Akerström T, et al.
references.title: Effect of antioxidant supplementation on insulin sensitivity in response to endurance exercise training.
references.finding: Vitamin C plus E did not prevent training-induced improvement in insulin sensitivity.

references.authors: Zhou Z, Chen C, Teo EC, et al.
references.title: Intracellular Oxidative Stress Induced by Physical Exercise in Adults: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
references.finding: Oxidative damage depended on intensity times volume; HIIT and moderate aerobic exercise had the lowest probability of inducing large intracellular oxidative stress.

references.authors: Zou P, Wang X, Sun L, et al.
references.title: Semen Quality in Chinese College Students: Associations With Depression and Physical Activity in a Cross-Sectional Study.
references.finding: Men with low physical activity had 23% lower total sperm count.

references.authors: Castanedo-Cazares JP, Hernandez-Blanco D, Carlos-Ortega B, et al.
references.title: Near-visible light and UV photoprotection in the treatment of melasma: a double-blind randomized trial.
references.finding: Adding iron oxide (visible-light-blocking) to an SPF 50+ sunscreen improved melasma severity scores by 15% and colorimetry by 28% more than UV-only sunscreen over 8 weeks with hydroquinone.

references.authors: Correia G, Magina S
references.title: Efficacy of topical vitamin C in melasma and photoaging: A systematic review.
references.finding: Systematic review of randomized trials: topical vitamin C smoothed wrinkled skin and lightened pigmentation, but all studies were small and long-term use may be needed for visible change.

references.authors: De Dormael R, Bastien P, Sextius P, et al.
references.title: Vitamin C Prevents Ultraviolet-induced Pigmentation in Healthy Volunteers: Bayesian Meta-analysis Results from 31 Randomized Controlled versus Vehicle Clinical Studies.
references.finding: A Bayesian pooling of 31 intra-individual vehicle-controlled studies run by L'Oreal found topical vitamin C reduced UV-induced pigmentation dose-dependently but did not speed depigmentation afterwards.

references.authors: Diffey B, Cadars B
references.title: An appraisal of the need for infrared radiation protection in sunscreens.
references.finding: Annual solar IR-A doses are comparable to those of furnace workers who show little chronic skin damage, so there is no compelling evidence that solar IR causes observable skin harm and IR-protection claims in sunscreens are premature.

references.authors: Fisher GJ, Wang ZQ, Datta SC, et al.
references.title: Pathophysiology of premature skin aging induced by ultraviolet light.
references.finding: A single UV exposure induced collagenase, gelatinase and stromelysin in human skin and raised collagen breakdown by 58%; repeated exposures kept MMP activity elevated for 7 days, and tretinoin pretreatment blocked MMP induction by 70-80%.

references.authors: Green A, Williams G, Neale R, et al.
references.title: Daily sunscreen application and betacarotene supplementation in prevention of basal-cell and squamous-cell carcinomas of the skin: a randomised controlled trial.
references.finding: Daily SPF 15+ sunscreen for 4.5 years did not change the number of people developing basal- or squamous-cell carcinoma, but cut the number of squamous-cell tumours by 39% (rate ratio 0.61); 30 mg/day beta-carotene had no effect on either cancer.

references.authors: Green AC, Williams GM, Logan V, et al.
references.title: Reduced melanoma after regular sunscreen use: randomized trial follow-up.
references.finding: Ten years after the 4.5-year Nambour trial ended, 11 primary melanomas occurred in the daily-sunscreen group vs 22 in the discretionary group (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.24-1.02, P=0.051); invasive melanomas 3 vs 11 (HR 0.27).

references.authors: Grether-Beck S, Marini A, Jaenicke T, et al.
references.title: Effective photoprotection of human skin against infrared A radiation by topically applied antioxidants: results from a vehicle controlled, double-blind, randomized study.
references.finding: SPF 30 sunscreen plus an antioxidant cocktail (grape seed extract, vitamin E, ubiquinone, vitamin C) reduced IR-A-induced MMP-1 in human skin, whereas the same sunscreen alone did not; the outcome was a molecular marker, not visible aging.

references.authors: Guyuron B, Rowe DJ, Weinfeld AB, et al.
references.title: Factors contributing to the facial aging of identical twins.
references.finding: Within identical twin pairs, longer smoking, more sun exposure and lack of sunscreen were associated with an older appearance; heavier weight looked older before 40 but younger after 40.

references.authors: Hercberg S, Ezzedine K, Guinot C, et al.
references.title: Antioxidant supplementation increases the risk of skin cancers in women but not in men.
references.finding: SU.VI.MAX: a nutritional-dose antioxidant capsule (vitamin C, E, beta-carotene, selenium, zinc) for 7.5 years raised skin-cancer incidence in women (HR 1.68) and melanoma (HR 4.31, few cases), with no significant effect in men.

references.authors: Hughes MC, Williams GM, Baker P, et al.
references.title: Sunscreen and prevention of skin aging: a randomized trial.
references.finding: Over 4.5 years, daily broad-spectrum sunscreen users showed no detectable increase in skin aging and 24% less photoaging than discretionary users (relative odds 0.76, 95% CI 0.59-0.98); 30 mg/day beta-carotene had no overall effect.

references.authors: Humbert PG, Haftek M, Creidi P, et al.
references.title: Topical ascorbic acid on photoaged skin. Clinical, topographical and ultrastructural evaluation: double-blind study vs. placebo.
references.finding: In a 6-month double-blind trial, 5% vitamin C cream improved clinical global scores, skin microrelief and deep furrows versus its vehicle, with ultrastructural evidence of elastic-tissue repair.

references.authors: Kafi R, Kwak HS, Schumacher WE, et al.
references.title: Improvement of naturally aged skin with vitamin A (retinol).
references.finding: 0.4% retinol applied up to 3 times weekly for 24 weeks reduced fine wrinkling versus vehicle and increased glycosaminoglycans and procollagen I in biopsies.

references.authors: Liebel F, Kaur S, Ruvolo E, et al.
references.title: Irradiation of skin with visible light induces reactive oxygen species and matrix-degrading enzymes.
references.finding: Visible light (400-700 nm) induced ROS, pro-inflammatory cytokines and MMP-1 in skin equivalents and free-radical activity in human skin; standard UVA/UVB sunscreens barely reduced this, while a sunscreen with an antioxidant combination did (Johnson & Johnson authors).

references.authors: Lin JY, Selim MA, Shea CR, et al.
references.title: UV photoprotection by combination topical antioxidants vitamin C and vitamin E.
references.finding: In pig skin, 15% L-ascorbic acid plus 1% alpha-tocopherol applied for 4 days gave a 4-fold protection against UV erythema and sunburn cells, better than either vitamin alone, and reduced thymine dimers.

references.authors: Lin FH, Lin JY, Gupta RD, et al.
references.title: Ferulic acid stabilizes a solution of vitamins C and E and doubles its photoprotection of skin.
references.finding: Adding ferulic acid to 15% L-ascorbic acid plus 1% alpha-tocopherol improved the solution's chemical stability and doubled its photoprotection of (pig) skin from about 4-fold to about 8-fold, also reducing thymine dimers.

references.authors: Loureiro KD, Kao KK, Jones KL, et al.
references.title: Minor malformations characteristic of the retinoic acid embryopathy and other birth outcomes in children of women exposed to topical tretinoin during early pregnancy.
references.finding: First-trimester exposure to topical tretinoin was not associated with more miscarriage, major birth defects, or the minor malformations typical of retinoic-acid embryopathy.

references.authors: Matta MK, Florian J, Zusterzeel R, et al.
references.title: Effect of Sunscreen Application on Plasma Concentration of Sunscreen Active Ingredients: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
references.finding: All six common organic sunscreen filters exceeded the FDA 0.5 ng/mL systemic-absorption threshold after a single application; the clinical significance is unknown and the authors did not advise against sunscreen.

references.authors: Mouret S, Baudouin C, Charveron M, et al.
references.title: Cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers are predominant DNA lesions in whole human skin exposed to UVA radiation.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: In whole human skin, UVA produced cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers in larger amounts than the oxidative lesion 8-oxo-dG, and UVA-induced dimers were repaired more slowly than UVB-induced ones; skin protected keratinocytes well against UVB but weakly against UVA.

references.authors: Passeron T, Bouillon R, Callender V, et al.
references.title: Sunscreen photoprotection and vitamin D status.
references.finding: International expert consensus (including industry scientists): broad-spectrum sunscreens that prevent sunburn are unlikely to compromise vitamin D status in healthy people; at-risk groups should be screened and supplemented.

references.authors: Pinnell SR, Yang H, Omar M, et al.
references.title: Topical L-ascorbic acid: percutaneous absorption studies.
references.finding: In pig skin, L-ascorbic acid only penetrated when formulated at pH below 3.5, absorption peaked at 20% concentration, tissue levels saturated after 3 daily applications with a ~4-day half-life, and common derivatives did not raise skin vitamin C.

references.authors: Rueegg CS, Stenehjem JS, Egger M, et al.
references.title: Challenges in assessing the sunscreen-melanoma association.
references.finding: Sunscreen-melanoma associations varied by design; adjusting for sun exposure, sunburn and phenotype consistently moved estimates toward protection, and the RCT showed HR 0.49, while cohort studies showed positive associations likely due to confounding.

references.authors: Schroeder P, Lademann J, Darvin ME, et al.
references.title: Infrared radiation-induced matrix metalloproteinase in human skin: implications for protection.
references.finding: Physiological doses of near-infrared (IR-A) raised dermal MMP-1 in 80% of people and lowered skin antioxidant content; topical antioxidants prevented the MMP-1 rise, a mitochondrial ROS-mediated response.

references.authors: Silva ESD, Tavares R, Paulitsch FDS, et al.
references.title: Use of sunscreen and risk of melanoma and non-melanoma skin cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Mostly case-control studies showed no association between sunscreen use and melanoma (OR 1.10) or non-melanoma skin cancer (OR 0.99); early studies' positive associations faded over time.

references.authors: Vierkötter A, Schikowski T, Ranft U, et al.
references.title: Airborne particle exposure and extrinsic skin aging.
references.finding: Higher traffic-related soot and particle exposure at home was associated with about 20% more pigment spots on the face and, less strongly, more wrinkles.

references.authors: Weinstock MA, Bingham SF, Lew RA, et al.
references.title: Topical tretinoin therapy and all-cause mortality.
references.finding: The VATTC trial was stopped 6 months early because of excess deaths in the tretinoin group; the difference persisted after adjustment, but the investigators judged a causal effect unlikely.

references.authors: Weinstock MA, Bingham SF, Digiovanna JJ, et al.
references.title: Tretinoin and the prevention of keratinocyte carcinoma (Basal and squamous cell carcinoma of the skin): a veterans affairs randomized chemoprevention trial.
references.finding: VATTC: high-dose topical tretinoin 0.1% for 1.5-5.5 years did not reduce basal-cell (53% vs 54% at 5 years) or squamous-cell carcinoma (28% vs 31%) or actinic keratoses in high-risk veterans.

references.authors: Weiss JS, Ellis CN, Headington JT, et al.
references.title: Topical tretinoin improves photoaged skin. A double-blind vehicle-controlled study.
references.finding: Tretinoin cream improved photoaging on all treated forearms and 14 of 15 treated faces over 16 weeks, versus no improvement on vehicle-treated faces; irritation was the main side effect.

references.authors: Almeida FN, Leray C, Albignac M, et al.
references.title: Py-GC-MS/MS quantification of microplastics in vertebrate tissues: Addressing false positives of polyethylene.
references.finding: Lipids interfere with polyethylene quantification by Py-GC/MS; using longer-chain markers to avoid false positives raised the polyethylene quantification limit to 50 ug/g.

references.authors: Amato-Lourenço LF, Dantas KC, Júnior GR, et al.
references.title: Microplastics in the Olfactory Bulb of the Human Brain.
references.finding: Micro-FTIR found 16 microplastic particles and fibres (5.5-26 um, mostly polypropylene) in the olfactory bulbs of 8 of 15 decedents, with clean procedural blanks.

references.authors: A Monikh F, Materić D, Valsami-Jones E, et al.
references.title: Challenges in studying microplastics in human brain.
references.finding: Correspondence from microplastic analytical chemists in Nature Medicine setting out the challenges of measuring microplastics in human brain, in response to the Nihart study.

references.authors: Andersson AG, Xu Y, Kärrman A, et al.
references.title: Serum, urinary and fecal concentrations of perfluoroalkyl substances after interventions with cholestyramine/colesevelam and probenecid - cross-over trials in Ronneby, Sweden.
references.finding: Bile acid sequestrants raised faecal PFOS excretion 23-fold; 12 weeks of colesevelam lowered serum PFOS by 38% versus 2% in the control period; probenecid did not help.

references.authors: Blaauwendraad SM, Boxem AJ, Gaillard R, et al.
references.title: Periconception bisphenol and phthalate concentrations in women and men, time to pregnancy, and risk of miscarriage.
references.n: 938 women preconception; 1366 women and 1202 men in early pregnancy
references.finding: BPS in women was linked to longer time to pregnancy, but several phthalate metabolites were linked to shorter time to pregnancy; authors call the findings hypothesis-generating.

references.authors: Busse K, Ebner I, Humpf HU, et al.
references.title: Comment on "Plastic Teabags Release Billions of Microparticles and Nanoparticles into Tea".
references.finding: Published comment challenging the Hernandez 2019 teabag particle findings (followed by an author response).

references.authors: Carwile JL, Luu HT, Bassett LS, et al.
references.title: Polycarbonate bottle use and urinary bisphenol A concentrations.
references.finding: One week of drinking cold beverages from polycarbonate bottles raised urinary BPA by 69%.

references.authors: Carwile JL, Ye X, Zhou X, et al.
references.title: Canned soup consumption and urinary bisphenol A: a randomized crossover trial.
references.finding: One serving of canned soup daily for 5 days raised urinary BPA from 1.1 to 20.8 ug/L (about 1,200%) versus fresh soup.

references.authors: Castellini C, Muselli M, Parisi A, et al.
references.title: Association between urinary bisphenol A concentrations and semen quality: A meta-analytic study.
references.finding: Urinary BPA was only weakly associated with lower sperm motility, and the association disappeared after correction for publication bias; authors judged it clinically negligible.

references.authors: Charifson M, Seok E, Wang Y, et al.
references.title: Evaluating associations of bisphenol and phthalate exposure with time to pregnancy and subfecundity in a New York City pregnancy cohort.
references.finding: Total bisphenol exposure and some phthalate groups were associated with longer time to pregnancy and higher odds of subfecundity, unlike most earlier null studies.

references.authors: Chen JC, Baumert BO, Li Y, et al.
references.title: Associations of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, polychlorinated biphenyls, organochlorine pesticides, and polybrominated diphenyl ethers with oxidative stress markers: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Across persistent pollutants, organochlorine pesticides showed consistent links with oxidative stress markers, but PFAS associations were mostly inconsistent.

references.authors: Cox KD, Covernton GA, Davies HL, et al.
references.title: Human Consumption of Microplastics.
references.finding: Estimated US intake of 39,000-52,000 microplastic particles per year from food (74,000-121,000 with inhalation); bottled-water-only drinkers may ingest ~90,000 extra particles per year versus ~4,000 for tap.

references.authors: Cuffney M, Wilkie AA, Kotlarz N, et al.
references.title: Factors associated with per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) serum concentrations in residents of New Hanover County, North Carolina: The GenX exposure study.
references.finding: Drinking municipal water treated with a home filter was associated with lower serum levels of all seven PFAS measured versus unfiltered tap water.

references.authors: Delaere I, Harris K, Gaskin S, et al.
references.title: Changes in serum perfluorooctane sulfonic acid and perfluorohexane sulfonic acid concentrations in firefighters accessing a voluntary perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances reduction treatment program.
references.finding: Firefighters using plasma donation and/or cholestyramine showed faster PFOS decline (apparent half-life 1.2 vs 7.3 years) than untreated colleagues; small, non-randomized, no statistical testing.

references.authors: den Braver-Sewradj SP, van Spronsen R, Hessel EVS
references.title: Substitution of bisphenol A: a review of the carcinogenicity, reproductive toxicity, and endocrine disruption potential of alternative substances.
references.finding: Data for BPS, BPAF and to a lesser extent BPF indicate a reproductive-toxicity hazard with a possible endocrine mode of action; for most alternatives data are very limited or absent.

references.authors: Due I, Rubio L, Catalán J, et al.
references.title: Mammalian reproductive and developmental toxicity of micro- and nanoplastics: a critical appraisal of evidence using the SciRAP tool.
references.finding: Systematic appraisal of in vivo mammalian micro/nanoplastic reproductive studies: many report harm to testis, ovary and gametes, but particle characterization, dose and dose-response were often missing.

references.authors: EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (EFSA CONTAM Panel); Schrenk D, Bignami M, et al.
references.title: Risk to human health related to the presence of perfluoroalkyl substances in food.
references.finding: EFSA set a tolerable weekly intake of 4.4 ng/kg body weight for the sum of PFOA, PFNA, PFHxS and PFOS, based on reduced vaccine antibody responses in children, and noted parts of the European population exceed it.

references.authors: EFSA Panel on Food Contact Materials, Enzymes and Processing Aids (CEP); Lambré C, Barat Baviera JM, et al.
references.title: Re-evaluation of the risks to public health related to the presence of bisphenol A (BPA) in foodstuffs.
references.finding: EFSA lowered the BPA tolerable daily intake from 4 ug/kg to 0.2 ng/kg body weight per day (20,000-fold), based on immune (Th17) effects in mice, and concluded that average dietary exposure exceeds it by two to three orders of magnitude.

references.authors: Ehrlich V, Bil W, Vandebriel R, et al.
references.title: Consideration of pathways for immunotoxicity of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).
references.finding: Review of PFAS immunotoxicity: substantial experimental and epidemiological evidence that several PFAS affect immune function, via NF-kB/PPAR signalling, calcium signalling and oxidative stress among other pathways.

references.authors: Ferguson KK, McElrath TF, Chen YH, et al.
references.title: Urinary phthalate metabolites and biomarkers of oxidative stress in pregnant women: a repeated measures analysis.
references.finding: IQR increases in urinary phthalate metabolites were associated with higher urinary 8-OHdG and 8-isoprostane across repeated measures in pregnancy.

references.authors: Fillman T, Coffin S, Ta B, et al.
references.title: Associations between PFAS in public water system drinking water and serum among Southern California adults.
references.finding: People whose public water had detectable PFAS had higher serum PFAS (e.g., PFHxS +80%, PFOA +30%, PFOS +31% with treated-water detections).

references.authors: Garcia MA, Liu R, Nihart A, et al.
references.title: Quantitation and identification of microplastics accumulation in human placental specimens using pyrolysis gas chromatography mass spectrometry.
references.finding: Py-GC/MS found microplastics in all 62 placentas (6.5-685 ug/g, mean 127 ug/g), mostly polyethylene, while microscopy and FTIR on a subset saw particles >1 um but no nanoplastics.

references.authors: Gasiorowski R, Forbes MK, Silver G, et al.
references.title: Effect of Plasma and Blood Donations on Levels of Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances in Firefighters in Australia: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
references.finding: Over 12 months, plasma donation every 6 weeks lowered serum PFOS by 2.9 ng/mL and PFHxS by 1.1 ng/mL, and blood donation every 12 weeks lowered PFOS by 1.1 ng/mL, versus no change with observation.

references.authors: Glazier HA
references.title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Atheromas.
references.finding: Letter to the editor responding to Marfella 2024 (NEJM correspondence on microplastics in atheromas).

references.authors: Grandjean P, Andersen EW, Budtz-Jørgensen E, et al.
references.title: Serum vaccine antibody concentrations in children exposed to perfluorinated compounds.
references.finding: A doubling of child serum PFAS at age 5 was associated with 49% lower overall tetanus/diphtheria antibody concentrations at age 7.

references.authors: Harley KG, Kogut K, Madrigal DS, et al.
references.title: Reducing Phthalate, Paraben, and Phenol Exposure from Personal Care Products in Adolescent Girls: Findings from the HERMOSA Intervention Study.
references.finding: Three days of personal-care products labelled free of phthalates, parabens, triclosan and BP-3 lowered urinary MEP by 27%, methyl/propyl paraben by ~44% and triclosan and BP-3 by ~36%.

references.authors: Hernandez LM, Xu EG, Larsson HCE, et al.
references.title: Plastic Teabags Release Billions of Microparticles and Nanoparticles into Tea.
references.finding: Steeping one plastic (nylon/PET) teabag at 95 C released about 11.6 billion microplastic and 3.1 billion nanoplastic particles into the cup.

references.authors: Hernández AF, Lacasaña M, Tsatsakis AM, et al.
references.title: Cellular and Molecular Mechanisms of Micro- and Nanoplastics Driving Adverse Human Health Effects.
references.finding: Narrative review: oxidative stress, inflammation, barrier disruption and immune dysregulation are plausible mechanisms, but human data are limited to biomonitoring and animal studies use pristine particles at high doses.

references.authors: Holda MK, Batko J
references.title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Atheromas.
references.finding: Letter to the editor responding to Marfella 2024 (NEJM correspondence on microplastics in atheromas).

references.authors: Hu CJ, Garcia MA, Nihart A, et al.
references.title: Microplastic presence in dog and human testis and its potential association with sperm count and weights of testis and epididymis.
references.finding: Pyrolysis-GC/MS reported microplastics in every testis (mean 328 ug/g in humans, 123 ug/g in dogs), mostly polyethylene; in dogs PVC and PET levels correlated with lower normalized testis weight.

references.authors: Hu CJ, Garcia MA, Nihart A, et al.
references.title: Response to comment on: "Microplastic presence in dog and human testis and its potential association with sperm count and weights of testis and epididymis".
references.finding: Authors' reply: controls were described in their placenta paper; after re-evaluation only 6 of the 12 polymers (PE, PP, PVC, nylon, SBR, PET) give enough confidence for health-based work.

references.authors: Hussain KA, Romanova S, Okur I, et al.
references.title: Assessing the Release of Microplastics and Nanoplastics from Plastic Containers and Reusable Food Pouches: Implications for Human Health.
references.finding: Microwaving polypropylene containers and polyethylene pouches released the most particles (up to 4.2 million micro- and 2.1 billion nanoplastics per cm2 in 3 min); months of fridge or room storage also released particles.

references.authors: Hussey MR, Kornberg TG, Sherrick JM, et al.
references.title: The relationship between PFAS exposure and dyslipidemia: an updated review, meta-analysis, and evaluation of bias.
references.finding: Pooled cross-sectional data link PFOA and PFOS to higher total and LDL cholesterol, but longitudinal estimates trended to null and heterogeneity tracked confounding and recruitment from contaminated areas.

references.authors: Kalkman DN, Renkens MPL, Grundeken MJ
references.title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Atheromas.
references.finding: Letter to the editor responding to Marfella 2024 (NEJM correspondence on microplastics in atheromas).

references.authors: Lane T, de Ruijter VN, Wardani I, et al.
references.title: A QA/QC screening framework to assess studies reporting microplastic presence in human organs, tissues, and bodily fluids.
references.finding: A 14-criterion QA/QC screen of human-tissue microplastic studies found none met all essential criteria; blank documentation, positive controls and sample representativeness were common gaps.

references.authors: Leslie HA, van Velzen MJM, Brandsma SH, et al.
references.title: Discovery and quantification of plastic particle pollution in human blood.
references.finding: Double-shot Py-GC/MS quantified plastic particles >=700 nm in whole blood (mean of quantifiable sum 1.6 ug/mL), mainly PET, polyethylene and styrene polymers.

references.authors: Li Y, Fletcher T, Mucs D, et al.
references.title: Half-lives of PFOS, PFHxS and PFOA after end of exposure to contaminated drinking water.
references.finding: After contaminated water was replaced, serum PFHxS, PFOS and PFOA fell 13%, 20% and 26% per year (half-lives 5.3, 3.4 and 2.7 years), faster in women.

references.authors: Li D, Shi Y, Yang L, et al.
references.title: Microplastic release from the degradation of polypropylene feeding bottles during infant formula preparation.
references.finding: Polypropylene infant feeding bottles released up to 16 million microplastic particles per litre during formula preparation, more with sterilization and hot water.

references.authors: Lin CY, Lee HL, Hwang YT, et al.
references.title: The association between total serum isomers of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, lipid profiles, and the DNA oxidative/nitrative stress biomarkers in middle-aged Taiwanese adults.
references.finding: Linear PFOS was associated with higher urinary 8-OHdG and 8-nitroguanine and with LDL cholesterol.

references.authors: Lü L, Liu Y, Yang Y, et al.
references.title: Bisphenol A Exposure Interferes with Reproductive Hormones and Decreases Sperm Counts: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Epidemiological Studies.
references.finding: Urinary BPA was associated with slightly lower sperm concentration and total count and with higher SHBG and estradiol, but not robustly with below-reference semen quality.

references.authors: Lucas A, Harray A, Duong L, et al.
references.title: Randomised controlled trial of a low plastic diet and lifestyle intervention for adults with cardiometabolic risk factors: the Plastic Exposure Reduction Transforms Health (PERTH) trial - a protocol.
references.finding: Protocol of the PERTH RCT testing whether a 4-week low-plastic diet and lifestyle intervention lowers urinary bisphenols and phthalates and improves cardiometabolic markers.

references.authors: MacKeown H, Magi E, Di Carro M, et al.
references.title: Removal of perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances from tap water by means of point-of-use treatment: A review.
references.finding: Point-of-use filters (activated carbon, ion exchange, reverse osmosis) can remove PFAS, but only five real-life studies exist, short-chain PFAS are harder to remove and poorly maintained carbon can raise PFAS in water.

references.authors: Marfella R, Prattichizzo F, Sardu C, et al.
references.title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Atheromas and Cardiovascular Events.
references.finding: Polyethylene was detected in 58% of excised carotid plaques (PVC in 12%); patients with detectable plastic had a higher risk of heart attack, stroke or death (HR 4.53, 95% CI 2.00-10.27).

references.authors: Marfella R, Prattichizzo F
references.title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Atheromas. Reply.
references.finding: Authors' reply to the NEJM letters on microplastics in atheromas.

references.authors: Mhaouty-Kodja S, Zalko D, Tait S, et al.
references.title: A critical review to identify data gaps and improve risk assessment of bisphenol A alternatives for human health.
references.finding: Critical review: BPS and BPF are found worldwide in people and are being regulated because of toxicity; newer BPA alternatives have large toxicology data gaps (risk of regrettable substitution).

references.authors: Møller JJ, Lyngberg AC, Hammer PEC, et al.
references.title: Substantial decrease of PFAS with anion exchange resin treatment - A clinical cross-over trial.
references.finding: Cholestyramine 4 g three times daily for 12 weeks lowered serum PFOS by 60% (from a median of 191 ng/mL) and other PFAS by 15-44%, with no serious adverse events.

references.authors: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
references.title: Guidance on PFAS Exposure, Testing, and Clinical Follow-Up
references.finding: NASEM clinical guidance: offer PFAS blood testing to likely exposed patients; for the summed serum level of 7 PFAS, <2 ng/mL usual care, 2-20 ng/mL exposure reduction plus lipid screening, >20 ng/mL add thyroid testing and kidney/testicular cancer and ulcerative colitis assessment.

references.authors: Nihart AJ, Garcia MA, El Hayek E, et al.
references.title: Bioaccumulation of microplastics in decedent human brains.
references.n: decedent brain, liver and kidney samples (2016 and 2024) plus 12 dementia brains
references.finding: Py-GC/MS reported median ~4,900 ug/g of plastic (mostly polyethylene) in 2024 brain samples, 7-30x higher than liver or kidney, rising from 2016 to 2024, and higher still (median ~26,000 ug/g) in dementia brains.

references.authors: Nihart AJ, Garcia MA, El Hayek E, et al.
references.title: Author Correction: Bioaccumulation of microplastics in decedent human brains.
references.finding: Author correction to Nihart 2025: duplicated supplementary microscopy panels removed, mis-sized scale bars fixed, an omitted sample-preparation step added and a supplementary particle-count table recalculated.

references.authors: Peng CY, Tsai EM, Kao TH, et al.
references.title: Canned food intake and urinary bisphenol a concentrations: a randomized crossover intervention study.
references.finding: A canned-food meal raised urinary BPA by up to 206% at 4 h versus fresh food, returning to baseline by 24 h.

references.authors: Plachetka L, Stanislas V, Bauer A, et al.
references.title: Urinary bisphenol levels and blood pressure after soda consumption from cans, PET and glass bottles.
references.finding: Drinking soda from cans raised urinary BPA by 22% versus PET bottles; BPS, BPF and BPE were detected independent of packaging.

references.authors: Qian N, Gao X, Lang X, et al.
references.title: Rapid single-particle chemical imaging of nanoplastics by SRS microscopy.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Stimulated Raman scattering imaging counted about 240,000 plastic particles per litre of bottled water, about 90% of them nanoplastics, orders of magnitude more than earlier microplastic-only counts.

references.authors: Rauert C, Charlton N, Bagley A, et al.
references.title: Assessing the Efficacy of Pyrolysis-Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry for Nanoplastic and Microplastic Analysis in Human Blood.
references.finding: Validation study concluding that Py-GC/MS is currently not suitable for polyethylene and PVC in biological matrices because of interferences, with realistic detection limits up to 20x higher than nominal and no other polymers detectable in human blood.

references.authors: Rudel RA, Gray JM, Engel CL, et al.
references.title: Food packaging and bisphenol A and bis(2-ethyhexyl) phthalate exposure: findings from a dietary intervention.
references.finding: Three days of fresh, unpackaged food cut urinary BPA by 66% and DEHP metabolites by 53-56% (geometric means).

references.authors: Sathyanarayana S, Alcedo G, Saelens BE, et al.
references.title: Unexpected results in a randomized dietary trial to reduce phthalate and bisphenol A exposures.
references.finding: A 5-day catered "low-exposure" diet unexpectedly raised urinary DEHP metabolites (median 284 to 7028 nmol/g) and BPA because ingredients such as ground coriander and milk were contaminated.

references.authors: Schlezinger JJ, Bello A, Mangano KM, et al.
references.title: Per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in circulation in a Canadian population: their association with serum-liver enzyme biomarkers and piloting a novel method to reduce serum-PFAS.
references.finding: In a 4-week dietary fibre trial, long-chain PFAS fell significantly only in the fibre group (secondary analysis; total PFAS fell in both arms).

references.authors: Schwabl P, Köppel S, Königshofer P, et al.
references.title: Detection of Various Microplastics in Human Stool: A Prospective Case Series.
references.finding: All 8 stool samples contained microplastics (median 20 particles per 10 g, 50-500 um), mostly polypropylene and PET.

references.authors: Siwakoti RC, Park S, Ferguson KK, et al.
references.title: Prenatal per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and maternal oxidative stress: Evidence from the LIFECODES study.
references.finding: Each IQR increase in plasma PFOS was associated with 9.7% higher urinary 8-isoprostane; other PFAS showed mixed or inverse associations.

references.authors: Soltani NS, Taylor MP, Wilson SP
references.title: International quantification of microplastics in indoor dust: prevalence, exposure and risk assessment.
references.finding: Synthetic fibres (polyester, polyamide) were common in household dust, mainly from indoor sources; more frequent vacuuming was associated with less microplastic in dust.

references.authors: Symeonides C, Aromataris E, Mulders Y, et al.
references.title: An Umbrella Review of Meta-Analyses Evaluating Associations between Human Health and Exposure to Major Classes of Plastic-Associated Chemicals.
references.finding: Umbrella review: BPA linked to PCOS, type 2 diabetes and CVD; phthalates to pregnancy loss, reduced sperm quality and insulin resistance; some PFAS to lower birth weight; no meta-analyses existed for microplastics.

references.authors: Tefera Y, Shearer C, Day M, et al.
references.title: Is drinking water with low PFAS a significant source of human exposure? Evidence summary.
references.finding: Drinking water with low PFAS (10-100 ng/L) measurably raised blood PFAS, most consistently PFHxS, especially in children and heavy water drinkers; below ~10 ng/L links were inconsistent.

references.authors: Thomas KV, Belz S, Booth AM, et al.
references.title: Communicating Confidence in the Reliability of Micro- and Nanoplastic Identification in Human Health Studies.
references.finding: Proposes confidence levels for micro/nanoplastic identification in human studies, requiring orthogonal analytical techniques and transparent reporting of contamination and limits.

references.authors: Uppu RM, Peijnenburg W, Hays SM
references.title: Comment on: "Microplastic presence in dog and human testis and its potential association with sperm count and weights of testis and epididymis".
references.finding: Comment on Hu 2024: no reported blanks, negative/positive or background controls, unvalidated digestion and ultracentrifugation steps, and no LOD/LOQ, internal standards or matrix spikes for the Py-GC/MS method.

references.authors: Vom Saal FS, Antoniou M, Belcher SM, et al.
references.title: The Conflict between Regulatory Agencies over the 20,000-Fold Lowering of the Tolerable Daily Intake (TDI) for Bisphenol A (BPA) by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA).
references.finding: Commentary endorsing EFSA's 20,000-fold BPA TDI cut and criticizing the German BfR and US FDA for maintaining higher limits based on guideline studies.

references.authors: Wang X, Tian S
references.title: Microplastics and Nanoplastics in Atheromas.
references.finding: Letter to the editor responding to Marfella 2024 (NEJM correspondence on microplastics in atheromas).

references.authors: Wang H, He H, Wei Y, et al.
references.title: Do phthalates and their metabolites cause poor semen quality? A systematic review and meta-analysis of epidemiological studies on risk of decline in sperm quality.
references.finding: Urinary MBP and MBzP and semen DEHP were associated with lower sperm concentration; other phthalate metabolites and motility/morphology showed no significant association.

references.authors: Yuan M, Chai J, Song J, et al.
references.title: Association of bisphenol A exposure with in vitro fertilization outcomes: A meta-analysis and systematic review.
references.finding: Higher BPA exposure was associated with lower normal fertilization rates and fewer high-quality embryos in IVF/ICSI, but not with clinical pregnancy or implantation.

references.authors: Ahlqvist VH, Sjöqvist H, Dalman C, et al.
references.title: Acetaminophen Use During Pregnancy and Children's Risk of Autism, ADHD, and Intellectual Disability.
references.finding: Small associations of prenatal acetaminophen with autism (HR 1.05) and ADHD (HR 1.07) disappeared in sibling comparisons (HR 0.98 for both), suggesting familial confounding.

references.authors: Alwan S, Conover EA, Harris-Sagaribay L, et al.
references.title: Paracetamol use in pregnancy - caution over causal inference from available data.
references.finding: Letter from teratology and pharmacoepidemiology experts cautioning against causal inference from the observational acetaminophen-pregnancy data.

references.authors: Ambrosone CB, Zirpoli GR, Hutson AD, et al.
references.title: Dietary Supplement Use During Chemotherapy and Survival Outcomes of Patients With Breast Cancer Enrolled in a Cooperative Group Clinical Trial (SWOG S0221).
references.n: 1134 women with breast cancer in a chemotherapy trial
references.finding: Antioxidant supplement use before and during chemotherapy was associated with higher recurrence (adjHR 1.41, CI 0.98-2.04); B12 and iron use were significantly linked to worse outcomes.

references.authors: Anagnostis P, Papanikolaou D, Ioannidou PG, et al.
references.title: The effect of statins on semen parameters in patients with hypercholesterolemia: A systematic review.
references.finding: Systematic review of pravastatin and simvastatin found no consistent harmful effect on semen volume or concentration, with mixed motility and morphology findings.

references.authors: Andersen E, Juhl CR, Kjøller ET, et al.
references.title: Sperm count is increased by diet-induced weight loss and maintained by exercise or GLP-1 analogue treatment: a randomized controlled trial.
references.finding: An 8-week low-calorie diet (-16.5 kg) raised sperm concentration 1.49-fold and count 1.41-fold; the gain was kept at 52 weeks in men who maintained weight loss (including with liraglutide or exercise) but lost in those who regained.

references.authors: Ardissino D, Merlini PA, Savonitto S, et al.
references.title: Effect of transdermal nitroglycerin or N-acetylcysteine, or both, in the long-term treatment of unstable angina pectoris.
references.finding: Transdermal nitroglycerin plus oral NAC reduced outcome events (13% vs 39% placebo) but caused side effects, mainly intolerable headache, in 35%.

references.authors: Aroda VR, Edelstein SL, Goldberg RB, et al.
references.title: Long-term Metformin Use and Vitamin B12 Deficiency in the Diabetes Prevention Program Outcomes Study.
references.finding: Metformin 850 mg twice daily was associated with more low or borderline B12 (<=298 pg/mL: 19.1% vs 9.5% at 5 years); each year of use raised deficiency odds 13%, and neuropathy was more common in metformin users with low B12.

references.authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine. Electronic address: ASRM@asrm.org, Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
references.title: Role of metformin for ovulation induction in infertile patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS): a guideline.
references.finding: ASRM: metformin raises ovulation versus placebo in PCOS but should not be first-line for anovulation because clomiphene or letrozole are much more effective; no added miscarriage when stopped at conception.

references.authors: Bairati I, Meyer F, Gélinas M, et al.
references.title: A randomized trial of antioxidant vitamins to prevent second primary cancers in head and neck cancer patients.
references.finding: Alpha-tocopherol (with beta-carotene initially) during and after radiotherapy raised second primary cancers during supplementation (HR 2.88).

references.authors: Banach M, Serban C, Sahebkar A, et al.
references.title: Effects of coenzyme Q10 on statin-induced myopathy: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
references.finding: CoQ10 supplementation did not significantly reduce statin-associated muscle pain (SMD -0.53, CI -1.33 to 0.28) or CK.

references.authors: Bannister CA, Holden SE, Jenkins-Jones S, et al.
references.title: Can people with type 2 diabetes live longer than those without? A comparison of mortality in people initiated with metformin or sulphonylurea monotherapy and matched, non-diabetic controls.
references.n: 78,241 metformin users, 12,222 sulphonylurea users, 90,463 matched controls
references.finding: In UK primary-care data, people with type 2 diabetes started on metformin had 15% longer adjusted survival than matched non-diabetic controls; this finding underpins much of the anti-aging interest in metformin.

references.authors: Barzilai N, Crandall JP, Kritchevsky SB, et al.
references.title: Metformin as a Tool to Target Aging.
references.finding: Rationale paper for TAME (Targeting Aging with Metformin), proposing metformin as a first test of a drug targeting aging itself, based largely on observational data in diabetes.

references.authors: Bateman BT, Hernandez-Diaz S, Fischer MA, et al.
references.title: Statins and congenital malformations: cohort study.
references.finding: First-trimester statin use showed no teratogenic effect after adjustment for confounders such as diabetes (RR 1.07, 0.85-1.37).

references.authors: Batsis JA, Gavras A, Gross DC, et al.
references.title: Effect of Incretin-Based and Nonpharmacologic Weight Loss on Body Composition : A Systematic Review.
references.finding: Systematic review: loss of muscle-related indices exceeded prespecified benchmarks in about two thirds of incretin interventions and nearly half of non-drug weight-loss interventions.

references.authors: Bauer AZ, Swan SH, Kriebel D, et al.
references.title: Paracetamol use during pregnancy - a call for precautionary action.
references.finding: Consensus statement by 91 scientists calling for precaution: pregnant women should use acetaminophen only when indicated, at the lowest dose for the shortest time, citing neurodevelopmental and urogenital associations.

references.authors: Block KI, Koch AC, Mead MN, et al.
references.title: Impact of antioxidant supplementation on chemotherapeutic efficacy: a systematic review of the evidence from randomized controlled trials.
references.finding: No trial showed reduced chemotherapy efficacy with antioxidants and many reported fewer toxicities or better survival, but trials were small and underpowered.

references.authors: Bosman E, Esterhuizen AD, Rodrigues FA, et al.
references.title: Effect of metformin therapy and dietary supplements on semen parameters in hyperinsulinaemic males.
references.finding: Uncontrolled study: 3 months of metformin (with or without supplements) raised normal sperm forms from about 4% to 5.5% and improved chromatin packaging in hyperinsulinaemic men.

references.authors: Boulé NG, Robert C, Bell GJ, et al.
references.title: Metformin and exercise in type 2 diabetes: examining treatment modality interactions.
references.finding: Metformin raised exercise heart rate and lactate; adding exercise reduced metformin's lowering of the post-meal glucose response (interaction P=0.05).

references.authors: Boulé NG, Kenny GP, Larose J, et al.
references.title: Does metformin modify the effect on glycaemic control of aerobic exercise, resistance exercise or both?
references.finding: Over 22 weeks of aerobic, resistance or combined training, background metformin use did not significantly change the training effects on HbA1c, fitness, strength or body weight.

references.authors: Bray JJH, Foster-Davies H, Salem A, et al.
references.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists improve biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
references.finding: GLP-1 receptor agonists lowered CRP (-0.54 mg/L), TNF-alpha and malondialdehyde (SMD -0.84) and raised adiponectin versus standard therapy or placebo; CRP fall tracked blood-pressure and insulin-resistance improvement.

references.authors: Cameron AR, Morrison VL, Levin D, et al.
references.title: Anti-Inflammatory Effects of Metformin Irrespective of Diabetes Status.
references.n: cell, cohort and a nondiabetic heart-failure RCT
references.finding: Metformin suppressed NF-kB-linked inflammatory signalling in cells, lowered the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio versus sulfonylurea in a diabetes cohort, and reduced plasma cytokines in nondiabetic heart failure.

references.authors: Chang JC, Chen YJ, Chen IC, et al.
references.title: Perinatal Outcomes After Statin Exposure During Pregnancy.
references.finding: Statin use in pregnancy was not associated with congenital anomalies but was associated with low birth weight (RR 1.51) and preterm birth (RR 1.99).

references.authors: Chapman LE, Darling AL, Brown JE
references.title: Association between metformin and vitamin B12 deficiency in patients with type 2 diabetes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Metformin lowered vitamin B12 by about 57 pmol/L within 6 weeks to 3 months in pooled trials, pushing some patients into deficiency or borderline status.

references.authors: Chen X, Yang Y, Chen L, et al.
references.title: Pregnancy outcomes and birth defects in offspring following Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs exposure during pregnancy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Early-pregnancy NSAID exposure was associated with more congenital anomalies (OR 1.28) and major birth defects (OR 1.19); miscarriage association was not significant (OR 1.20).

references.authors: Cheungpasitporn W, Thongprayoon C, Kittanamongkolchai W, et al.
references.title: Proton pump inhibitors linked to hypomagnesemia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
references.finding: PPI use was associated with a 43% higher risk of hypomagnesemia (RR 1.43; 1.63 in high-quality studies).

references.authors: Choudhury A, Jena A, Jearth V, et al.
references.title: Vitamin B12 deficiency and use of proton pump inhibitors: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: PPI users had modestly higher odds of B12 deficiency (OR 1.42) with significant heterogeneity; most studies found no difference in serum B12 levels.

references.authors: Corrigan JJ, Ulfers LL
references.title: Effect of vitamin E on prothrombin levels in warfarin-induced vitamin K deficiency.
references.finding: Vitamin E 100-400 IU/day for 4 weeks did not change prothrombin time in warfarin users, though it subtly reduced functional factor II; higher doses may potentiate vitamin K deficiency.

references.authors: Cowie MR, Fisher M
references.title: SGLT2 inhibitors: mechanisms of cardiovascular benefit beyond glycaemic control.
references.finding: Proposed SGLT2-inhibitor benefit mechanisms include natriuresis, ketone use, reduced inflammation and oxidative stress and less AGE signalling; mostly from mechanistic work.

references.authors: Cholesterol Treatment Trialists' Collaboration
references.title: Effect of statin therapy on muscle symptoms: an individual participant data meta-analysis of large-scale, randomised, double-blind trials.
references.finding: Statins caused a 7% relative excess of muscle pain or weakness in year 1 (about 11 per 1000 person-years); only about 1 in 15 muscle complaints on statins was actually due to the drug.

references.authors: Deameh MG, Ramez M, Rowaiee R, et al.
references.title: Effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists on male reproductive hormones, semen parameters, and metabolic outcomes: a systematic review.
references.finding: GLP-1 agonists consistently raised total testosterone in men with obesity or type 2 diabetes while preserving LH/FSH; semen improvements were reported in obese or hypogonadal men but not in healthy men.

references.authors: De Caterina R, Cipollone F, Filardo FP, et al.
references.title: Low-density lipoprotein level reduction by the 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme-A inhibitor simvastatin is accompanied by a related reduction of F2-isoprostane formation in hypercholesterolemic subjects: no further effect of vitamin E.
references.finding: Simvastatin's LDL lowering was accompanied by a proportional fall in urinary F2-isoprostanes; adding vitamin E 600 mg/day did not lower lipid peroxidation further.

references.authors: de Jager J, Kooy A, Lehert P, et al.
references.title: Long term treatment with metformin in patients with type 2 diabetes and risk of vitamin B-12 deficiency: randomised placebo controlled trial.
references.finding: Metformin 850 mg three times daily for 4.3 years lowered B12 by 19% versus placebo and raised absolute B12-deficiency risk by 7.2 percentage points (number needed to harm ~14), with higher homocysteine.

references.authors: Drobnis EZ, Nangia AK
references.title: Pain Medications and Male Reproduction.
references.finding: Exogenous opioids suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis and act directly on the testis, lowering semen quality and raising DNA fragmentation; NSAIDs have less effect; paracetamol may be of concern.

references.authors: Dutta D, Mahajan K, Jena S, et al.
references.title: Feto-maternal safety of statins in pregnancy: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Statins in pregnancy were not associated with congenital malformations (OR 1.05); low birth weight signals were confined to non-pravastatin use in cohort studies.

references.authors: Eisa N, Barood O
references.title: Lean Mass Changes With Incretin Therapy Versus Lifestyle Intervention: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials.
references.finding: Lean mass made up 25-39% of weight lost on incretin drugs (semaglutide 35%, tirzepatide 25%), similar to diet-based weight loss (26%); adding resistance training cut it to about 17.5%.

references.authors: Etayo-Urtasun P, Sáez de Asteasu ML, Izquierdo M
references.title: The effects of metformin and exercise training on cardiorespiratory, blood pressure, and metabolic adaptations across the spectrum of glucose dysregulation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Adding metformin to structured exercise modestly attenuated VO2peak gains (MD -1.19 mL/kg/min) and blood-pressure reductions, with no difference in weight, glycemic or lipid outcomes (moderate certainty for VO2peak).

references.authors: US Food and Drug Administration
references.title: FDA requests removal of strongest warning against using cholesterol-lowering statins during pregnancy; still advises most pregnant patients should stop taking statins (Drug Safety Communication, 20 July 2021)
references.finding: FDA removed the pregnancy contraindication for statins because observational data showed no increase in birth defects, while advising most patients to stop on learning they are pregnant, allowing continuation in very high-risk patients, and advising against breastfeeding.

references.authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Novo Nordisk
references.title: WEGOVY (semaglutide) injection, prescribing information (revised 06/2021)
references.finding: Label section 8.3: discontinue semaglutide at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy because of its long half-life; discontinue when pregnancy is recognized.

references.authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Eli Lilly
references.title: ZEPBOUND (tirzepatide) injection, prescribing information (revised 11/2023)
references.finding: A single 5 mg tirzepatide dose cut ethinyl estradiol Cmax 59% and AUC 20%; users of oral contraceptives should switch to a non-oral method or add a barrier method for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose escalation.

references.authors: Grammer EE, Stahl ME, Ortiz de Zevallos J, et al.
references.title: Influence of metformin on exercise metabolism and capacity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Metformin raised blood lactate during exercise (SMD 0.98) and modulated exercise metabolism; effects on exercise capacity depended on dose, duration and population.

references.authors: Gregorič N, Šikonja J, Janež A, et al.
references.title: Semaglutide improved sperm morphology in obese men with type 2 diabetes mellitus and functional hypogonadism.
references.n: obese men with type 2 diabetes and functional hypogonadism
references.finding: Semaglutide raised normal sperm morphology (median 2% to 4%) and testosterone, whereas testosterone therapy lowered sperm concentration and count.

references.authors: Hall SD, Wang Z, Huang SM, et al.
references.title: The interaction between St John's wort and an oral contraceptive.
references.finding: St John's wort increased norethindrone clearance and halved ethinyl estradiol half-life; breakthrough bleeding rose from 2 to 7 of 12 women.

references.authors: Horowitz JD, Henry CA, Syrjanen ML, et al.
references.title: Combined use of nitroglycerin and N-acetylcysteine in the management of unstable angina pectoris.
references.finding: Adding IV NAC to IV nitroglycerin cut myocardial infarction (3 vs 10 patients) but caused symptomatic hypotension in 7 vs 0 patients.

references.authors: Huijgen NA, de Ridder MA, Verhamme KM, et al.
references.title: Are proton-pump inhibitors harmful for the semen quality of men in couples who are planning pregnancy?
references.finding: PPI use 6-12 months before semen analysis was associated with threefold higher odds of low total motile sperm count (OR 2.96), but use in the preceding 6 months was not.

references.authors: Imhann F, Bonder MJ, Vich Vila A, et al.
references.title: Proton pump inhibitors affect the gut microbiome.
references.finding: PPI use was associated with lower gut microbial diversity and changes in 20% of taxa, including more oral bacteria and potential pathogens, an effect larger than antibiotics at population level.

references.authors: Jastreboff AM, Aronne LJ, Ahmad NN, et al.
references.title: Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity.
references.finding: Tirzepatide 5, 10 and 15 mg weekly cut body weight 15.0%, 19.5% and 20.9% vs 3.1% with placebo over 72 weeks.

references.authors: Javaid M, Kadhim K, Bawamia B, et al.
references.title: Bleeding Risk in Patients Receiving Omega-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
references.finding: Omega-3 PUFAs did not increase bleeding overall (RR 1.09, 0.91-1.31); high-dose purified EPA raised relative bleeding risk about 50% but absolute risk only 0.6%.

references.authors: Kanbay M, Shah E, AlShiab R, et al.
references.title: Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Dual GIP/GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Inflammatory and Metabolic Biomarkers in Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
references.finding: Incretin therapies lowered CRP (SMD -0.37) and MDA (SMD -0.98, only 3 trials) and raised adiponectin; IL-6 and TNF-alpha effects were not significant overall.

references.authors: Keihani S, Martin C, Craig JR, et al.
references.title: Semen parameters are unaffected by statin use in men evaluated for infertility.
references.n: 118 statin users vs 7698 unmedicated subfertile men
references.finding: Statin use for over 3 months was not associated with changes in semen parameters other than a small fall in volume in combination users.

references.authors: Keihani S, Craig JR, Zhang C, et al.
references.title: Proton-pump inhibitor use does not affect semen quality in subfertile men.
references.n: 248 PPI users vs 7698 unmedicated subfertile men
references.finding: PPI use for over 3 months was not associated with changes in semen parameters.

references.authors: Keys MT, Thinggaard M, Larsen LA, et al.
references.title: Reassessing the evidence of a survival advantage in Type 2 diabetes treated with metformin compared with controls without diabetes: a retrospective cohort study.
references.n: Danish national registers incl. discordant twins
references.finding: Reanalysis using Danish registers and discordant twins found metformin-treated type 2 diabetes was associated with higher, not lower, mortality than no diabetes (adjusted IRR 1.32 singletons, 1.64 twins), contradicting Bannister 2014.

references.authors: Kokkinos PF, Faselis C, Myers J, et al.
references.title: Interactive effects of fitness and statin treatment on mortality risk in veterans with dyslipidaemia: a cohort study.
references.finding: Statin use and higher fitness were independently associated with lower mortality, and the combination (highly fit statin users HR 0.30) was lowest of all.

references.authors: Konopka AR, Laurin JL, Schoenberg HM, et al.
references.title: Metformin inhibits mitochondrial adaptations to aerobic exercise training in older adults.
references.finding: Metformin (vs placebo) during 12 weeks of aerobic training attenuated the training-induced rise in whole-body insulin sensitivity and VO2max and abolished the rise in muscle mitochondrial respiration; responses were highly variable.

references.authors: Konopka AR, Miller BF
references.title: Taming expectations of metformin as a treatment to extend healthspan.
references.finding: Argues that TAME goals may not match healthspan goals: metformin's benefits are documented in people with chronic disease, and whether they extend to healthy people (and alongside exercise) is unknown.

references.authors: Kristensen DM, Hass U, Lesné L, et al.
references.title: Intrauterine exposure to mild analgesics is a risk factor for development of male reproductive disorders in human and rat.
references.n: Danish and Finnish birth cohorts plus rat studies
references.finding: Mild analgesic use in pregnancy (especially second trimester) was dose-dependently linked to cryptorchidism in the Danish but not the Finnish cohort; paracetamol was anti-androgenic in rats.

references.authors: Kristensen DM, Desdoits-Lethimonier C, Mackey AL, et al.
references.title: Ibuprofen alters human testicular physiology to produce a state of compensated hypogonadism.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.n: young healthy men plus human testis explants
references.finding: Daily ibuprofen in young men lowered the testosterone/LH ratio, producing compensated hypogonadism, and suppressed testosterone production in human testis explants.

references.authors: Kulkarni AS, Peck BD, Walton RG, et al.
references.title: Metformin alters skeletal muscle transcriptome adaptations to resistance training in older adults.
references.finding: Metformin dampened the muscle gene-expression response to resistance training while shifting some aging-related pathways (senescence, autophagy) in a possibly favourable direction.

references.authors: Lam JR, Schneider JL, Zhao W, et al.
references.title: Proton pump inhibitor and histamine 2 receptor antagonist use and vitamin B12 deficiency.
references.finding: Two or more years of PPI use was associated with 65% higher odds of B12 deficiency (OR 1.65), higher at >1.5 pills/day (OR 1.95).

references.authors: Lam JR, Schneider JL, Quesenberry CP, et al.
references.title: Proton Pump Inhibitor and Histamine-2 Receptor Antagonist Use and Iron Deficiency.
references.finding: Two or more years of PPI use was associated with iron deficiency (OR 2.49), rising with dose and falling after stopping.

references.authors: Lauterburg BH, Mitchell JR
references.title: Therapeutic doses of acetaminophen stimulate the turnover of cysteine and glutathione in man.
references.finding: Single therapeutic doses of acetaminophen (600-1200 mg) markedly increased turnover of the cysteine pool used for glutathione synthesis, showing that normal doses draw on glutathione.

references.authors: Lawenda BD, Kelly KM, Ladas EJ, et al.
references.title: Should supplemental antioxidant administration be avoided during chemotherapy and radiation therapy?
references.finding: Concluded from RCTs that supplemental antioxidants during chemotherapy and radiotherapy should be discouraged because of possible tumour protection.

references.authors: Li DK, Ferber JR, Odouli R, et al.
references.title: Use of nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs during pregnancy and the risk of miscarriage.
references.finding: NSAID use around conception was associated with more miscarriage (aHR 1.89), stronger for early loss and longer use; acetaminophen users were used as an indication control.

references.authors: Lilja M, Mandić M, Apró W, et al.
references.title: High doses of anti-inflammatory drugs compromise muscle strength and hypertrophic adaptations to resistance training in young adults.
references.finding: Ibuprofen 1200 mg/day halved quadriceps growth (3.7% vs 7.5%) in young men and women and blunted strength gains versus low-dose aspirin during 8 weeks of resistance training.

references.authors: Lundberg TR, Howatson G
references.title: Analgesic and anti-inflammatory drugs in sports: Implications for exercise performance and training adaptations.
references.finding: NSAIDs and paracetamol inhibit COX; NSAIDs interfere with hypertrophy and strength gains in young people, while effects in elite athletes are unproven.

references.authors: Malin SK, Gerber R, Chipkin SR, et al.
references.title: Independent and combined effects of exercise training and metformin on insulin sensitivity in individuals with prediabetes.
references.finding: Exercise, metformin (2000 mg/day) and both combined all raised clamp insulin sensitivity over 12 weeks; the rise was 25-30% higher with exercise alone than with exercise plus metformin, a non-significant difference read as possible blunting.

references.authors: Meng LC, van Gelder MMHJ, Chuang HM, et al.
references.title: Paternal metformin use and risk of congenital malformations in offspring in Norway and Taiwan: population based, cross national cohort study.
