references.finding: After restricting to fathers with type 2 diabetes and adjusting for diabetes severity, paternal metformin during sperm development was not linked to malformations (pooled RR 0.89, 0.77-1.03), including in sibling comparisons.

references.authors: Micu MC, Micu R, Ostensen M
references.title: Luteinized unruptured follicle syndrome increased by inactive disease and selective cyclooxygenase 2 inhibitors in women with inflammatory arthropathies.
references.n: 59 monitored cycles with NSAIDs vs untreated cycles in women with inflammatory arthritis
references.finding: Continuous periovulatory NSAIDs caused luteinized unruptured follicle in 35.6% of cycles vs 3.4% untreated; etoricoxib was the main culprit and ibuprofen 1600 mg/day caused none.

references.authors: Mikus CR, Boyle LJ, Borengasser SJ, et al.
references.title: Simvastatin impairs exercise training adaptations.
references.finding: Simvastatin 40 mg blunted the training-induced gain in cardiorespiratory fitness (1.5% vs 10%) and turned a 13% rise in muscle citrate synthase into a 4.5% fall over 12 weeks.

references.authors: Miller BF, Thyfault JP
references.title: Exercise-Pharmacology Interactions: Metformin, Statins, and Healthspan.
references.finding: Reviews how metformin and statins may blunt exercise adaptations and argues their healthspan use in disease-free people must be tested alongside exercise.

references.authors: Mistry S, Eschler DC
references.title: Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis Caused by SGLT2 Inhibitors and a Ketogenic Diet: A Case Series and Review of Literature.
references.finding: Euglycemic DKA occurred with an SGLT2 inhibitor after only one week of a ketogenic diet; patients on these drugs should avoid ketogenic diets.

references.authors: Moayyedi P, Eikelboom JW, Bosch J, et al.
references.title: Safety of Proton Pump Inhibitors Based on a Large, Multi-Year, Randomized Trial of Patients Receiving Rivaroxaban or Aspirin.
references.finding: Pantoprazole 40 mg for about 3 years caused no excess of pneumonia, fracture, dementia or other harms versus placebo except enteric infections (1.4% vs 1.0%).

references.authors: Moreno-Cabañas A, Morales-Palomo F, Alvarez-Jimenez L, et al.
references.title: Effects of chronic metformin treatment on training adaptations in men and women with hyperglycemia: A prospective study.
references.finding: Among people doing 16 weeks of HIIT, those already taking metformin gained about half as much VO2max (12.7% vs 25.3%) as non-users, although insulin-resistance improvements were similar.

references.authors: Neeland IJ, Linge J, Birkenfeld AL
references.title: Changes in lean body mass with glucagon-like peptide-1-based therapies and mitigation strategies.
references.finding: Lean-mass loss on GLP-1 therapies is largely proportional to weight lost and may be adaptive (less muscle fat, better insulin sensitivity), but older or frail patients risk sarcopenia.

references.authors: Oesterle A, Laufs U, Liao JK
references.title: Pleiotropic Effects of Statins on the Cardiovascular System.
references.finding: Statins block isoprenoid synthesis and thereby Rho/Rac signalling and NADPH oxidase activity, lowering ROS and inflammation in cells and animals; how much this adds clinically beyond LDL lowering is debated.

references.authors: Owen MR, Doran E, Halestrap AP
references.title: Evidence that metformin exerts its anti-diabetic effects through inhibition of complex 1 of the mitochondrial respiratory chain.
references.finding: Metformin slowly accumulates in mitochondria and inhibits respiratory-chain complex I in hepatoma cells and rat liver, which restrains gluconeogenesis.

references.authors: Palleja A, Mikkelsen KH, Forslund SK, et al.
references.title: Recovery of gut microbiota of healthy adults following antibiotic exposure.
references.finding: After a 4-day broad-spectrum antibiotic cocktail, gut microbiota recovered to near-baseline within 1.5 months, though 9 common species were still missing at 180 days.

references.authors: Panza GA, Taylor BA, Thompson PD, et al.
references.title: The Effect of Atorvastatin on Habitual Physical Activity among Healthy Adults.
references.finding: Atorvastatin 80 mg for 6 months did not reduce habitual physical activity differently from placebo.

references.authors: Peel A, Lyons H, Tully CA, et al.
references.title: The effect of obesity interventions on male fertility: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Lifestyle weight-loss interventions modestly improved sperm morphology and progressive motility in men; data on GLP-1 agonists and on conception outcomes were too limited to judge.

references.authors: Peters AL, Buschur EO, Buse JB, et al.
references.title: Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis: A Potential Complication of Treatment With Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibition.
references.finding: Case series establishing euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis with SGLT2 inhibitors; normal glucose delayed recognition.

references.authors: Pilmark NS, Lyngbæk M, Oberholzer L, et al.
references.title: The interaction between metformin and physical activity on postprandial glucose and glucose kinetics: a randomised, clinical trial.
references.finding: Metformin 2 g/day plus 12 weeks of interval cycling was not better than training alone for post-meal glucose; VO2peak rose 15% with no between-group difference.

references.authors: Pons-Rejraji H, Brugnon F, Sion B, et al.
references.title: Evaluation of atorvastatin efficacy and toxicity on spermatozoa, accessory glands and gonadal hormones of healthy men: a pilot prospective clinical trial.
references.finding: Atorvastatin 10 mg for 5 months was followed by a 31% fall in total sperm count and changes in accessory-gland markers, some persisting 3 months after stopping.

references.authors: Prada D, Ritz B, Bauer AZ, et al.
references.title: Evaluation of the evidence on acetaminophen use and neurodevelopmental disorders using the Navigation Guide methodology.
references.finding: Navigation Guide review: 27 of 46 studies reported positive associations of prenatal acetaminophen with ADHD/autism, with higher-quality studies more often positive; authors urge limiting use.

references.authors: Qu H, Guo M, Chai H, et al.
references.title: Effects of Coenzyme Q10 on Statin-Induced Myopathy: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
references.finding: CoQ10 reduced statin-associated muscle pain, weakness, cramps and tiredness versus placebo, without changing CK.

references.authors: Rena G, Hardie DG, Pearson ER
references.title: The mechanisms of action of metformin.
references.finding: Metformin acts through AMPK-dependent and independent routes, including inhibition of mitochondrial respiration (complex I) and possibly mitochondrial glycerophosphate dehydrogenase, with a growing role for the gut.

references.authors: Ridker PM, Danielson E, Fonseca FA, et al.
references.title: Rosuvastatin to prevent vascular events in men and women with elevated C-reactive protein.
references.n: 17,802 adults with LDL <130 mg/dL and hsCRP >=2 mg/L (JUPITER)
references.finding: Rosuvastatin 20 mg cut LDL 50% and hsCRP 37% and nearly halved major cardiovascular events (HR 0.56), with more physician-reported diabetes.

references.authors: Rubino D, Abrahamsson N, Davies M, et al.
references.title: Effect of Continued Weekly Subcutaneous Semaglutide vs Placebo on Weight Loss Maintenance in Adults With Overweight or Obesity: The STEP 4 Randomized Clinical Trial.
references.finding: After a 20-week semaglutide run-in (-10.6%), continuing semaglutide lost a further 7.9% by week 68 whereas switching to placebo regained 6.9%.

references.authors: Schoenfeld BJ
references.title: The use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs for exercise-induced muscle damage: implications for skeletal muscle development.
references.finding: Occasional NSAID use is unlikely to impair muscle growth; chronic use is less clear and may be detrimental in people with high growth potential.

references.authors: Schürks M, Glynn RJ, Rist PM, et al.
references.title: Effects of vitamin E on stroke subtypes: meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
references.finding: Vitamin E raised haemorrhagic stroke risk 22% while lowering ischaemic stroke 10%; no net effect on total stroke.

references.authors: Sharpe A, Morley LC, Tang T, et al.
references.title: Metformin for ovulation induction (excluding gonadotrophins) in women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
references.finding: Cochrane: in PCOS, metformin may improve live birth versus placebo (OR 1.59, low quality) but quadruples GI side effects; adding it to clomiphene has uncertain effect on live birth; clomiphene beats metformin in obese women.

references.authors: Singh U, Devaraj S, Jialal I, et al.
references.title: Comparison effect of atorvastatin (10 versus 80 mg) on biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress in subjects with metabolic syndrome.
references.finding: Atorvastatin 80 mg cut oxidized LDL 39% (vs 24% with 10 mg) and lowered hsCRP and NF-kB activity over 12 weeks.

references.authors: Smarr MM, Grantz KL, Sundaram R, et al.
references.title: Urinary paracetamol and time-to-pregnancy.
references.finding: Men in the highest quartile of urinary paracetamol had longer time to pregnancy (fecundability OR 0.67); no association when modelled continuously or in women.

references.authors: Stone S, Khamashta MA, Nelson-Piercy C
references.title: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and reversible female infertility: is there a link?
references.finding: COX-2 inhibition blocks follicle rupture; animal data and three small clinical studies link regular NSAIDs to reversible anovulation, so withdrawal should be considered during fertility work-up.

references.authors: Tan CSS, Lee SWH
references.title: Warfarin and food, herbal or dietary supplement interactions: A systematic review.
references.finding: Systematic review of warfarin interactions: 45 foods, herbs or supplements potentiated warfarin, some causing serious bleeding; St John's wort, green tea and others flagged.

references.authors: Taylor BA, Lorson L, White CM, et al.
references.title: A randomized trial of coenzyme Q10 in patients with confirmed statin myopathy.
references.n: 120 patients with reported statin myalgia; 41 randomized to CoQ10 or placebo
references.finding: Only 36% of people reporting statin myalgia had symptoms on blinded simvastatin vs placebo; ubiquinol CoQ10 600 mg/day raised serum CoQ10 fourfold but did not reduce pain.

references.authors: Teede HJ, Tay CT, Laven JJE, et al.
references.title: Recommendations From the 2023 International Evidence-based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome.
references.finding: 2023 International Evidence-based PCOS Guideline (endorsed by ASRM, ESHRE, Endocrine Society, ESE): 254 recommendations including letrozole as first-line ovulation induction, metformin for metabolic features, and anti-obesity medicines alongside lifestyle.

references.authors: Terada T, Boulé NG
references.title: Does metformin therapy influence the effects of intensive lifestyle intervention? Exploring the interaction between first line therapies in the Look AHEAD trial.
references.finding: Background metformin was associated with slightly smaller weight loss (-4.7 vs -5.7 kg) under intensive lifestyle intervention and added little glycemic benefit, but did not change fitness gains.

references.authors: Trappe TA, Carroll CC, Dickinson JM, et al.
references.title: Influence of acetaminophen and ibuprofen on skeletal muscle adaptations to resistance exercise in older adults.
references.journal: Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol
references.finding: Over-the-counter doses of acetaminophen (4 g/day) or ibuprofen (1.2 g/day) during 12 weeks of resistance training did not inhibit muscle growth and strength and appeared to enhance them (muscle volume +12.5% and +10.9% vs +8.6% on placebo) in older adults.

references.authors: Vahedian-Azimi A, Makvandi S, Banach M, et al.
references.title: Fetal toxicity associated with statins: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Statin use in pregnancy was not significantly associated with birth defects (OR 1.48, 0.90-2.42), though the authors call for more data.

references.authors: Wachira JK, Larson MK, Harris WS
references.title: n-3 Fatty acids affect haemostasis but do not increase the risk of bleeding: clinical observations and mechanistic insights.
references.finding: Omega-3 fatty acids alter platelet function but did not increase clinically significant bleeding, including with antiplatelet or anticoagulant drugs.

references.authors: Walton RG, Dungan CM, Long DE, et al.
references.title: Metformin blunts muscle hypertrophy in response to progressive resistance exercise training in older adults: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial: The MASTERS trial.
references.finding: MASTERS: metformin 1700 mg/day during 14 weeks of progressive resistance training blunted gains in lean body mass and thigh muscle area versus placebo, with a non-significant trend to smaller strength gains.

references.authors: Watkins PB, Kaplowitz N, Slattery JT, et al.
references.title: Aminotransferase elevations in healthy adults receiving 4 grams of acetaminophen daily: a randomized controlled trial.
references.finding: Starting 4 g/day acetaminophen produced ALT >3x the upper limit in 31-44% of healthy adults within 2 weeks versus 0% on placebo.

references.authors: Wensink MJ, Lu Y, Tian L, et al.
references.title: Preconception Antidiabetic Drugs in Men and Birth Defects in Offspring : A Nationwide Cohort Study.
references.finding: Offspring of fathers who filled metformin prescriptions during sperm development had more major birth defects (aOR 1.40), especially genital defects in boys; exposure outside that window showed no excess.

references.authors: Whitten DL, Myers SP, Hawrelak JA, et al.
references.title: The effect of St John's wort extracts on CYP3A: a systematic review of prospective clinical trials.
references.finding: High-hyperforin St John's wort extracts (>10 mg/day) consistently induce CYP3A; low-hyperforin extracts (<4 mg/day) did not.

references.authors: Wilding JPH, Batterham RL, Calanna S, et al.
references.title: Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity.
references.finding: Semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly plus lifestyle cut body weight 14.9% vs 2.4% with placebo over 68 weeks.

references.authors: Yasueda A, Urushima H, Ito T
references.title: Efficacy and Interaction of Antioxidant Supplements as Adjuvant Therapy in Cancer Treatment: A Systematic Review.
references.finding: Harm from antioxidant supplements during cancer therapy remains unclear except for smokers having radiotherapy.

references.authors: Alangari A, Arif J, Al Qureshah F, et al.
references.title: Clinical benefits and risks of high-dose intravenous vitamin C: a systematic review.
references.finding: Systematic review of high-dose IV vitamin C: benefits in sepsis and cancer remain exploratory, and risks include oxalate nephropathy and hemolysis at very high doses in G6PD deficiency, supporting pre-infusion testing.

references.authors: Allen KJ, Gurrin LC, Constantine CC, et al.
references.title: Iron-overload-related disease in HFE hereditary hemochromatosis.
references.finding: Documented iron-overload-related disease developed in 28.4% of male but only 1.2% of female C282Y homozygotes; only one non-homozygote (a compound heterozygote) had such disease.

references.authors: Beretta A, Manuelli M, Cena H
references.title: Favism: Clinical Features at Different Ages.
references.finding: Favism (hemolysis after fava beans in G6PD deficiency) varies widely in severity, is most severe in young children and pregnancy, and often needs hospitalization and transfusion.

references.authors: Cappellini MD, Fiorelli G
references.title: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency.
references.finding: G6PD deficiency, an X-linked defect affecting over 400 million people, causes neonatal jaundice and acute hemolysis triggered by oxidant drugs, infections or fava beans; management is avoidance of oxidative triggers.

references.authors: European Association for the Study of the Liver
references.title: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on haemochromatosis.
references.finding: EASL haemochromatosis guideline: in HFE C282Y homozygotes, TSAT >45% with ferritin >200 ug/L (women) or TSAT >50% with ferritin >300 ug/L (men, postmenopausal women) suffices for diagnosis; phlebotomy targets ferritin <50 ug/L in induction and <100 ug/L in maintenance.

references.authors: Gammal RS, Pirmohamed M, Somogyi AA, et al.
references.title: Expanded Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium Guideline for Medication Use in the Context of G6PD Genotype.
references.finding: CPIC classifies dapsone, methylene blue, pegloticase, primaquine, rasburicase, tafenoquine and toluidine blue as high-risk in G6PD deficiency, nitrofurantoin as medium risk, and vitamin C at standard doses as low-to-no risk.

references.authors: Garcia-Casal MN, Pasricha SR, Martinez RX, et al.
references.title: Serum or plasma ferritin concentration as an index of iron deficiency and overload.
references.finding: At a threshold of 30 ug/L, ferritin is reasonably sensitive and very specific for iron deficiency in people presenting for care (low-certainty evidence); evidence that high ferritin detects iron overload is very low certainty, and screening performance in healthy people is unknown.

references.authors: Gasper AV, Al-Janobi A, Smith JA, et al.
references.title: Glutathione S-transferase M1 polymorphism and metabolism of sulforaphane from standard and high-glucosinolate broccoli.
references.finding: GSTM1-null subjects had higher plasma sulforaphane and excreted more of it than GSTM1-positive subjects after broccoli; genotype altered sulforaphane metabolism.

references.authors: Kowdley KV, Brown KE, Ahn J, et al.
references.title: ACG Clinical Guideline: Hereditary Hemochromatosis.
references.finding: ACG hemochromatosis guideline: ferritin <1,000 ng/mL at diagnosis identifies low risk of advanced fibrosis; elevated ferritin is more often due to fatty liver or alcohol than to hemochromatosis in people who are not C282Y homozygotes or C282Y/H63D compound heterozygotes.

references.authors: London SJ, Yuan JM, Chung FL, et al.
references.title: Isothiocyanates, glutathione S-transferase M1 and T1 polymorphisms, and lung-cancer risk: a prospective study of men in Shanghai, China.
references.n: 232 lung cancer cases and 710 controls nested in 18,244 men
references.finding: Detectable urinary isothiocyanates were linked to lower lung cancer risk (RR 0.65), most strongly in GSTM1-null (0.36) and GSTM1/GSTT1 double-null men (0.28).

references.authors: Luzzatto L, Ally M, Notaro R
references.title: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency.
references.finding: About 500 million people carry G6PD mutations; most are asymptomatic but can develop severe acute hemolysis after fava beans, drugs such as primaquine or rasburicase, or infection.

references.authors: Méar L, Herr M, Fauconnier A, et al.
references.title: Polymorphisms and endometriosis: a systematic review and meta-analyses.
references.finding: Among many studied polymorphisms, GSTT1 null was among the few robustly associated with endometriosis, while GSTM1 null was among candidates needing confirmation in well-defined cohorts.

references.authors: Nkhoma ET, Poole C, Vannappagari V, et al.
references.title: The global prevalence of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: G6PD deficiency affects an estimated 400 million people, with the highest prevalence in sub-Saharan Africa and malaria-endemic regions.

references.authors: Pilling LC, Tamosauskaite J, Jones G, et al.
references.title: Common conditions associated with hereditary haemochromatosis genetic variants: cohort study in UK Biobank.
references.finding: C282Y homozygosity was associated with liver disease (OR 4.30), arthritis, diabetes (OR 1.53) and more incident morbidity in both men (15.7% vs 5.0%) and women (10.1% vs 3.4%), supporting re-examination of early case-finding.

references.authors: Steck SE, Gammon MD, Hebert JR, et al.
references.title: GSTM1, GSTT1, GSTP1, and GSTA1 polymorphisms and urinary isothiocyanate metabolites following broccoli consumption in humans.
references.finding: GST genotypes did not substantially change isothiocyanate excretion; GSTM1-null subjects were more often high excreters (62% vs 39%).

references.authors: Walsh A, Dixon JL, Ramm GA, et al.
references.title: The clinical relevance of compound heterozygosity for the C282Y and H63D substitutions in hemochromatosis.
references.n: 249 C282Y/H63D compound heterozygotes and 483 C282Y homozygotes
references.finding: C282Y/H63D compound heterozygotes often had raised iron indices but did not develop progressive disease without cofactors such as fatty liver, diabetes or excess alcohol.

references.authors: Whitlock EP, Garlitz BA, Harris EL, et al.
references.title: Screening for hereditary hemochromatosis: a systematic review for the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force.
references.finding: USPSTF systematic review: up to 38-50% of C282Y homozygotes may develop iron overload and 10-33% hemochromatosis-related morbidity, but evidence was insufficient to estimate the benefit of population genetic screening.

references.authors: Wu W, Lu J, Tang Q, et al.
references.title: GSTM1 and GSTT1 null polymorphisms and male infertility risk: an updated meta-analysis encompassing 6934 subjects.
references.finding: GSTM1 null genotype was associated with a significantly higher risk of male infertility in Asian and Caucasian groups; GSTT1 findings were inconsistent.

references.authors: Ascherio A, Rimm EB, Giovannucci E, et al.
references.title: Blood donations and risk of coronary heart disease in men
references.finding: Lifetime blood donation lowered ferritin but was not associated with MI or fatal CHD (RR 1.2 for >=30 donations vs never).

references.authors: Atsma F, Veldhuizen I, Verbeek A, et al.
references.title: Healthy donor effect: its magnitude in health research among blood donors
references.finding: Donors were healthier than the general population (better self-rated health, fewer GP visits), demonstrating a strong healthy donor effect.

references.authors: Daghlas I, Gill D
references.title: Genetically predicted iron status and life expectancy
references.n: Mendelian randomization using parental lifespan GWAS
references.finding: Each SD of genetically higher serum iron corresponded to 0.7 fewer years of parental lifespan and lower odds of reaching the 90th age percentile (OR 0.81).

references.authors: Danesh J, Appleby P
references.title: Coronary heart disease and iron status: meta-analyses of prospective studies
references.finding: Ferritin >=200 vs <200 ug/L showed no association with coronary heart disease (RR 1.0, 0.8-1.3); no strong link for any iron marker.

references.authors: Depalma RG, Hayes VW, Chow BK, et al.
references.title: Ferritin levels, inflammatory biomarkers, and mortality in peripheral arterial disease: a substudy of the Iron (Fe) and Atherosclerosis Study (FeAST) Trial
references.finding: In a FeAST substudy, ferritin correlated with IL-6 and hsCRP, and higher ferritin tracked with mortality, illustrating ferritin's overlap with inflammation.

references.authors: Di Angelantonio E, Thompson SG, Kaptoge S, et al.
references.title: Efficiency and safety of varying the frequency of whole blood donation (INTERVAL): a randomised trial of 45 000 donors
references.finding: INTERVAL: shorter donation intervals collected more blood but caused more symptoms (tiredness, restless legs), lower hemoglobin and ferritin, and more deferrals.

references.authors: Dixon SJ, Lemberg KM, Lamprecht MR, et al.
references.title: Ferroptosis: an iron-dependent form of nonapoptotic cell death
references.finding: Defined ferroptosis: an iron-dependent, lipid-peroxidation-driven cell death triggered by cystine/glutathione depletion and blocked by ferrostatin-1.

references.authors: Edgren G, Nyrén O, Melbye M
references.title: Cancer as a ferrotoxic disease: are we getting hard stainless evidence?
references.finding: JNCI editorial accompanying the FeAST cancer analysis, questioning how firm the evidence is that iron reduction prevents cancer.

references.authors: Falkingham M, Abdelhamid A, Curtis P, et al.
references.title: The effects of oral iron supplementation on cognition in older children and adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
references.finding: Iron supplements improved attention/concentration and, in anaemic people only, IQ by 2.5 points; trials were small and weak.

references.authors: Fiani D, Chahine S, Zaboube M, et al.
references.title: Psychiatric and cognitive outcomes of iron supplementation in non-anemic children, adolescents, and menstruating adults: A meta-analysis and systematic review
references.finding: In non-anaemic iron-deficient youth and menstruating adults, iron improved anxiety, fatigue and memory; effects vanished when iron-replete people were analysed alone.

references.authors: Finkelstein JL, Cuthbert A, Weeks J, et al.
references.title: Daily oral iron supplementation during pregnancy
references.finding: Daily iron in pregnancy reduces maternal anaemia, iron deficiency and iron-deficiency anaemia at term and probably reduces low birthweight (RR 0.84).

references.authors: Gill D, Del Greco M F, Walker AP, et al.
references.title: The Effect of Iron Status on Risk of Coronary Artery Disease: A Mendelian Randomization Study-Brief Report
references.n: ~60,800 CAD cases and 123,500 controls (two-sample Mendelian randomization)
references.finding: Genetically higher iron status was associated with slightly LOWER coronary artery disease risk (OR 0.94 per SD serum iron).

references.authors: Gill D, Benyamin B, Moore LSP, et al.
references.title: Associations of genetically determined iron status across the phenome: A mendelian randomization study
references.finding: Higher genetic iron status lowered iron-deficiency anemia and hypercholesterolemia but raised skin and soft-tissue infections (cellulitis/abscess OR 1.25).

references.authors: Hansen R, Sejer EPF, Holm C, et al.
references.title: Iron supplements in pregnant women with normal iron status: A systematic review and meta-analysis
references.finding: Daily iron in iron-replete pregnant women probably reduced iron-deficiency anaemia at term and low birthweight.

references.authors: Houschyar KS, Lüdtke R, Dobos GJ, et al.
references.title: Effects of phlebotomy-induced reduction of body iron stores on metabolic syndrome: results from a randomized clinical trial
references.finding: Removing 550-800 mL blood lowered systolic BP by 16.6 mmHg vs control at 6 weeks, without changing insulin resistance (HOMA).

references.authors: Hu FB
references.title: The iron-heart hypothesis: search for the ironclad evidence
references.finding: JAMA editorial accompanying FeAST arguing that conclusive ('ironclad') evidence for the iron-heart hypothesis was still lacking.

references.authors: Hunnicutt J, He K, Xun P
references.title: Dietary iron intake and body iron stores are associated with risk of coronary heart disease in a meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies
references.finding: Heme iron intake was associated with higher CHD incidence (RR 1.57) while total iron, serum iron and transferrin saturation were inversely associated.

references.authors: Hurrell R, Egli I
references.title: Iron bioavailability and dietary reference values
references.finding: Iron bioavailability is ~14-18% from mixed diets and 5-12% from vegetarian diets; body iron status influences absorption more than diet composition.

references.authors: Institute of Medicine (US) Panel on Micronutrients
references.title: Dietary Reference Intakes for Vitamin A, Vitamin K, Arsenic, Boron, Chromium, Copper, Iodine, Iron, Manganese, Molybdenum, Nickel, Silicon, Vanadium, and Zinc
references.finding: IOM DRI report for vitamin A, copper, iodine, iron, manganese, zinc and others (ULs: zinc 40 mg, copper 10 mg, iron 45 mg, iodine 1100 ug, manganese 11 mg, preformed vitamin A 3000 ug).

references.authors: Jiang L, Wang K, Lo K, et al.
references.title: Sex-Specific Association of Circulating Ferritin Level and Risk of Type 2 Diabetes: A Dose-Response Meta-Analysis of Prospective Studies
references.finding: Each 100 ug/L higher ferritin was associated with 22% higher type 2 diabetes risk, stronger in women (RR 1.53) than men (RR 1.21).

references.authors: Kakhlon O, Cabantchik ZI
references.title: The labile iron pool: characterization, measurement, and participation in cellular processes(1)
references.finding: The labile (chelatable, redox-active) iron pool promotes ROS formation and rises and falls with iron import, chelation and ferritin turnover.

references.authors: Kaptoge S, Di Angelantonio E, Moore C, et al.
references.title: Longer-term efficiency and safety of increasing the frequency of whole blood donation (INTERVAL): extension study of a randomised trial of 20 757 blood donors
references.finding: Each week shorter inter-donation interval lowered ferritin by ~5-6.5% and increased low-hemoglobin deferrals.

references.authors: Kell DB, Pretorius E
references.title: Serum ferritin is an important inflammatory disease marker, as it is mainly a leakage product from damaged cells
references.finding: Argues serum ferritin is largely a leakage product of damaged cells, explaining its correlation with inflammation and oxidative stress as well as with iron stores.

references.authors: Khambalia AZ, Aimone A, Nagubandi P, et al.
references.title: High maternal iron status, dietary iron intake and iron supplement use in pregnancy and risk of gestational diabetes mellitus: a prospective study and systematic review
references.finding: Higher ferritin (OR 1.41 per unit), serum iron and heme iron intake were associated with gestational diabetes; two supplement trials showed no association.

references.authors: Kunutsor SK, Apekey TA, Walley J, et al.
references.title: Ferritin levels and risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective evidence
references.finding: Top vs bottom fifth of ferritin: type 2 diabetes RR 1.73; heme iron intake RR 1.28.

references.authors: Liu Y, Clarke R, Bennett DA, et al.
references.title: Iron Status and Risk of Heart Disease, Stroke, and Diabetes: A Mendelian Randomization Study in European Adults
references.n: UK Biobank plus consortia with 181,522 CAD and 80,154 T2D cases (Mendelian randomization)
references.finding: Genetically higher iron biomarkers were modestly protective for coronary disease (7-14% lower risk per SD) but raised type 2 diabetes risk.

references.authors: Manco M, Fernandez-Real JM
references.title: Back to past leeches: repeated phlebotomies and cardiovascular risk
references.finding: Commentary on the phlebotomy trial noting design drawbacks (unblinded, short) while discussing iron depletion and metabolic risk.

references.authors: Pasricha SR, Tye-Din J, Muckenthaler MU, et al.
references.title: Iron deficiency
references.finding: Iron deficiency is a leading cause of global disease burden; harms occur even without anaemia; hepcidin limits absorption of high-dose oral iron.

references.authors: Peña-Rosas JP, De-Regil LM, Garcia-Casal MN, et al.
references.title: Daily oral iron supplementation during pregnancy
references.finding: Prenatal iron cut anaemia at term by 70% but raised the risk of haemoglobin above 130 g/L.

references.authors: Pilling LC, Tamosauskaite J, Jones G, et al.
references.title: Common conditions associated with hereditary haemochromatosis genetic variants: cohort study in UK Biobank
references.finding: HFE C282Y homozygosity (1 in 156) was associated with liver disease, arthritis and diabetes; diagnosed haemochromatosis in 21.7% of homozygous men and 9.8% of women.

references.authors: Rahman MM, Abe SK, Rahman MS, et al.
references.title: Maternal anemia and risk of adverse birth and health outcomes in low- and middle-income countries: systematic review and meta-analysis
references.n: 26 studies in low- and middle-income countries
references.finding: Maternal anaemia was associated with low birthweight (RR 1.31), preterm birth (RR 1.63) and perinatal mortality (RR 1.51).

references.authors: Salonen JT, Tuomainen TP, Salonen R, et al.
references.title: Donation of blood is associated with reduced risk of myocardial infarction. The Kuopio Ischaemic Heart Disease Risk Factor Study
references.finding: Men who had donated blood in the previous 24 months had 88% lower risk of acute MI (1 event in 153 donors).

references.authors: Sempos CT, Looker AC, Gillum RE, et al.
references.title: Serum ferritin and death from all causes and cardiovascular disease: the NHANES II Mortality Study. National Health and Nutrition Examination Study
references.finding: Serum ferritin was not associated with cardiovascular or all-cause death in US adults; low ferritin predicted higher mortality in Black men.

references.authors: Stockwell BR, Friedmann Angeli JP, Bayir H, et al.
references.title: Ferroptosis: A Regulated Cell Death Nexus Linking Metabolism, Redox Biology, and Disease
references.finding: Ferroptosis review: iron, polyunsaturated lipid peroxidation and loss of GPX4/glutathione defences link metabolism, redox biology and disease.

references.authors: Sullivan JL
references.title: Iron and the sex difference in heart disease risk
references.finding: Proposed the 'iron hypothesis': higher stored iron in men and postmenopausal women explains their higher heart disease risk, and suggested phlebotomy as a test.

references.authors: Timmers PRHJ, Wilson JF, Joshi PK, et al.
references.title: Multivariate genomic scan implicates novel loci and haem metabolism in human ageing
references.n: Multivariate GWAS of healthspan, parental lifespan and longevity
references.finding: Identified haem metabolism as a pathway linked to human ageing traits.

references.authors: Ullum H, Rostgaard K, Kamper-Jørgensen M, et al.
references.title: Blood donation and blood donor mortality after adjustment for a healthy donor effect
references.finding: Each extra annual donation was linked to 18.6% lower mortality, shrinking to 7.5% after adjusting for the healthy donor effect; not proof of benefit.

references.authors: van den Hurk K, van Kraaij MGJ, Zalpuri S
references.title: Lessons from the INTERVAL study
references.finding: Letter on INTERVAL urging attention to iron deficiency in frequent donors and ferritin monitoring.

references.authors: Vaucher P, Druais PL, Waldvogel S, et al.
references.title: Effect of iron supplementation on fatigue in nonanemic menstruating women with low ferritin: a randomized controlled trial
references.n: 198 non-anaemic menstruating women with ferritin <50 ug/L
references.finding: 80 mg/day oral iron for 12 weeks reduced fatigue scores by 47.7% vs 28.8% with placebo.

references.authors: Wang X, Fang X, Zheng W, et al.
references.title: Genetic Support of A Causal Relationship Between Iron Status and Type 2 Diabetes: A Mendelian Randomization Study
references.finding: Genetically higher serum iron (OR 1.07), ferritin (OR 1.19) and transferrin saturation (OR 1.06) were associated with higher type 2 diabetes risk.

references.authors: Wood RJ
references.title: The iron-heart disease connection: is it dead or just hiding?
references.finding: Reviewed why the iron-heart hypothesis remained unresolved and called for better measures of the potentially damaging forms of iron.

references.authors: Young MF, Oaks BM, Rogers HP, et al.
references.title: Maternal low and high hemoglobin concentrations and associations with adverse maternal and infant health outcomes: an updated global systematic review and meta-analysis
references.finding: Both low and high maternal haemoglobin were associated with adverse outcomes; high Hb with gestational diabetes (OR 1.71), pre-eclampsia and stillbirth.

references.authors: Zacharski LR, Chow BK, Howes PS, et al.
references.title: Reduction of iron stores and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with peripheral arterial disease: a randomized controlled trial
references.finding: FeAST: phlebotomy to lower ferritin did not significantly reduce all-cause death (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.67-1.08) or death plus MI and stroke (HR 0.88, 0.72-1.07).

references.authors: Zacharski LR, Chow BK, Howes PS, et al.
references.title: Decreased cancer risk after iron reduction in patients with peripheral arterial disease: results from a randomized trial
references.finding: FeAST secondary analysis: iron reduction (mean ferritin ~80 vs ~123 ng/mL) was associated with fewer new visceral cancers (HR 0.65, 0.43-0.97).

references.authors: Zhao Z, Li S, Liu G, et al.
references.title: Body iron stores and heme-iron intake in relation to risk of type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
references.finding: Highest vs lowest ferritin: prospective T2D RR 1.66; highest vs lowest heme iron intake RR 1.31.

references.authors: Bhatti P, Mirick DK, Randolph TW, et al.
references.title: Oxidative DNA damage during sleep periods among nightshift workers.
references.finding: Night-shift workers excreted less urinary 8-OH-dG during day sleep than day workers during night sleep, interpreted as reduced oxidative DNA repair linked to melatonin disruption.

references.authors: Bhatti P, Mirick DK, Randolph TW, et al.
references.title: Oxidative DNA damage during night shift work.
references.finding: Melatonin was much lower during night work than night sleep, and urinary 8-OH-dG during night work was only 20% of night-sleep levels, interpreted as reduced repair.

references.authors: Boeri L, Passarelli F, Basadonna LM, et al.
references.title: Oxidative Stress and Semen Quality Among Night- and Day-Shift Workers: A Cross-Sectional Study.
references.finding: Night-shift work independently predicted elevated oxidative stress (d-ROMs, OR 2.1); in an uncontrolled subgroup, antioxidant supplementation lowered d-ROMs more in night workers.

references.authors: Brown TM, Brainard GC, Cajochen C, et al.
references.title: Recommendations for daytime, evening, and nighttime indoor light exposure to best support physiology, sleep, and wakefulness in healthy adults.
references.finding: Expert consensus: daytime light ≥250 lux melanopic EDI at the eye; ≤10 lux melanopic EDI in the 3 h before bed; ≤1 lux melanopic EDI in the sleep environment (≤10 if some light is needed).

references.authors: Buxton OM, Cain SW, O'Connor SP, et al.
references.title: Adverse metabolic consequences in humans of prolonged sleep restriction combined with circadian disruption.
references.finding: Three weeks of sleep restriction (5.6 h/24 h) combined with 28-h days lowered resting metabolic rate and raised postprandial glucose through inadequate insulin secretion; reversed with recovery.

references.authors: Chang AM, Aeschbach D, Duffy JF, et al.
references.title: Evening use of light-emitting eReaders negatively affects sleep, circadian timing, and next-morning alertness.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Reading a light-emitting e-reader for ~4 h before bed for 5 nights, vs a printed book, lengthened sleep onset, suppressed melatonin, delayed the circadian clock and reduced next-morning alertness.

references.authors: Chang AM, Czeisler CA
references.title: Reply to Zeitzer: Good science, in or out of the laboratory, should prevail.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Authors' reply defending the controlled laboratory design and its relevance to everyday evening device use.

references.authors: Duraccio KM, Zaugg KK, Blackburn RC, et al.
references.title: Does iPhone night shift mitigate negative effects of smartphone use on sleep outcomes in emerging adults?
references.finding: iPhone Night Shift mode did not improve sleep outcomes vs normal phone use; among those sleeping >6.8 h, no phone before bed gave the best sleep.

references.authors: Figueiro MG, Steverson B, Heerwagen J, et al.
references.title: The impact of daytime light exposures on sleep and mood in office workers.
references.finding: High morning circadian-effective light was associated with shorter sleep onset latency, better sleep quality and stronger circadian entrainment, especially in winter.

references.authors: Gan Y, Yang C, Tong X, et al.
references.title: Shift work and diabetes mellitus: a meta-analysis of observational studies.
references.finding: Ever shift work was associated with 9% higher diabetes risk (OR 1.09), higher in men (1.37) and rotating shifts.

references.authors: Gao Y, Gan T, Jiang L, et al.
references.title: Association between shift work and risk of type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of observational studies.
references.finding: Shift work was associated with higher type 2 diabetes risk (~10%), especially night and rotating shifts, with possible dose-response with years of exposure in women.

references.authors: Gaskins AJ, Rich-Edwards JW, Lawson CC, et al.
references.title: Work schedule and physical factors in relation to fecundity in nurses.
references.finding: No shift-work pattern was associated with time to pregnancy; working >40 h/week and heavy lifting were.

references.authors: Gooley JJ, Chamberlain K, Smith KA, et al.
references.title: Exposure to room light before bedtime suppresses melatonin onset and shortens melatonin duration in humans.
references.finding: Room light (<200 lux) before bedtime vs dim light delayed melatonin onset in 99% and shortened melatonin duration by ~90 min; room light during sleep hours suppressed melatonin >50% in 85% of trials.

references.authors: Green A, Barak S, Shine L, et al.
references.title: Exposure by males to light emitted from media devices at night is linked with decline of sperm quality and correlated with sleep quality measures.
references.finding: Evening and post-bedtime smartphone/tablet use correlated negatively with sperm motility, progressive motility and concentration.

references.authors: IARC Monographs Vol 124 group
references.title: Carcinogenicity of night shift work.
references.finding: IARC Monograph 124 classified night shift work as probably carcinogenic to humans (Group 2A), based on limited human evidence and sufficient animal evidence.

references.authors: Jiang Z, Dou Y, Lei Y, et al.
references.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction Unravels the Potential Molecular Link Between Night Shift Work-Related Circadian Disruption and Elevated Blood Pressure in Human and Mouse Models.
references.finding: Simulated night-shift work in mice raised blood pressure with clock-gene disruption, mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress; in human night workers exposure duration tracked blood pressure and mitochondrial markers.

references.authors: Mason IC, Grimaldi D, Reid KJ, et al.
references.title: Light exposure during sleep impairs cardiometabolic function.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: One night of sleeping in 100 lux room light vs <3 lux raised night-time heart rate, lowered heart rate variability and increased next-morning insulin resistance.

references.authors: Mínguez-Alarcón L, Souter I, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Occupational factors and markers of ovarian reserve and response among women at a fertility centre.
references.n: 313-473 women at a fertility centre (EARTH study)
references.finding: Women working evening/night/rotating shifts had 2.3 fewer mature oocytes retrieved after ovarian stimulation than day workers.

references.authors: Morris CJ, Yang JN, Garcia JI, et al.
references.title: Endogenous circadian system and circadian misalignment impact glucose tolerance via separate mechanisms in humans.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Postprandial glucose was 17% higher in the biological evening than morning, and circadian misalignment itself raised it a further 6%, via reduced insulin sensitivity.

references.authors: Morris CJ, Purvis TE, Hu K, et al.
references.title: Circadian misalignment increases cardiovascular disease risk factors in humans.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Three days of circadian misalignment raised 24-h blood pressure (+3.0/1.5 mmHg) and IL-6, CRP, resistin and TNF-alpha by 3-29%.

references.authors: Obayashi K, Saeki K, Iwamoto J, et al.
references.title: Exposure to light at night, nocturnal urinary melatonin excretion, and obesity/dyslipidemia in the elderly: a cross-sectional analysis of the HEIJO-KYO study.
references.finding: Bedroom light ≥3 lux at night was associated with higher odds of obesity (OR 1.89) and dyslipidaemia (OR 1.72), independent of urinary melatonin.

references.authors: Park YM, White AJ, Jackson CL, et al.
references.title: Association of Exposure to Artificial Light at Night While Sleeping With Risk of Obesity in Women.
references.finding: Sleeping with a TV or light on was associated with gaining ≥5 kg (RR 1.17) and incident obesity (RR 1.33) over ~5.7 years.

references.authors: Phillips AJK, Vidafar P, Burns AC, et al.
references.title: High sensitivity and interindividual variability in the response of the human circadian system to evening light.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Half-maximal melatonin suppression occurred at only ~25 lux of evening light; 10, 30 and 50 lux delayed melatonin onset by 22, 77 and 109 min; individual sensitivity varied over 10-fold.

references.authors: Reiter RJ, Tamura H, Tan DX, et al.
references.title: Melatonin and the circadian system: contributions to successful female reproduction.
references.finding: Follicular fluid melatonin exceeds blood levels and protects the oocyte from oxidative stress around ovulation; light at night suppresses melatonin and should be avoided.

references.authors: Scheer FA, Hilton MF, Mantzoros CS, et al.
references.title: Adverse metabolic and cardiovascular consequences of circadian misalignment.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Eating and sleeping ~12 h out of phase lowered leptin 17%, raised glucose 6% despite 22% more insulin, reversed the cortisol rhythm and raised blood pressure; 3 of 8 had prediabetic postprandial glucose.

references.authors: Schöllhorn I, Stefani O, Lucas RJ, et al.
references.title: Melanopic irradiance defines the impact of evening display light on sleep latency, melatonin and alertness.
references.finding: At equal screen brightness, low-melanopic display light shortened sleep latency, reduced melatonin suppression and advanced melatonin onset vs high-melanopic light, dose-dependently.

references.authors: Singh S, Keller PR, Busija L, et al.
references.title: Blue-light filtering spectacle lenses for visual performance, sleep, and macular health in adults.
references.finding: Blue-light filtering spectacle lenses probably do not reduce eye strain; effects on sleep quality were indeterminate with mixed results and high risk of bias.

references.authors: Stocker LJ, Macklon NS, Cheong YC, et al.
references.title: Influence of shift work on early reproductive outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Shift work was associated with menstrual disruption (aOR 1.15) and infertility (OR 1.80, I² 94%); night shifts with early pregnancy loss (OR 1.29).

references.authors: Stothard ER, McHill AW, Depner CM, et al.
references.title: Circadian Entrainment to the Natural Light-Dark Cycle across Seasons and the Weekend.
references.finding: A summer weekend of camping achieved ~69% of the circadian advance of a full week; the biological night expanded in winter natural light.

references.authors: Teixeira KRC, Dos Santos CP, de Medeiros LA, et al.
references.title: Night workers have lower levels of antioxidant defenses and higher levels of oxidative stress damage when compared to day workers.
references.finding: Night workers had higher TBARS and hydrogen peroxide and lower total antioxidant capacity, catalase and SOD than day workers; social jetlag was not associated with these markers.

references.authors: Tian R, Yang T, Xiao C, et al.
references.title: Outdoor artificial light at night and male sperm quality: A retrospective cohort study in China.
references.finding: Each 100 nW/cm²/sr higher outdoor artificial light at night was associated with lower sperm motility, most strongly in men under 25.

references.authors: Torquati L, Mielke GI, Brown WJ, et al.
references.title: Shift work and the risk of cardiovascular disease. A systematic review and meta-analysis including dose-response relationship.
references.finding: Shift workers had 17% higher risk of any CVD event and 26% higher CHD morbidity; risk rose 7.1% per additional 5 years after the first 5 years.

references.authors: Travis RC, Balkwill A, Fensom GK, et al.
references.title: Night Shift Work and Breast Cancer Incidence: Three Prospective Studies and Meta-analysis of Published Studies.
references.finding: Night shift work was not associated with breast cancer (RR 0.99), even after 20 or 30+ years.

references.authors: van Maanen A, Meijer AM, van der Heijden KB, et al.
references.title: The effects of light therapy on sleep problems: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Light therapy improved sleep problems overall (g 0.39), circadian rhythm sleep disorders (g 0.41) and insomnia (g 0.47); effects small to medium, smaller in RCTs, with publication bias.

references.authors: Vetter C, Devore EE, Wegrzyn LR, et al.
references.title: Association Between Rotating Night Shift Work and Risk of Coronary Heart Disease Among Women.
references.finding: Longer duration of rotating night-shift work was associated with a statistically significant but small absolute increase in CHD risk, which waned after stopping shift work.

references.authors: Wang Y, He M, Ling X, et al.
references.title: Rotating shiftwork in men is linked to decreased fecundity, attributable primarily to sperm concentration and vitality: 24-month follow-up in 3425 males of PREBIC cohort.
references.finding: Rotating shift workers had 16% lower hazard of pregnancy within 1 year and ~11% lower sperm concentration and total count; fixed shift workers did not differ from day workers.

references.authors: Windred DP, Burns AC, Rutter MK, et al.
references.title: Personal light exposure patterns and incidence of type 2 diabetes: analysis of 13 million hours of light sensor data and 670,000 person-years of prospective observation.
references.finding: Brighter night-light exposure was associated with higher type 2 diabetes risk (HR 1.29, 1.39 and 1.53 for 50-70th, 70-90th and 90-100th percentiles vs darkest nights); authors disclose lighting-industry funding.

references.authors: Windred DP, Burns AC, Lane JM, et al.
references.title: Brighter nights and darker days predict higher mortality risk: A prospective analysis of personal light exposure in >88,000 individuals.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Brighter day light was associated with lower all-cause mortality (aHR ~0.66-0.83 for top decile) and brighter night light with higher mortality (aHR 1.21-1.34 top decile) over 8 years.

references.authors: Wright KP Jr, McHill AW, Birks BR, et al.
references.title: Entrainment of the human circadian clock to the natural light-dark cycle.
references.finding: A week of camping with natural light only advanced the circadian clock (melatonin onset moved toward sunset) and reduced differences between late and early chronotypes.

references.authors: Zanif U, Lai AS, Parks J, et al.
references.title: Melatonin supplementation and oxidative DNA damage repair capacity among night shift workers: a randomised placebo-controlled trial.
references.finding: Melatonin before day sleep for 4 weeks gave a borderline 1.8-fold increase in urinary 8-OH-dG during day sleep (p = 0.06), interpreted as better repair capacity; no change during night work.

references.authors: Zeitzer JM
references.title: Real life trumps laboratory in matters of public health.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Letter arguing that the e-reader laboratory findings may not translate to real-life public-health relevance.

references.authors: Allen JG, MacNaughton P, Satish U, et al.
references.title: Associations of Cognitive Function Scores with Carbon Dioxide, Ventilation, and Volatile Organic Compound Exposures in Office Workers: A Controlled Exposure Study of Green and Conventional Office Environments.
references.finding: In a blinded chamber study, cognitive scores were 61% higher under low-VOC "Green" conditions and 101% higher with extra ventilation than under conventional conditions; VOCs and CO2 were independently associated with lower scores.

references.authors: Andersen C, Omelekhina Y, Rasmussen BB, et al.
references.title: Emissions of soot, PAHs, ultrafine particles, NO(x,) and other health relevant compounds from stressed burning of candles in indoor air.
references.finding: Chamber tests showed candles burning in a draught emit soot-dominated PM2.5, PAHs, ultrafine particles, NOx and formaldehyde, with wax and wick type strongly affecting soot and PAH emissions.

references.authors: Angulo Milhem S, Verriele M, Nicolas M, et al.
references.title: Does the ubiquitous use of essential oil-based products promote indoor air quality? A critical literature review.
references.finding: Essential-oil cleaning products and air fresheners are major indoor sources of terpenes, which react with ozone to form secondary pollutants including formaldehyde and fine particles.

references.authors: Arnold WA, Blum A, Branyan J, et al.
references.title: Quaternary Ammonium Compounds: A Chemical Class of Emerging Concern.
references.finding: Multi-institution review finding increased human QAC exposure since COVID-19 and suspected dermal, respiratory, developmental, reproductive and mitochondrial effects, plus antimicrobial-resistance concerns.

references.authors: Bush RK, Portnoy JM, Saxon A, et al.
references.title: The medical effects of mold exposure.
references.finding: AAAAI position paper: moulds cause allergic and well-defined diseases (asthma, rhinitis, ABPA, hypersensitivity pneumonitis), while many newer hypothesized mould illnesses remain unproven.

references.authors: Carignan CC, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Butt CM, et al.
references.title: Urinary Concentrations of Organophosphate Flame Retardant Metabolites and Pregnancy Outcomes among Women Undergoing in Vitro Fertilization.
references.finding: Women in the highest vs lowest quartile of summed urinary organophosphate flame retardant metabolites had 10% lower fertilization, 31% lower implantation, 41% lower clinical pregnancy and 38% lower live birth proportions per IVF cycle.

references.authors: Casas L, Espinosa A, Borràs-Santos A, et al.
references.title: Domestic use of bleach and infections in children: a multicentre cross-sectional study.
references.finding: Children in bleach-using homes had more influenza (RRR 1.20), recurrent tonsillitis (1.35) and any infection (1.18).

references.authors: Cherry N, Labrèche F, Collins J, et al.
references.title: Occupational exposure to solvents and male infertility.
references.finding: High solvent exposure was associated with motile sperm <12 million/mL (OR 3.83 in Montreal, 2.90 in a replication series); moderate exposure replicated in only one series.

references.authors: Cherry N, Moore H, McNamee R, et al.
references.title: Occupation and male infertility: glycol ethers and other exposures.
references.finding: High glycol ether exposure in the 3 months before the clinic visit was associated with low motile sperm count (adjusted OR 2.25, 95% CI 1.08-4.69); moderate exposure OR 1.46 (0.93-2.28).

references.authors: Cohen BL
references.title: Test of the linear-no threshold theory of radiation carcinogenesis for inhaled radon decay products.
references.finding: County lung cancer mortality fell with average home radon, which the author interpreted as failure of the linear no-threshold model.

references.authors: Cohen J, Hubbard H, Özkaynak H, et al.
references.title: Meta-analysis of soil and dust ingestion studies.
references.finding: Mean soil plus dust ingestion was about 36-68 mg/day in infants, 56-72 mg/day in young children and 12-32 mg/day in adolescents and adults.

references.authors: Cox LA Jr
references.title: The gas stove-childhood asthma kerfuffle: A teaching opportunity.
references.finding: Commentary arguing the gas stove-childhood asthma attributable fraction claim reflects questionable research practices and is not supported as causal.

references.authors: Craner J
references.title: A critique of the ACOEM statement on mold: undisclosed conflicts of interest in the creation of an "evidence-based" statement.
references.finding: Critique arguing the 2003 ACOEM mould statement was shaped by undisclosed litigation-related conflicts of interest.

references.authors: Cummings BE, Waring MS
references.title: Potted plants do not improve indoor air quality: a review and analysis of reported VOC removal efficiencies.
references.finding: Translating chamber data into clean air delivery rates showed 10-1000 potted plants per m2 of floor would be needed to match the VOC removal of normal building air exchange.

references.authors: Darby S, Hill D, Auvinen A, et al.
references.title: Radon in homes and risk of lung cancer: collaborative analysis of individual data from 13 European case-control studies.
references.finding: Lung cancer risk rose 16% per 100 Bq/m3 of usual radon (linear, no threshold); absolute risk to age 75 at 0/100/400 Bq/m3 was 0.4/0.5/0.7% for never-smokers and 10/12/16% for smokers.

references.authors: DeSesso JM, Harris SB, Scialli AR, et al.
references.title: Systematic assessment of quaternary ammonium compounds for the potential to elicit developmental and reproductive effects.
references.finding: Systematic assessment relying largely on unpublished guideline studies found no adverse developmental or reproductive effects of QACs at expected exposures and rated the positive mouse studies "not reliable".

references.authors: Ding M, Lawson C, Johnson C, et al.
references.title: Occupational exposure to high-level disinfectants and risk of miscarriage among nurses.
references.finding: Prospectively, occupational high-level disinfectant use was not associated with miscarriage (HR 0.84), except in pregnancies within 12 months of baseline use (HR 1.78).

references.authors: Doyle P, Roman E, Beral V, et al.
references.title: Spontaneous abortion in dry cleaning workers potentially exposed to perchloroethylene.
references.finding: Spontaneous abortion was more common in dry-cleaning machine operators (17.1%) than in non-operators (11.6%) and unexposed pregnancies (10.9%).

references.authors: Dumas O, Varraso R, Boggs KM, et al.
references.title: Association of Occupational Exposure to Disinfectants With Incidence of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Among US Female Nurses.
references.finding: Weekly occupational use of disinfectants to clean surfaces was associated with higher COPD incidence over 2009-2015.

references.authors: Fisk WJ, Lei-Gomez Q, Mendell MJ
references.title: Meta-analyses of the associations of respiratory health effects with dampness and mold in homes.
references.finding: Building dampness and mould were associated with 30-50% increases in respiratory and asthma outcomes (central ORs 1.34-1.75).

references.authors: Friborg JT, Yuan JM, Wang R, et al.
references.title: Incense use and respiratory tract carcinomas: a prospective cohort study.
references.finding: Long-term heavy incense use was associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the respiratory tract (RR 1.8) and upper respiratory tract cancers, but not with lung cancer overall.

references.authors: Garg A, Kashtan Y, Nicholson M, et al.
references.title: Exposure and health risks of benzene from combustion by gas stoves: A modelling approach in U.S. homes.
references.finding: Indoor-air modelling of the highest-emitting 5% of US gas stoves found benzene cancer risks above 1 in a million under medium-high use without ventilation; efficient vented hoods reduced exposure.

references.authors: Gibson EA, Stapleton HM, Calero L, et al.
references.title: Flame retardant exposure assessment: findings from a behavioral intervention study.
references.finding: One week of instructed house cleaning or hand-washing (then both) lowered some urinary flame-retardant metabolites and, in women with above-median baseline exposure, some hand-wipe levels, by about half in some cases.

references.authors: Goodman JE, Biesemeier JA, Johnson GT, et al.
references.title: Fecundability and serum PBDE concentrations in women.
references.finding: Letter (with author reply) disputing the CHAMACOS PBDE-fecundability analysis.

references.authors: Gøtzsche PC, Johansen HK
references.title: House dust mite control measures for asthma.
references.finding: Cochrane: chemical and physical house dust mite control (including mattress encasings) had no effect on asthma symptoms, peak flow or medication use (Cochrane has since flagged the review as outdated).

references.authors: Groves-Kirkby CJ, Denman AR, Phillips PS, et al.
references.title: Domestic radon remediation of UK dwellings by Sub-Slab Depressurisation: evidence for a baseline contribution from constructional materials.
references.finding: Sub-slab depressurisation brought all homes below 200 Bq/m3, with mitigation factors below 0.2 (over 80% reduction) in more than 75% of homes.

references.authors: Gruenwald T, Seals BA, Knibbs LD, et al.
references.title: Population Attributable Fraction of Gas Stoves and Childhood Asthma in the United States.
references.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
references.finding: Applying a meta-analytic OR of 1.34 to US gas-stove prevalence, 12.7% (95% CI 6.3-19.3%) of current childhood asthma was attributed to gas stove use.

references.authors: Harley KG, Marks AR, Chevrier J, et al.
references.title: PBDE concentrations in women's serum and fecundability.
references.finding: Higher serum PBDEs were associated with longer time to pregnancy (fecundability OR 0.5-0.7 for BDE-100, BDE-153 and the sum of four congeners), with no link to menstrual cycle characteristics.

references.authors: Hoffman K, Garantziotis S, Birnbaum LS, et al.
references.title: Monitoring indoor exposure to organophosphate flame retardants: hand wipes and house dust.
references.finding: Hand-wipe (not dust) TPHP and TDCIPP predicted their urinary metabolites (top vs bottom hand-wipe TPHP: DPHP 2.4-fold); urinary BDCIPP and DPHP were moderately to strongly reliable over 5 days (ICC 0.81 and 0.51).

references.authors: Hostetler KA
references.title: Reproductive toxicology.
references.finding: Letter on behalf of the ADBAC and DDAC industry steering committees disputing the 2014 mouse QAC fertility study (with author reply).

references.authors: Howden-Chapman P, Matheson A, Crane J, et al.
references.title: Effect of insulating existing houses on health inequality: cluster randomised study in the community.
references.finding: Retrofitting insulation made homes warmer and drier (RH -2.3%) and halved reports of poor self-rated health, reduced wheeze (OR 0.57) and days off school and work.

references.authors: Howden-Chapman P, Pierse N, Nicholls S, et al.
references.title: Effects of improved home heating on asthma in community dwelling children: randomised controlled trial.
references.finding: Installing non-polluting, more effective heaters lowered NO2 and reduced school absence, doctor visits, sleep disturbed by wheezing and night cough, but did not significantly improve lung function.

references.authors: Hrubec TC, Seguin RP, Xu L, et al.
references.title: Altered toxicological endpoints in humans from common quaternary ammonium compound disinfectant exposure.
references.finding: QACs were detected in the blood of 80% of volunteers and blood QAC levels tracked higher inflammatory cytokines, lower mitochondrial function and altered sterol synthesis.

references.authors: Hurraß J, Heinzow B, Walser-Reichenbach S, et al.
references.title: AWMF mold guideline "Medical clinical diagnostics for indoor mold exposure" - Update 2023 AWMF Register No. 161/001.
references.finding: German AWMF guideline (2023 update) on medical diagnostics for indoor mould exposure.

references.authors: Ingle ME, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Carignan CC, et al.
references.title: The association between urinary concentrations of phosphorous-containing flame retardant metabolites and semen parameters among men from a fertility clinic.
references.finding: Associations between urinary OPFR metabolites and semen parameters were weak and inconsistent; BDCIPP was about 2-fold higher in summer samples.

references.authors: Ingle ME, Mínguez-Alarcón L, Carignan CC, et al.
references.title: Exploring reproductive associations of serum polybrominated diphenyl ether and hydroxylated brominated diphenyl ether concentrations among women undergoing in vitro fertilization.
references.finding: Contrary to earlier reports, an interquartile rise in serum BDE-153 was associated with higher implantation (RR 1.26), clinical pregnancy (1.32) and live birth (1.34); PBDE levels fell up to 80% between 2005 and 2016 recruits.

references.authors: Ingle ME, Watkins D, Rosario Z, et al.
references.title: An exploratory analysis of urinary organophosphate ester metabolites and oxidative stress among pregnant women in Puerto Rico.
references.finding: Interquartile rises in urinary OPE metabolites were associated with 12-21% higher 8-isoprostane and 18-19% higher 8-OHdG; metabolite ICCs were 0.51-0.60 across pregnancy.

references.authors: Johnson PI, Altshul L, Cramer DW, et al.
references.title: Serum and follicular fluid concentrations of polybrominated diphenyl ethers and in-vitro fertilization outcome.
references.finding: Detectable BDE-153 in follicular fluid was associated with failed embryo implantation (adjusted OR 10.0, 95% CI 1.9-52); serum correlated only moderately with follicular fluid levels.

references.authors: Kashtan YS, Nicholson M, Finnegan C, et al.
references.title: Gas and Propane Combustion from Stoves Emits Benzene and Increases Indoor Air Pollution.
references.finding: Gas and propane burners and ovens emitted 2.8-6.5 ug benzene per minute, 10-25 times more than electric coil or radiant stoves; induction and the food itself emitted none, and benzene spread to bedrooms.

references.authors: Kashtan Y, Nicholson M, Finnegan CJ, et al.
references.title: Nitrogen dioxide exposure, health outcomes, and associated demographic disparities due to gas and propane combustion by U.S. stoves.
references.finding: Modelling estimated that gas and propane stoves add 4.0 ppb to long-term NO2 exposure on average (75% of the WHO guideline), with four-fold higher exposure in homes under 800 ft2 and higher exposure in Black, Hispanic and Native households.

references.authors: Kawamoto M, Page E
references.title: Notes from the field: Use of unvalidated urine mycotoxin tests for the clinical diagnosis of illness--United States, 2014.
references.finding: CDC/NIOSH warned that direct-to-consumer urine mycotoxin tests are unvalidated and were used to diagnose mould illness without evidence of building mould.

references.authors: Kirkpatrick ZA, Melin VE, Hrubec TC
references.title: Quaternary ammonium compound exposure causes infertility by altering endocrine signaling and gametogenesis.
references.finding: Oral QAC exposure lowered LH, FSH, progesterone and estrogen in mice and disrupted Sertoli cell metabolism and spermatogenesis.

references.authors: Klausen FB, Amidi A, Kjærgaard SK, et al.
references.title: The effect of air quality on sleep and cognitive performance in school children aged 10-12 years: a double-blinded, placebo-controlled, crossover trial.
references.journal: Int J Occup Med Environ Health
references.finding: Sleeping with added CO2 (2,000-3,000 ppm) or reduced ventilation did not affect next-morning cognitive performance.

references.authors: Krewski D, Lubin JH, Zielinski JM, et al.
references.title: Residential radon and risk of lung cancer: a combined analysis of 7 North American case-control studies.
references.finding: Odds of lung cancer were 1.11 at 100 Bq/m3, consistent with extrapolation from miner data, and higher with more accurate dosimetry.

references.authors: Lam J, Lanphear BP, Bellinger D, et al.
references.title: Developmental PBDE Exposure and IQ/ADHD in Childhood: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
references.finding: Navigation Guide review rated the evidence "sufficient" that developmental PBDE exposure lowers IQ: a 10-fold higher PBDE exposure was associated with 3.7 fewer IQ points (95% CI 0.83-6.56); evidence for ADHD was "limited".

references.authors: Lam J, Koustas E, Sutton P, et al.
references.title: Exposure to formaldehyde and asthma outcomes: A systematic review, meta-analysis, and economic assessment.
references.finding: Each 10 ug/m3 more formaldehyde was associated with higher odds of childhood asthma diagnosis (OR 1.20).

references.authors: Lawson CC, Rocheleau CM, Whelan EA, et al.
references.title: Occupational exposures among nurses and risk of spontaneous abortion.
references.finding: Self-reported exposure to sterilizing agents/disinfectants was associated with a 2-fold risk of late (12-20 week) spontaneous abortion; antineoplastic drugs with a 2-fold risk overall.

references.authors: Lebel ED, Finnegan CJ, Ouyang Z, et al.
references.title: Methane and NO(x) Emissions from Natural Gas Stoves, Cooktops, and Ovens in Residential Homes.
references.finding: Gas stoves leak 0.8-1.3% of their gas as unburned methane (three-quarters while off); NOx emissions scale with gas burned, and without a working hood a small kitchen can exceed the 1-h US NO2 standard (100 ppb) within minutes.

references.authors: Lebel ED, Michanowicz DR, Bilsback KR, et al.
references.title: Composition, Emissions, and Air Quality Impacts of Hazardous Air Pollutants in Unburned Natural Gas from Residential Stoves in California.
references.finding: Unburned gas contained benzene in 99% of samples (mean 0.7-12 ppmv by region); leaks from idle stoves could raise indoor benzene above California's 8-h reference level.

references.authors: Li W, Long C, Fan T, et al.
references.title: Gas cooking and respiratory outcomes in children: A systematic review.
references.finding: Systematic review by Gradient (a consultancy that has worked for gas-industry clients) judged most gas cooking-asthma studies cross-sectional and biased, with cohort studies largely null, and concluded causal inference is not supported.

references.authors: Li Y, Luo D, Zhao X, et al.
references.title: Urinary concentrations of organophosphate esters in relation to semen quality: A cross-sectional study.
references.finding: Higher urinary DPHP and BMPP were associated with below-reference sperm count and OPE mixtures with lower motility and normal morphology.

references.authors: Li W, Goodman JE, Long C
references.title: Population attributable fraction of gas cooking and childhood asthma: What was missed?
references.finding: Gradient consultancy commentary, funded by the American Gas Association, arguing that the 12.7% population attributable fraction for gas cooking and childhood asthma is not valid.

references.authors: Li C, Li X, Zhang Z
references.title: Oxidative stress and pro-inflammatory cytokines following perchloroethylene exposure in young female dry-cleaning workers.
references.finding: Young female dry-cleaning workers with high plasma perchloroethylene had higher MDA, SOD and catalase and altered cytokines compared with controls.

references.authors: Li C, Guo X, Ren H, et al.
references.title: Urinary Organophosphate Esters and Increased Oxidative Stress in Healthy Older Adults: The China BAPE Study.
references.finding: Urinary OPE metabolites, singly and as a mixture, were associated with higher urinary 8-OHdG, 8-OHG and MDA in a Chinese panel study.

references.authors: Lin W, Brunekreef B, Gehring U
references.title: Meta-analysis of the effects of indoor nitrogen dioxide and gas cooking on asthma and wheeze in children.
references.finding: Gas cooking was associated with childhood asthma (OR 1.32, 95% CI 1.18-1.48) and indoor NO2 with current wheeze (OR 1.15 per 15 ppb); no evidence of publication bias.

references.authors: McGwin G, Lienert J, Kennedy JI
references.title: Formaldehyde exposure and asthma in children: a systematic review.
references.finding: Pooled mostly cross-sectional studies: OR 1.17 (random effects) for childhood asthma per 10 ug/m3 formaldehyde.

references.authors: McHugh EG, Grady ST, Collins CM, et al.
references.title: Pulmonary, inflammatory, and oxidative effects of indoor nitrogen dioxide in patients with COPD.
references.finding: Low-level indoor NO2 (median 6.8 ppb) was not associated with CRP, urinary 8-OHdG or MDA, with suggestive lung-function decrements in severe COPD.

references.authors: McMartin KI, Chu M, Kopecky E, et al.
references.title: Pregnancy outcome following maternal organic solvent exposure: a meta-analysis of epidemiologic studies.
references.finding: Maternal occupational organic solvent exposure was associated with major malformations (OR 1.64) and a non-significant trend for spontaneous abortion (OR 1.25, 95% CI 0.99-1.58).

references.authors: Melin VE, Potineni H, Hunt P, et al.
references.title: Exposure to common quaternary ammonium disinfectants decreases fertility in mice.
references.finding: Six months of exposure to an ADBAC+DDAC quaternary ammonium disinfectant reduced fertility and fecundity in mice; QAC residues persisted in caging for months.

references.authors: Melin VE, Melin TE, Dessify BJ, et al.
references.title: Quaternary ammonium disinfectants cause subfertility in mice by targeting both male and female reproductive processes.
references.finding: ADBAC+DDAC exposure reduced corpora lutea and estrus time in females and sperm concentration and motility in males.

references.authors: Mendez D, Warner KE, Courant PN
references.title: Effects of radon mitigation vs smoking cessation in reducing radon-related risk of lung cancer.
references.finding: Modelling showed that for smokers, quitting reduces radon-related lung cancer risk more than radon mitigation does.

references.authors: Milton DK, Glencross PM, Walters MD
references.title: Risk of sick leave associated with outdoor air supply rate, humidification, and occupant complaints.
references.finding: Office workers in lower-ventilation areas (about 12 vs 24 L/s per person) had 53% more short-term sick leave.

references.authors: Mitro SD, Dodson RE, Singla V, et al.
references.title: Consumer Product Chemicals in Indoor Dust: A Quantitative Meta-analysis of U.S. Studies.
references.finding: US indoor dust consistently contains phthalates (highest), phenols, replacement flame retardants, fragrances and PFAS; several phthalates and flame retardants had the highest residential intakes.

references.authors: Morgan WJ, Crain EF, Gruchalla RS, et al.
references.title: Results of a home-based environmental intervention among urban children with asthma.
references.finding: A tailored, home-based programme targeting allergens and tobacco smoke reduced symptom days (3.39 vs 4.20 per 2 weeks) during and for a year after the intervention, with falls in dust-mite and cockroach allergen.

references.authors: Moro AM, Charão M, Brucker N, et al.
references.title: Effects of low-level exposure to xenobiotics present in paints on oxidative stress in workers.
references.finding: Painters with solvent biomarkers below exposure limits had higher MDA and antioxidant enzyme activities and lower thiols and ALA-D than unexposed controls.

references.authors: Nielsen GD, Wolkoff P
references.title: Cancer effects of formaldehyde: a proposal for an indoor air guideline value.
references.finding: Argues that the WHO formaldehyde guideline of 0.1 mg/m3 (0.08 ppm) protects against nasal cancer, since nasal cytotoxicity has a non-linear dose-response and no human nasopharyngeal excess was seen below about 1 ppm average.

references.authors: Nussbaumer-Streit B, Mayr V, Dobrescu AI, et al.
references.title: Household interventions for secondary prevention of domestic lead exposure in children.
references.finding: Cochrane: household education and dust-control interventions did not lower children's blood lead (education MD -0.03 log units; environmental interventions also no clear effect).

references.authors: Pacheco Da Silva E, Varraso R, Fezeu LK, et al.
references.title: Longitudinal Associations Between Household Use of "Green" Cleaning Products and Asthma Symptoms.
references.finding: Persistent use of irritant/sprayed cleaning products was associated with more asthma symptoms and incidence over 2 years; "green" product use was also associated with asthma symptoms.

references.authors: Paulin LM, Diette GB, Scott M, et al.
references.title: Home interventions are effective at decreasing indoor nitrogen dioxide concentrations.
references.finding: Replacing the gas stove with electric cut median kitchen NO2 by 51% at 3 months; HEPA-plus-carbon purifiers cut it 27% immediately (20% at 3 months); a new range hood did not significantly lower NO2.

references.authors: Pilotto LS, Nitschke M, Smith BJ, et al.
references.title: Randomized controlled trial of unflued gas heater replacement on respiratory health of asthmatic schoolchildren.
references.finding: Replacing unflued gas heaters in schools lowered classroom NO2 (15.5 vs 47.0 ppb) and cut daytime and night-time asthma symptoms (RR about 0.3-0.45), without changing lung function.

references.authors: Puskin JS
references.title: Smoking as a confounder in ecologic correlations of cancer mortality rates with average county radon levels.
references.finding: Smoking-related cancers showed the same negative county-radon correlation while non-smoking cancers did not, indicating that confounding by smoking explains the ecological finding.

references.authors: Qian X, Wan Y, Wang A, et al.
references.title: Urinary metabolites of multiple volatile organic compounds among general population in Wuhan, central China: Inter-day reproducibility, seasonal difference, and their associations with oxidative stress biomarkers.
references.finding: After false-discovery adjustment, 16 urinary VOC metabolites were positively associated with urinary 8-OHdG and 8-OHG and four with HNE-mercapturic acid.

references.authors: Quansah R, Jaakkola MS, Hugg TT, et al.
references.title: Residential dampness and molds and the risk of developing asthma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Dampness and mould were associated with new-onset asthma (summary estimates 1.27-1.48), strongest for mould odour (1.73).

references.authors: Que DE, den Ouden F, Bosschaerts S, et al.
references.title: Trends of Organophosphate Ester Flame Retardant Metabolites in Age- and Sex-Stratified Pooled Australian Urine Samples from the Past Decade (2012-2023).
references.finding: Most OPFR metabolites were stable or rising over the decade, and mean exposures were below derived no-effect levels.

references.authors: Rodgers KM, Bennett D, Moran R, et al.
