references.title: Do flame retardant concentrations change in dust after older upholstered furniture is replaced?
references.n: California homes replacing pre-2014 upholstered furniture
references.finding: Replacing older upholstered furniture, or only its foam, with TB117-2013 products lowered dust PBDEs and chlorinated and aryl organophosphate flame retardants in nearly all homes over 6-18 months.

references.authors: Romero Starke K, Friedrich S, Schubert M, et al.
references.title: Are Healthcare Workers at an Increased Risk for Obstructive Respiratory Diseases Due to Cleaning and Disinfection Agents? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
references.journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
references.finding: Healthcare workers exposed to cleaning/disinfection agents had higher new-onset asthma risk (bleach ES 2.44, glutaraldehyde 1.91); all studies were at high risk of bias.

references.authors: Satish U, Mendell MJ, Shekhar K, et al.
references.title: Is CO2 an indoor pollutant? Direct effects of low-to-moderate CO2 concentrations on human decision-making performance.
references.finding: Pure CO2 at 1,000 and 2,500 ppm (vs 600 ppm) reduced decision-making scores on six and seven of nine scales in 2.5-h blinded sessions.

references.authors: Sauni R, Verbeek JH, Uitti J, et al.
references.title: Remediating buildings damaged by dampness and mould for preventing or reducing respiratory tract symptoms, infections and asthma.
references.finding: Cochrane: repairing mould-damaged houses and offices reduced wheeze (OR 0.64) and respiratory infections in adults (moderate to very low quality); school remediation evidence was inconsistent.

references.authors: Scully RR, Basner M, Nasrini J, et al.
references.title: Effects of acute exposures to carbon dioxide on decision making and cognition in astronaut-like subjects.
references.finding: Acute CO2 at 600-5,000 ppm showed no clear dose-response on decision-making or cognition, conflicting with earlier chamber studies.

references.authors: Sehgal AR, Schuellerman P, Dolata J, et al.
references.title: Asthma Control Before and After Changing Gas Stoves to Electric Stoves.
references.finding: Uncontrolled before-after study: after gas stoves were replaced with electric ones, indoor NO2 fell from 21.0 to 6.3 ppb and Asthma Control Questionnaire scores improved from 2.6 to 1.5 within 2-3 months.

references.authors: Sehgal N, Morello-Frosch R, Padula AM, et al.
references.title: Mixture effects of prenatal exposure to polybrominated diphenyl ethers on urinary oxidative stress biomarkers in the Chemicals in Our Bodies cohort.
references.finding: Higher second-trimester serum PBDE mixtures were associated with higher urinary 8-iso-PGF2alpha and related isoprostane metabolites.

references.authors: Sethi TK, El-Ghamry MN, Kloecker GH
references.title: Radon and lung cancer.
references.finding: Radon is the second leading cause of lung cancer; alpha-particle DNA damage via reactive oxygen species is a proposed mechanism and a shared pathway with tobacco smoke; US EPA action level 4 pCi/L.

references.authors: Sjödin A, Mueller JF, Jones R, et al.
references.title: Serum elimination half-lives adjusted for ongoing exposure of tri-to hexabrominated diphenyl ethers: Determined in persons moving from North America to Australia.
references.finding: In a person moving from North America to lower-exposure Australia, serum elimination half-lives were about 0.9 (BDE-28), 1.2 (BDE-47), 1.0 (BDE-99), 2.2 (BDE-100) and 4.1 years (BDE-153).

references.authors: Snijder CA, te Velde E, Roeleveld N, et al.
references.title: Occupational exposure to chemical substances and time to pregnancy: a systematic review.
references.finding: Occupational lead and pesticides showed strong indications of longer time to pregnancy; evidence for organic solvents and other metals was equivocal.

references.authors: Strøm-Tejsen P, Zukowska D, Wargocki P, et al.
references.title: The effects of bedroom air quality on sleep and next-day performance.
references.finding: Lowering bedroom CO2 from about 2,400-2,600 ppm to 660-835 ppm by ventilation improved actigraphic sleep quality, next-day sleepiness and a logical-thinking test.

references.authors: Sundell J, Levin H, Nazaroff WW, et al.
references.title: Ventilation rates and health: multidisciplinary review of the scientific literature.
references.finding: Higher office ventilation (up to about 25 L/s per person) is associated with fewer sick building symptoms; home ventilation above 0.5 air changes per hour was linked to fewer allergic manifestations in Nordic children.

references.authors: Svanes Ø, Bertelsen RJ, Lygre SHL, et al.
references.title: Cleaning at Home and at Work in Relation to Lung Function Decline and Airway Obstruction.
references.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
references.finding: Women who cleaned at home (FEV1 decline -22.1 vs -18.5 mL/yr) or worked as cleaners (-22.4 mL/yr) lost lung function faster, with sprays and other agents both implicated; no association in men.

references.authors: Welch LS, Schrader SM, Turner TW, et al.
references.title: Effects of exposure to ethylene glycol ethers on shipyard painters: II. Male reproduction.
references.finding: Shipyard painters exposed to 2-ethoxyethanol and 2-methoxyethanol had more oligospermia and azoospermia and lower sperm counts.

references.authors: World Health Organization Regional Office for Europe
references.title: WHO guidelines for indoor air quality: dampness and mould
references.finding: The most important means of avoiding adverse health effects is preventing or minimising persistent dampness and microbial growth on interior surfaces and in building structures.

references.authors: World Health Organization
references.title: WHO handbook on indoor radon: a public health perspective
references.finding: Public-health handbook for national radon programmes; indoor radon causes a substantial number of lung cancers in the general population.

references.authors: World Health Organization Regional Office for Europe
references.title: WHO guidelines for indoor air quality: selected pollutants (benzene, carbon monoxide, formaldehyde, naphthalene, nitrogen dioxide, PAHs, radon, trichloroethylene, tetrachloroethylene)
references.finding: WHO indoor air guidelines for nine pollutants commonly found indoors at levels of health concern, including formaldehyde, NO2, benzene and radon.

references.authors: World Health Organization
references.title: WHO global air quality guidelines: particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10), ozone, nitrogen dioxide, sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide
references.finding: 2021 update lowering air quality guideline levels, including for PM2.5 and NO2, based on evidence of harm at lower concentrations than previously understood.

references.authors: World Health Organization
references.title: Radon and health (fact sheet)
references.finding: WHO recommends a national reference level of 100 Bq/m3 (not above 300 Bq/m3 where that is unachievable); radon causes 3-14% of lung cancers and risk rises about 16% per 100 Bq/m3.

references.authors: Wong GW, Brunekreef B, Ellwood P, et al.
references.title: Cooking fuels and prevalence of asthma: a global analysis of phase three of the International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood (ISAAC).
references.finding: Open-fire cooking was associated with wheeze and asthma symptoms (OR 1.78 in 6-7-year-olds), while gas cooking was not clearly associated with asthma in the global analysis.

references.authors: Yamaguchi T, Nakajima D, Ezoe Y, et al.
references.title: Measurement of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in new residential buildings and VOCs behavior over time.
references.finding: VOCs such as toluene, hexane, MEK and pinene were highest at first occupancy of new homes and declined over the following year.

references.authors: Yu L, Wang B, Cheng M, et al.
references.title: Association between indoor formaldehyde exposure and asthma: A systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies.
references.finding: Each 10 ug/m3 increase in indoor formaldehyde was associated with 10% higher childhood asthma risk (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.00-1.21).

references.authors: Yuan Y, Meeker JD, Ferguson KK
references.title: Serum polybrominated diphenyl ether (PBDE) concentrations in relation to biomarkers of oxidative stress and inflammation: The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2003-2004.
references.finding: Serum PBDEs showed no association with oxidative stress biomarkers and only small positive associations of BDE-153 with alkaline phosphatase and neutrophil count.

references.authors: Zhang X, Wargocki P, Lian Z, et al.
references.title: Effects of exposure to carbon dioxide and bioeffluents on perceived air quality, self-assessed acute health symptoms, and cognitive performance.
references.finding: Adding pure CO2 up to 3,000 ppm had no effect on cognition or symptoms, but reduced ventilation (bioeffluents with CO2 at 3,000 ppm) increased headache, fatigue and sleepiness and slowed some tasks.

references.authors: Zock JP, Plana E, Jarvis D, et al.
references.title: The use of household cleaning sprays and adult asthma: an international longitudinal study.
references.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
references.finding: Weekly use of household cleaning sprays was associated with new asthma symptoms or medication (RR 1.49) and wheeze (RR 1.39), with a dose-response; glass, furniture and air-freshener sprays drove the risk.

references.authors: Aamir AB, Latif R, Sorath F, et al.
references.title: Acute kidney injury induced by topical hair straightening products: A systematic review.
references.finding: Systematic review of acute kidney injury after hair straightening (formaldehyde, glycolic and glyoxylic acid products): median onset 2 days, 6 needed dialysis, all recovered.

references.authors: Adhikari S, Kumar R, Driver EM, et al.
references.title: Mass trends of parabens, triclocarban and triclosan in Arizona wastewater collected after the 2017 FDA ban on antimicrobials and during the COVID-19 pandemic.
references.finding: Arizona wastewater mass loads of triclosan fell 89% and triclocarban 80% after the 2017 FDA ban, while paraben loads rose 72%.

references.authors: Aiello AE, Larson EL, Levy SB
references.title: Consumer antibacterial soaps: effective or just risky?
references.finding: Systematic review: consumer soaps with 0.1-0.45% triclosan were no more effective than plain soap at preventing infectious symptoms or reducing hand bacteria; lab data showed cross-resistance to antibiotics.

references.authors: Allmyr M, Panagiotidis G, Sparve E, et al.
references.title: Human exposure to triclosan via toothpaste does not change CYP3A4 activity or plasma concentrations of thyroid hormones.
references.finding: Triclosan toothpaste raised plasma triclosan from 0.009-0.81 to 26-296 ng/g without changing CYP3A4 activity or thyroid hormones.

references.authors: Bailey JT, Chang CJ, Gaston SA, et al.
references.title: Use of hair straighteners and chemical relaxers and incidence of non-reproductive cancers.
references.finding: Straightener/relaxer use was associated with thyroid (HR 1.71) and pancreatic cancer (HR 2.66) and possibly NHL, with little dose-response across many cancer types tested.

references.authors: Bertrand KA, Delp L, Coogan PF, et al.
references.title: Hair relaxer use and risk of uterine cancer in the Black Women's Health Study.
references.finding: Heavy hair-relaxer use was not associated with uterine cancer overall (HR 1.18, CI 0.81-1.71), but in postmenopausal women heavy and 20+ year use went with HRs of 1.64-1.71.

references.authors: Boronow KE, Brody JG, Schaider LA, et al.
references.title: Serum concentrations of PFASs and exposure-related behaviors in African American and non-Hispanic white women.
references.finding: Flossing with Oral-B Glide was associated with higher serum PFHxS; Glide and competitor flosses contained fluorine; interviews came years after blood draw.

references.authors: Calafat AM, Ye X, Wong LY, et al.
references.title: Urinary concentrations of four parabens in the U.S. population: NHANES 2005-2006.
references.finding: Methylparaben was detected in 99.1% and propylparaben in 92.7% of US urine samples (medians 63.5 and 8.7 ug/L); levels were higher in women and non-Hispanic Black participants, consistent with personal-care product use.

references.authors: Carslaw N, Shaw D
references.title: Modification of cleaning product formulations could improve indoor air quality.
references.finding: Indoor chemistry modelling: terpene fragrances in cleaning products react with ozone to raise formaldehyde and particles for hours after a 10-minute cleaning, more when outdoor ozone is higher.

references.authors: Chang CJ, O'Brien KM, Keil AP, et al.
references.title: Use of Straighteners and Other Hair Products and Incident Uterine Cancer.
references.finding: Straightener use in the prior 12 months was associated with higher uterine cancer incidence (HR 1.80), 2.55 with more than 4 uses a year; dyes and perms were not associated.

references.authors: Cherry N, Labrèche F, Collins J, et al.
references.title: Occupational exposure to solvents and male infertility.
references.n: 656 and 574 manual workers attending Canadian fertility clinics (two series)
references.finding: High occupational solvent exposure was associated with low motile sperm count (OR 3.83 and 2.90 in two series); moderate exposure only in the first series.

references.authors: Dairkee SH, Moore DH, Luciani MG, et al.
references.title: Reduction of daily-use parabens and phthalates reverses accumulation of cancer-associated phenotypes within disease-free breast tissue of study subjects.
references.n: healthy women in a 28-day product-reduction regimen (REDUXE)
references.finding: Stopping paraben- and phthalate-containing products lowered urinary parabens and phthalates and was reported to reverse cancer-associated gene-expression patterns in breast fine-needle aspirates; uncontrolled, surrogate-marker study.

references.authors: Darbre PD, Aljarrah A, Miller WR, et al.
references.title: Concentrations of parabens in human breast tumours.
references.finding: Parabens averaged 20.6 ng/g in 20 breast tumours, mostly methylparaben; no normal-tissue comparison was made.

references.authors: DeVito MJ, Schecter A
references.title: Exposure assessment to dioxins from the use of tampons and diapers.
references.finding: Trace dioxins in tampons give exposures 13,000-240,000 times lower than dietary dioxin intake.

references.authors: Dewalque L, Pirard C, Vandepaer S, et al.
references.title: Temporal variability of urinary concentrations of phthalate metabolites, parabens and benzophenone-3 in a Belgian adult population.
references.n: 32 adults, 11 spot urines each over 4 months
references.finding: A single spot urine reasonably represented 4-month exposure for parabens, benzophenone-3 and monoethyl phthalate, but not for DEHP metabolites.

references.authors: Diepgen TL, Ofenloch R, Bruze M, et al.
references.title: Prevalence of fragrance contact allergy in the general population of five European countries: a cross-sectional study.
references.finding: Clinically relevant fragrance contact allergy was estimated at 1.9% (conservative 0.8%) of the general population, about twice as common in women.

references.authors: Ding N, Batterman S, Park SK
references.title: Exposure to Volatile Organic Compounds and Use of Feminine Hygiene Products Among Reproductive-Aged Women in the United States.
references.finding: Frequent vaginal douching (2+ times a month) was associated with 81% higher blood 1,4-dichlorobenzene, and feminine powder with 36% higher ethylbenzene.

references.authors: Dodson RE, Nishioka M, Standley LJ, et al.
references.title: Endocrine disruptors and asthma-associated chemicals in consumer products.
references.finding: Consumer products, including 'alternative' ones, contained 55 endocrine-disrupting or asthma-associated compounds, highest in fragranced products and sunscreens; many were not on the label.

references.authors: Downs CA, DiNardo JC, Stien D, et al.
references.title: Benzophenone Accumulates over Time from the Degradation of Octocrylene in Commercial Sunscreen Products.
references.finding: Octocrylene-containing sunscreens contained benzophenone (mean 39 mg/kg) that rose to a mean 75 mg/kg after accelerated ageing; the octocrylene-free product had none.

references.authors: Eberle CE, Sandler DP, Taylor KW, et al.
references.title: Hair dye and chemical straightener use and breast cancer risk in a large US population of black and white women.
references.finding: Permanent dye use was associated with 45% higher breast cancer risk in Black women and 7% in White women; straightener use HR 1.18 (CI 0.99-1.41) with a frequency trend.

references.authors: Ellison CA, Doyle PR, Haven CA, et al.
references.title: Integrating experimental data and mechanistic modeling to assess potential lead exposure from tampon use.
references.finding: Procter & Gamble scientists' model: under conservative assumptions, less than 1 ng (under 0.3%) of lead released from a tampon over 4 h would be available to vaginal tissue, as lead binds menstrual red cells and is reabsorbed by the tampon.

references.authors: Estill CF, Mayer A, Slone J, et al.
references.title: Assessment of triphenyl phosphate (TPhP) exposure to nail salon workers by air, hand wipe, and urine analysis.
references.finding: Post-shift urinary DPHP (1.35 vs 0.84 ug/g creatinine pre-shift) and hand-wipe TPHP rose over the workday and correlated, pointing to dermal uptake in technicians.

references.authors: European Commission
references.title: Commission Regulation (EU) No 358/2014 of 9 April 2014 amending Annexes II and V to Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 on cosmetic products
references.journal: Official Journal of the European Union
references.finding: Banned isopropyl-, isobutyl-, phenyl-, benzyl- and pentylparaben in cosmetics and restricted triclosan to specified products at up to 0.3% (0.2% in mouthwash).

references.authors: European Commission
references.title: Commission Regulation (EU) No 1004/2014 of 18 September 2014 amending Annex V to Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 on cosmetic products
references.journal: Official Journal of the European Union
references.finding: Limited butyl- and propylparaben to 0.14% (as acid), barred them from leave-on nappy-area products for children under 3, and kept methyl/ethylparaben at 0.4% each, 0.8% for mixtures.

references.authors: European Commission
references.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/1176 of 7 July 2022 amending Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 as regards the use of certain UV filters in cosmetic products
references.journal: Official Journal of the European Union
references.finding: Capped benzophenone-3 at 6% in face, hand and lip products, 2.2% in body products and 0.5% when used only to protect the formulation, and octocrylene at 10% (9% in propellant sprays).

references.authors: European Commission
references.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/1545 of 26 July 2023 amending Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 as regards labelling of fragrance allergens in cosmetic products
references.journal: Official Journal of the European Union
references.finding: Requires about 80 fragrance allergens to be named on labels above 0.001% in leave-on and 0.01% in rinse-off products, with transition to 2026 (placing on market) and 2028 (availability).

references.authors: European Commission
references.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/996 of 3 April 2024 amending Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 as regards the use of Vitamin A, Alpha-Arbutin and Arbutin and certain substances with potential endocrine disrupting properties in cosmetic products
references.journal: Official Journal of the European Union
references.finding: Prohibited the UV filter 4-methylbenzylidene camphor (from 2025-2026) and further restricted triclosan and triclocarban, including excluding them from mouthwash.

references.authors: Farooq H, Mhatre P, Aggarwal R, et al.
references.title: A systematic review of association between use of hair products and benign and malignant gynecological conditions.
references.journal: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
references.finding: Systematic review: evidence on hair products and gynaecological conditions is insufficient to determine whether a positive association exists; noted permanent dye breast cancer RR 1.08 and relaxer-fibroid and relaxer-fecundability associations.

references.authors: US Food and Drug Administration
references.title: Safety and Effectiveness of Consumer Antiseptics; Topical Antimicrobial Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use. Final rule. 81 FR 61106
references.finding: Found 19 consumer antiseptic wash ingredients, including triclosan and triclocarban, not generally recognized as safe and effective, effective September 2017; deferred benzalkonium chloride, benzethonium chloride and chloroxylenol.

references.authors: US Food and Drug Administration
references.title: Sunscreen Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use; Proposed Rule. 84 FR 6204
references.finding: Proposed only zinc oxide and titanium dioxide as generally recognized as safe and effective, PABA and trolamine salicylate as not, and 12 organic filters including oxybenzone and avobenzone as needing more data; blood levels under 0.5 ng/mL would waive carcinogenicity studies.

references.authors: US Food and Drug Administration
references.title: FDA Finds Insufficient Data to Determine Safety of PFAS in Cosmetic Products (Report on the Use of PFAS in Cosmetic Products and Associated Risks)
references.finding: Under MoCRA, FDA found 51 PFAS in 1,744 cosmetic formulations; of the 25 most used, 5 appeared low concern, 1 had a potential safety concern, and for most safety could not be established because toxicology data were incomplete.

references.authors: US Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs / FDA
references.title: Use of Formaldehyde and Formaldehyde-Releasing Chemicals as an Ingredient in Hair Smoothing Products or Hair Straightening Products (RIN 0910-AI83), proposed rule: pending EO 12866 regulatory review
references.finding: FDA's proposed rule to ban formaldehyde and formaldehyde-releasing chemicals in hair smoothing/straightening products was received for White House review on 6 August 2026 and had not been concluded; no ban is yet in effect.

references.authors: US Food and Drug Administration
references.title: Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022 (MoCRA)
references.finding: MoCRA requires safety substantiation records, serious adverse event reporting within 15 business days, facility registration and product listing, mandates an FDA fragrance-allergen labelling rule (not yet issued) and a PFAS report (published December 2025).

references.authors: US Food and Drug Administration
references.title: The Facts on Tampons and Tampon Safety
references.finding: FDA commissioned an independent literature review of tampon contaminants (2024) and reports that its 2026 laboratory study found the amount of metals likely released during use is too small to cause harm.

references.authors: Ferguson KK, McElrath TF, Chen YH, et al.
references.title: Urinary phthalate metabolites and biomarkers of oxidative stress in pregnant women: a repeated measures analysis.
references.finding: Urinary phthalate metabolites, including monoethyl phthalate from fragrance-related diethyl phthalate, were associated with higher urinary 8-OHdG and 8-isoprostane across pregnancy.

references.authors: Ferguson KK, Lan Z, Yu Y, et al.
references.title: Urinary concentrations of phenols in association with biomarkers of oxidative stress in pregnancy: Assessment of effects independent of phthalates.
references.finding: Dichlorophenols, benzophenone-3, triclosan and some parabens were associated with higher urinary 8-OHdG and 8-isoprostane, but none was consistently selected once correlated phthalate metabolites were included.

references.authors: Filley AR, Woodruff CM
references.title: The Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022: What dermatologists need to know.
references.finding: Overview for dermatologists of the US Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022.

references.authors: Geier J, Schubert S, Reich K, et al.
references.title: Contact sensitization to essential oils: IVDK data of the years 2010-2019.
references.finding: 8.3% of dermatitis patients tested reacted to at least one essential oil (ylang-ylang 3.9%, lemongrass 2.6%); masseurs and cosmeticians were at higher risk.

references.authors: Gonzalez H, Farbrot A, Larkö O, et al.
references.title: Percutaneous absorption of the sunscreen benzophenone-3 after repeated whole-body applications, with and without ultraviolet irradiation.
references.finding: Volunteers excreted 1.2-8.7% of applied BP-3 in urine and were still excreting it 5 days after the last application; UV exposure did not change absorption.

references.authors: Halden RU, Lindeman AE, Aiello AE, et al.
references.title: The Florence Statement on Triclosan and Triclocarban.
references.finding: Florence Statement: triclosan and triclocarban are persistent, bioaccumulative endocrine disruptors without demonstrated benefit in most consumer uses; antimicrobials should be used only where they provide evidence-based health benefit.

references.authors: Han C, Lim YH, Hong YC
references.title: Ten-year trends in urinary concentrations of triclosan and benzophenone-3 in the general U.S. population from 2003 to 2012.
references.finding: Urinary triclosan trended down and BP-3 up after 2005-2006; higher income groups had higher levels of both; BP-3 was higher in women and non-Hispanic Whites.

references.authors: Harley KG, Kogut K, Madrigal DS, et al.
references.title: Reducing Phthalate, Paraben, and Phenol Exposure from Personal Care Products in Adolescent Girls: Findings from the HERMOSA Intervention Study.
references.finding: Three days of products labelled free of phthalates, parabens, triclosan and BP-3 lowered urinary MEP 27%, methylparaben 44%, propylparaben 45%, triclosan 36% and BP-3 36%; ethyl- and butylparaben unexpectedly rose.

references.authors: Harris KJ, Munoz G, Woo V, et al.
references.title: Targeted and Suspect Screening of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances in Cosmetics and Personal Care Products.
references.finding: Polyfluoroalkyl phosphate esters (PAPs) were found in 99.7% of products, sometimes at very high levels, with lower PFCAs and PFSAs.

references.authors: Harvey PW, Everett DJ
references.title: Significance of the detection of esters of p-hydroxybenzoic acid (parabens) in human breast tumours.
references.finding: Editorial accompanying the Darbre paper discussing its design and what can and cannot be inferred from finding parabens in tumours, explicitly not the cause of the tumours.

references.authors: Helm JS, Nishioka M, Brody JG, et al.
references.title: Measurement of endocrine disrupting and asthma-associated chemicals in hair products used by Black women.
references.finding: Hair products used by Black women contained parabens, diethyl phthalate, nonylphenols, cyclosiloxanes and fragrances, mostly unlabelled; children's relaxers contained chemicals restricted in California or the EU.

references.authors: Hernandez AM, Smith SJ, Vahora MS, et al.
references.title: Systematic Review of the Epidemiology of Hair Relaxer Use and Hormone-Sensitive Reproductive Outcomes Among Black Adult Women in the United States.
references.finding: Systematic review by a private risk-consulting firm (Benchmark Risk Group, which funded it): weight of evidence does not support hair relaxers as a risk factor for breast, ovarian or uterine cancer in US Black women; no study characterised product chemicals.

references.authors: Homburg M, Rasmussen ÅK, Ramhøj L, et al.
references.title: The Influence of Triclosan on the Thyroid Hormone System in Humans - A Systematic Review.
references.finding: Systematic review of human studies: triclosan-thyroid associations were inconsistent in direction and it is not possible to conclude that current exposure affects thyroid function.

references.authors: Huang K, Zhang X, Wang B, et al.
references.title: Accurate assessment of parabens exposure in healthy Chinese female adults: Findings from a multi-pathway exposure assessment coupled with intervention study.
references.finding: Personal-care products supplied over 99% of paraben exposure; unadjusted spot-urine intraclass correlations were poor (0.13-0.30) and improved only after kinetic modelling.

references.authors: Hutter HP, Wallner P, Moshammer H, et al.
references.title: Blood concentrations of polycyclic musks in healthy young adults.
references.finding: Galaxolide and tonalide were the polycyclic musks most often found in plasma (max 4,100 and 800 ng/L); body-lotion use and age predicted galaxolide; women had higher levels.

references.authors: Hutter HP, Wallner P, Moshammer H, et al.
references.title: Synthetic musks in blood of healthy young adults: relationship to cosmetics use.
references.finding: Polycyclic musks in blood were predicted by younger age and use of lotion and perfume; nitro musks were less frequent and lower than in the 1990s.

references.authors: Hutter HP, Wallner P, Hartl W, et al.
references.title: Higher blood concentrations of synthetic musks in women above fifty years than in younger women.
references.finding: Older women had higher plasma synthetic musks than younger women; galaxolide tracked frequent use of perfume, deodorant and shampoo.

references.authors: Iyer AP, Xue J, Honda M, et al.
references.title: Urinary levels of triclosan and triclocarban in several Asian countries, Greece and the USA: Association with oxidative stress.
references.finding: Triclosan was detected in 83% and triclocarban in 19% of samples; triclocarban correlated non-significantly with urinary 8-OHdG.

references.authors: Janjua NR, Mogensen B, Andersson AM, et al.
references.title: Systemic absorption of the sunscreens benzophenone-3, octyl-methoxycinnamate, and 3-(4-methyl-benzylidene) camphor after whole-body topical application and reproductive hormone levels in humans.
references.finding: Whole-body 10% BP-3, OMC and 4-MBC cream reached plasma levels up to 300 ng/mL BP-3; small hormone differences were unrelated to exposure.

references.authors: Janjua NR, Mortensen GK, Andersson AM, et al.
references.title: Systemic uptake of diethyl phthalate, dibutyl phthalate, and butyl paraben following whole-body topical application and reproductive and thyroid hormone levels in humans.
references.finding: Whole-body cream with diethyl phthalate, dibutyl phthalate and butylparaben produced serum peaks within hours but no short-term changes in reproductive or thyroid hormones.

references.authors: Janjua NR, Kongshoj B, Andersson AM, et al.
references.title: Sunscreens in human plasma and urine after repeated whole-body topical application.
references.finding: BP-3, 4-MBC and OMC appeared in plasma 1-2 h after first application; some 96-h plasma levels exceeded 24-h levels, suggesting accumulation.

references.authors: Jaskulak M, Cinkusz M, Franchuk K, et al.
references.title: Endocrine and Reproductive Health Considerations of Sunscreen UV Filters: Insights from a Comprehensive Review 2014-2024.
references.finding: Review of 2014-2024 human evidence: benzophenones associated with poorer sperm quality in some studies, weaker findings for ovarian reserve, mixed prenatal results; stresses balancing endocrine concerns with photoprotection.

references.authors: Jeffrey AM, Williams GM
references.title: The paper by Darbre et al. (2004) reports the measurement of parabens in 20 human breast tumors.
references.finding: Published letter criticising the Darbre et al. paraben-tumour study, with an author reply.

references.authors: Jin Y, Eppihimer M, Alam MS, et al.
references.title: Do metals in tampons pose a health risk? A toxicological risk assessment study.
references.finding: FDA laboratory study: 19 metals including trace lead, arsenic and cadmium were present, but releases under exaggerated extraction conditions gave margins of safety indicating negligible toxicological concern.

references.authors: Jovanovic N, Bright F, Thomsen C, et al.
references.title: Levers to decrease exposure to harmful chemicals: the case of Personal Care Products and cosmetics.
references.finding: Refraining from usual personal-care products for 5 days lowered urinary phenoxyacetic acid 64%, BPA 39%, methylparaben 30% and MEP 22%, but several chemicals remained detectable; authors argue regulation would be more efficient and fairer.

references.authors: Käfferlein HU, Göen T, Angerer J
references.title: Musk xylene: analysis, occurrence, kinetics, and toxicology.
references.finding: Musk xylene is lipophilic and persistent and found in milk, fat and blood, but there was no evidence of substantial human risk.

references.authors: Kang H, Kim S, Lee H, et al.
references.title: Parabens, bisphenols, and other environmental phenols exposure from cosmetics use in Korean adolescent girls: Findings from a 2-day intervention study.
references.finding: A 2-day cosmetics restriction did not lower chemical levels overall; excluding non-users at baseline, BPA fell 33% and benzophenones 12-23%.

references.authors: Kim JH, Kwak JM, Kang H
references.title: Web-based behavioral intervention to reduce exposure to phthalate metabolites, bisphenol A, triclosan, and parabens in mothers with young children: A randomized controlled trial.
references.finding: A web-based behavioural intervention lowered urinary MEHP, MEOHP, BPA, methylparaben and propylparaben versus written information (decreases of 4-28% after one month).

references.authors: Krause M, Klit A, Blomberg Jensen M, et al.
references.title: Sunscreens: are they beneficial for health? An overview of endocrine disrupting properties of UV-filters.
references.finding: Review of endocrine-disrupting properties of UV filters: rodent reproductive and thyroid effects, rapid skin absorption, BP-3 in 96% of US urine samples, few human outcome studies.

references.authors: Lamplugh A, Harries M, Xiang F, et al.
references.title: Occupational exposure to volatile organic compounds and health risks in Colorado nail salons.
references.finding: Formaldehyde exceeded the NIOSH recommended limit in one salon; modelled 20-year cancer risks from formaldehyde and benzene exceeded EPA benchmarks for technicians.

references.authors: Li Y, Fletcher T, Mucs D, et al.
references.title: Half-lives of PFOS, PFHxS and PFOA after end of exposure to contaminated drinking water.
references.finding: After contaminated water was replaced, serum PFAS half-lives were 5.3 years for PFHxS, 3.4 for PFOS and 2.7 for PFOA.

references.authors: Lundov MD, Opstrup MS, Johansen JD
references.title: Methylisothiazolinone contact allergy--growing epidemic.
references.finding: Methylisothiazolinone contact allergy rose from 2.0% to 3.7% of patch-tested patients in 2010-2012; cosmetics were the most common relevant source.

references.authors: Marcelis Q, Deconinck E, Rogiers V, et al.
references.title: Chemical characterization of menstrual and intimate care products: An extractables & leachables investigation.
references.n: menstrual and intimate care products from EU, US and China
references.finding: Of 55 extractable chemicals, 19 leached under realistic simulated use (fragrances, phthalates, plastic additives); menstrual sea sponges leached the most metals.

references.authors: Marroquin J, Kiomourtzoglou MA, Scranton A, et al.
references.title: Chemicals in menstrual products: A systematic review.
references.finding: Systematic review: phthalates, VOCs, parabens, phenols, fragrance chemicals and dioxins were detected in menstrual products; exposure per cycle and newer products (cups, period underwear) are unstudied.

references.authors: Matta MK, Zusterzeel R, Pilli NR, et al.
references.title: Effect of Sunscreen Application Under Maximal Use Conditions on Plasma Concentration of Sunscreen Active Ingredients: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
references.finding: Under maximal use (4 applications/day for 4 days), avobenzone, oxybenzone, octocrylene and ecamsule exceeded FDA's 0.5 ng/mL threshold on day 1; oxybenzone reached 169-210 ng/mL.

references.authors: Matta MK, Florian J, Zusterzeel R, et al.
references.title: Effect of Sunscreen Application on Plasma Concentration of Sunscreen Active Ingredients: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
references.finding: All six tested filters exceeded 0.5 ng/mL after a single application; oxybenzone peaked at 258 ng/mL (lotion) and homosalate at up to 23 ng/mL; authors say people should not stop using sunscreen.

references.authors: Meeker JD, Cantonwine DE, Rivera-González LO, et al.
references.title: Distribution, variability, and predictors of urinary concentrations of phenols and parabens among pregnant women in Puerto Rico.
references.finding: Intraclass correlations ranged from 0.24 (BPA) to 0.62 (benzophenone-3), 0.47 for triclosan; sunscreen and lotion use predicted BP-3, lotion and cosmetics predicted parabens, liquid soap predicted triclosan.

references.authors: Mendelsohn E, Hagopian A, Hoffman K, et al.
references.title: Nail polish as a source of exposure to triphenyl phosphate.
references.finding: Painting nails with a polish containing 0.97% triphenyl phosphate raised its urinary metabolite DPHP about 7-fold 10-14 h later; gloves blocked most uptake, showing the route is dermal.

references.authors: Mínguez-Alarcón L, Chiu YH, Nassan FL, et al.
references.title: Urinary concentrations of benzophenone-3 and reproductive outcomes among women undergoing infertility treatment with assisted reproductive technologies.
references.finding: Benzophenone-3 was associated with higher implantation, pregnancy and live birth among women who did outdoor work, a pattern the authors attribute partly to residual lifestyle confounding.

references.authors: Mohammed YH, Holmes A, Haridass IN, et al.
references.title: Support for the Safe Use of Zinc Oxide Nanoparticle Sunscreens: Lack of Skin Penetration or Cellular Toxicity after Repeated Application in Volunteers.
references.n: human volunteers, 5 days of repeated application
references.finding: Zinc oxide nanoparticle sunscreen stayed on the skin surface and in furrows and did not penetrate or harm the viable epidermis.

references.authors: Moos RK, Angerer J, Dierkes G, et al.
references.title: Metabolism and elimination of methyl, iso- and n-butyl paraben in human urine after single oral dosage.
references.finding: After oral dosing, 80-85% of the captured paraben metabolites were excreted in urine within 24 h; parent methylparaben made up 17% of the dose, butylparabens 6-7%.

references.authors: Moos RK, Apel P, Schröter-Kermani C, et al.
references.title: Daily intake and hazard index of parabens based upon 24 h urine samples of the German Environmental Specimen Bank from 1995 to 2012.
references.finding: Back-calculated median intakes ranged from 1.1 (isobutylparaben) to 47.5 ug/kg/day (methylparaben); about 5% exceeded acceptable intake for individual parabens and the cumulative hazard index was 1.3 at the 95th percentile, under deliberately conservative assumptions.

references.authors: Mustieles V, Balogh RK, Axelstad M, et al.
references.title: Benzophenone-3: Comprehensive review of the toxicological and human evidence with meta-analysis of human biomonitoring studies.
references.finding: BP-3 and its metabolite BP-1 show estrogenic activity at human-relevant concentrations; North Americans' urinary BP-3 averages 10-20 times European and Asian levels; authors endorse EU limits but say people should not stop sunscreen and suggest inorganic filters for susceptible groups.

references.authors: Nassan FL, Coull BA, Gaskins AJ, et al.
references.title: Personal Care Product Use in Men and Urinary Concentrations of Select Phthalate Metabolites and Parabens: Results from the Environment And Reproductive Health (EARTH) Study.
references.finding: Cologne/perfume and deodorant use raised urinary monoethyl phthalate by 83% and 74%; sunscreen and hand/body lotion raised urinary parabens by 66-156% and 79-147%, with the largest effects for use within 6 h of urine collection.

references.authors: Ogunsina K, O'Brien KM, White AJ, et al.
references.title: Hair Straightener Use in Relation to Prevalent and Incident Fibroids in the Sister Study with a Focus on Black Women.
references.n: Sister Study, focus on 4,162 Black women
references.finding: Straightener use at ages 10-13 was associated with young-onset fibroids (ORs about 1.2-1.8); sensitivity analyses suggested possible bias from fibroid misclassification.

references.authors: Ogunsina K, Richardson KA, White A, et al.
references.title: Occupational exposures among hairdressers and the occurrence of hormone-related conditions.
references.finding: Ever working as a hairdresser was associated with endometriosis (HR 1.61) but not fibroids, breast, ovarian or uterine cancer overall.

references.authors: Pak VM, Powers M, Liu J
references.title: Occupational chemical exposures among cosmetologists: risk of reproductive disorders.
references.finding: Review of reproductive risks for cosmetologists exposed to dyes, solvents and nail products; calls for more research and workplace controls.

references.authors: Parlett LE, Calafat AM, Swan SH
references.title: Women's exposure to phthalates in relation to use of personal care products.
references.finding: Women who had used perfume in the prior 24 h had 2.92 times higher urinary monoethyl phthalate; hair spray, nail polish and deodorant also predicted MEP.

references.authors: Patti MA, Henderson NB, Gajjar P, et al.
references.title: Gestational triclosan exposure and infant birth weight: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Gestational triclosan was not clearly associated with birth weight (GA-adjusted -12 g, CI -29 to 5); inverse associations were stronger in higher-exposure populations.

references.authors: Pierce JS, Abelmann A, Spicer LJ, et al.
references.title: Characterization of formaldehyde exposure resulting from the use of four professional hair straightening products.
references.finding: Keratin smoothing treatments produced airborne formaldehyde up to 1.19 ppm during application; even a product labelled formaldehyde-free released formaldehyde-releasing chemicals; estimated exposures can meet or exceed occupational limits.

references.authors: Pütz KW, Namazkar S, Plassmann M, et al.
references.title: Are cosmetics a significant source of PFAS in Europe? product inventories, chemical characterization and emission estimates.
references.finding: PFAS emissions from cosmetics in Europe are significant but considerably lower than those from washing PFAS-coated textiles.

references.authors: Ragnarsdóttir O, Abou-Elwafa Abdallah M, Harrad S
references.title: Dermal bioavailability of perfluoroalkyl substances using in vitro 3D human skin equivalent models.
references.finding: In 3D human skin models, shorter-chain PFAS (C5-C8 acids, C4-C7 sulfonates) permeated skin while longer chains were retained in the skin tissue.

references.authors: Rehfeld A, Dissing S, Skakkebæk NE
references.title: Chemical UV Filters Mimic the Effect of Progesterone on Ca(2+) Signaling in Human Sperm Cells.
references.finding: 13 of 29 UV filters induced calcium signals in human sperm in vitro, nine by activating the CatSper channel like progesterone, some at nanomolar levels and additively in mixtures.

references.authors: Reiner JL, Wong CM, Arcaro KF, et al.
references.title: Synthetic musk fragrances in human milk from the United States.
references.finding: Synthetic musks (galaxolide, tonalide, musk xylene, musk ketone) were found in US breast milk; estimated infant intake was lower than for legacy POPs such as PCBs.

references.authors: Riley P, Lamont T
references.title: Triclosan/copolymer containing toothpastes for oral health.
references.finding: Cochrane review: triclosan/copolymer fluoride toothpaste reduced plaque, gingivitis and bleeding (moderate quality) and slightly reduced caries versus fluoride toothpaste, with no serious safety concerns over up to 3 years.

references.authors: Robert T, Tang E, Kervadec J, et al.
references.title: Hair-straightening cosmetics containing glyoxylic acid induce crystalline nephropathy.
references.finding: Topical glyoxylic acid, used in 'formaldehyde-free' straighteners, was absorbed, metabolised to oxalate and caused calcium-oxalate kidney injury in mice, explaining recurrent acute kidney injury in a patient.

references.authors: Rubin CB, Brod B
references.title: Natural Does Not Mean Safe-The Dirt on Clean Beauty Products.
references.finding: JAMA Dermatology editorial arguing that 'natural' and 'clean' labels do not mean safe.

references.authors: Rundle CW, Hu S, Presley CL, et al.
references.title: Triclosen and Its Alternatives in Antibacterial Soaps.
references.n: survey of US antibacterial soap products
references.finding: After the FDA ban, benzalkonium chloride, chloroxylenol and (still) triclosan were the commonest antibacterials in soaps; the authors note antibacterial additives do not improve soap effectiveness.

references.authors: Samarasinghe SVAC, Krishnan K, Naidu R, et al.
references.title: Parabens generate reactive oxygen species in human spermatozoa.
references.finding: In vitro, parabens raised mitochondrial and cytosolic ROS in human sperm and reduced motility and viability in a chain-length-dependent way; methylparaben at clinically used concentrations raised ROS and oxidative DNA adducts but not DNA fragmentation.

references.authors: Sandborgh-Englund G, Adolfsson-Erici M, Odham G, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics of triclosan following oral ingestion in humans.
references.finding: After 4 mg oral triclosan, plasma levels peaked within 1-3 h, the terminal plasma half-life was 21 h, and most was excreted within 24 h.

references.authors: Shearston JA, Upson K, Gordon M, et al.
references.title: Tampons as a source of exposure to metal(loid)s.
references.finding: All 16 metal(loid)s measured were detectable, with geometric means of 120 ng/g lead, 6.74 ng/g cadmium and 2.56 ng/g arsenic; no product category was consistently lower; absorption was not studied.

references.authors: Shearston JA, Upson K, Gordon M, et al.
references.title: Communicating risk in the face of data gaps: Toxic metals in tampons.
references.finding: The tampon-metal authors' published commentary on communicating risk when absorption data are missing.

references.authors: Shin MY, Choi JW, Lee S, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics of transdermal methyl-, ethyl-, and propylparaben in humans following single dermal administration.
references.finding: After a single whole-arm dermal application of labelled methyl-, ethyl- and propylparaben, terminal half-lives were 9.3-12.2 h, longer than after oral intake, with a larger share of unconjugated (active) paraben in blood.

references.authors: Singh J, Mumford SL, Pollack AZ, et al.
references.title: Tampon use, environmental chemicals and oxidative stress in the BioCycle study.
references.finding: Tampon users had non-significantly higher blood mercury (25%) and urinary isoprostane (about 5%) than non-users; no association with inflammation markers.

references.authors: Smith KW, Braun JM, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Predictors and variability of urinary paraben concentrations in men and women, including before and during pregnancy.
references.n: fertility-clinic men and women with repeated urine samples
references.finding: Intraclass correlations for methyl- and propylparaben were 0.42-0.54, so a single urine sample reasonably ranked exposure over several months; concentrations were 3.8 times higher in African American participants.

references.authors: Snijder CA, te Velde E, Roeleveld N, et al.
references.title: Occupational exposure to chemical substances and time to pregnancy: a systematic review.
references.finding: Systematic review of occupational chemicals and time to pregnancy: reasonably consistent evidence for lead and pesticides, equivocal for organic solvents.

references.authors: Steinemann A
references.title: Fragranced consumer products: exposures and effects from emissions.
references.finding: In a national online survey, 34.7% of adults reported health problems such as migraine or breathing difficulty from fragranced products; self-reported, cross-sectional.

references.authors: Surber C
references.title: Letter to the Editor Regarding Benzophenone Accumulates over Time from the Degradation of Octocrylene in Commercial Sunscreen Products.
references.finding: Published letter to the editor challenging the Downs et al. octocrylene-benzophenone study.

references.authors: Taylor KM, Weisskopf M, Shine J
references.title: Human exposure to nitro musks and the evaluation of their potential toxicity: an overview.
references.finding: Nitro musks reach people through skin, dust and inhaled fragrance; human data are limited and animal evidence on developmental effects is conflicting; further epidemiology is warranted.

references.authors: Tran JM, Comstock JR, Reeder MJ
references.title: Natural Is Not Always Better: The Prevalence of Allergenic Ingredients in "Clean" Beauty Products.
references.finding: 93.8% of 'clean' beauty products contained at least one potential contact allergen, most often fragrance/botanicals (82.9%).

references.authors: Turati F, Pelucchi C, Galeone C, et al.
references.title: Personal hair dye use and bladder cancer: a meta-analysis.
references.finding: Personal hair dye use was not associated with bladder cancer (RR 0.93; permanent dyes 0.92).

references.authors: Upson K, Shearston JA, Kioumourtzoglou MA
references.title: Menstrual Products as a Source of Environmental Chemical Exposure: A Review from the Epidemiologic Perspective.
references.finding: Epidemiological review of menstrual products as a route of chemical exposure, noting vaginal tissue's high permeability and the lack of exposure data.

references.authors: Uter W, Aalto-Korte K, Agner T, et al.
references.title: The epidemic of methylisothiazolinone contact allergy in Europe: follow-up on changing exposures.
references.finding: After EU restrictions, methylisothiazolinone contact allergy prevalence fell by half from 2015 (5.97%) to 2017 (2.96%), with fewer leave-on cosmetic culprits.

references.authors: van der Burg B, Schreurs R, van der Linden S, et al.
references.title: Endocrine effects of polycyclic musks: do we smell a rat?
references.finding: Polycyclic musks were very weakly estrogenic in vitro without clear effects in young rats or zebrafish, but showed anti-estrogenic, anti-androgenic and anti-progestagenic activity in cell assays.

references.authors: van Eijk AM, Zulaika G, Lenchner M, et al.
references.title: Menstrual cup use, leakage, acceptability, safety, and availability: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Menstrual cups showed no adverse effect on vaginal flora and leakage similar to or lower than pads or tampons; rare harms included toxic shock (5 reports) and IUD dislodgement.

references.authors: Vélez MP, Arbuckle TE, Fraser WD
references.title: Female exposure to phenols and phthalates and time to pregnancy: the Maternal-Infant Research on Environmental Chemicals (MIREC) Study.
references.finding: Women in the top triclosan quartile had lower fecundability (FOR 0.84) on a single post-conception urine; BPA was not associated and some phthalates pointed to shorter time to pregnancy.

references.authors: Wang Z, Yuan G, Sun M, et al.
references.title: Decorative cosmetics and skin care products contribute significantly to short-chain perfluoroalkyl carboxylates exposure.
references.finding: Skin-model permeation plus product concentrations suggested dermal intake of short-chain PFCAs from cosmetics may exceed dietary intake, and that cosmetics can contribute substantially to PFOA intake in regular users.

references.authors: Watkins DJ, Ferguson KK, Anzalota Del Toro LV, et al.
references.title: Associations between urinary phenol and paraben concentrations and markers of oxidative stress and inflammation among pregnant women in Puerto Rico.
references.finding: Per interquartile increase, urinary isoprostane was 17% higher for benzophenone-3, 27% for butylparaben and 20% for propylparaben; triclosan went with 31% higher IL-6.

references.authors: Wise LA, Palmer JR, Reich D, et al.
references.title: Hair relaxer use and risk of uterine leiomyomata in African-American women.
references.finding: Ever use of hair relaxers was associated with 17% higher incidence of uterine fibroids, with trends for frequency, duration and number of scalp burns.

references.authors: Wise LA, Wang TR, Ncube CN, et al.
references.title: Use of Chemical Hair Straighteners and Fecundability in a North American Preconception Cohort.
references.finding: Hair relaxer use was associated with slightly lower fecundability (current FR 0.81, CI 0.64-1.03; former 0.89, CI 0.81-0.98; 10+ years 0.71), with non-monotonic patterns.

references.authors: Zhang Y, Birmann BM, Han J, et al.
references.title: Personal use of permanent hair dyes and cancer risk and mortality in US women: prospective cohort study.
references.finding: Personal permanent hair dye use was not associated with most cancers or cancer mortality (solid cancers HR 0.98); slight increases for basal cell carcinoma and some hormone-receptor-negative breast and ovarian cancers with high cumulative dose.

references.authors: Zhivagui M, Hoda A, Valenzuela N, et al.
references.title: DNA damage and somatic mutations in mammalian cells after irradiation with a nail polish dryer.
references.finding: UV-nail-polish-dryer light caused ROS, 8-oxoguanine-type damage, mitochondrial dysfunction and dose-dependent ROS-signature mutations in mouse and human cells.

references.authors: Zhong Q, Peng M, He J, et al.
references.title: Association of prenatal exposure to phenols and parabens with birth size: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Prenatal triclosan, BP-3, BPA and parabens showed mostly non-significant and inconsistent associations with birth size.

references.authors: Bao W, Liu B, Rong S, et al.
references.title: Association Between Bisphenol A Exposure and Risk of All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality in US Adults
references.finding: Top vs bottom tertile of urinary BPA: all-cause mortality HR 1.49 (1.01-2.19), CVD mortality 1.46 (0.67-3.15), cancer mortality 0.98; 344 deaths.

references.authors: Beyer A, Schorgg P, Karavasiloglou N, et al.
references.title: Urinary phthalate concentrations and mortality risk: A population-based study
references.finding: Higher MBzP and MnBP (low-molecular-weight phthalate metabolites, not DEHP) were linked to higher mortality (top quartile HR 1.27 and 1.35).

references.authors: Blaauwendraad SM, Boxem AJ, Gaillard R, et al.
references.title: Periconception bisphenol and phthalate concentrations in women and men, time to pregnancy, and risk of miscarriage
references.n: 938 preconception and 1,366 pregnant women, 1,202 men (Generation R Next)
references.finding: Preconception BPS and a DINCH metabolite (mCOCH) in women were linked to longer time to pregnancy, but several phthalate metabolites were linked to shorter time to pregnancy; authors call results hypothesis-generating.

references.authors: Blakey A, Ott K, Peters T, et al.
references.title: Anti-PVC advocacy disguised as science (Response to Carlstedt et al., PVC flooring is related to human uptake of phthalates in infants)
references.finding: Letter titled 'Anti-PVC advocacy disguised as science' disputing the Carlstedt PVC-flooring study; a reply was published.

references.authors: Bornehag CG, Carlstedt F, Jönsson BA, et al.
references.title: Prenatal phthalate exposures and anogenital distance in Swedish boys
references.finding: First-trimester DiNP metabolites (the DEHP replacement) were associated with shorter anoscrotal distance, but the reduction was small (about 4% per IQR).

references.authors: Braun JM, Smith KW, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Variability of urinary phthalate metabolite and bisphenol A concentrations before and during pregnancy
references.finding: During pregnancy ICCs were 0.50 for MEP, 0.45 for MBP, 0.25 for MBzP, 0.12 for BPA and 0.08 for sum-DEHP; one spot sample adequately classified MEP and MBP but not DEHP or BPA.

references.authors: Buckley JP, Pacyga DC, Xun X, et al.
references.title: Gestational Exposure to 10 Classes of Priority Chemicals and Birth Outcomes in the ECHO Cohort
references.finding: Among 113 analytes in 10 chemical classes, several phthalates and alternative plasticizers were linked to slightly shorter gestation; summed DiNP metabolites: 0.6 days shorter, preterm birth OR 1.16 per IQR.

references.authors: Calafat AM, Needham LL, Silva MJ, et al.
references.title: Exposure to di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate among premature neonates in a neonatal intensive care unit
references.finding: Premature infants receiving intensive care via PVC devices had DEHP metabolite levels several-fold to orders of magnitude above the general population (geometric mean MEHP 100 vs 3.4 ng/mL).

references.authors: Camacho L, Lewis SM, Vanlandingham MM, et al.
references.title: A two-year toxicology study of bisphenol A (BPA) in Sprague-Dawley rats: CLARITY-BPA core study results
references.finding: Guideline-compliant 2-year CLARITY-BPA rat study (2.5-25,000 ug/kg/day): no BPA-related effects in in-life data; inconsistent lesions, with a possible relationship only at 25,000 ug/kg/day.

references.authors: Carlstedt F, Jönsson BA, Bornehag CG
references.title: PVC flooring is related to human uptake of phthalates in infants
references.finding: Infants with PVC flooring in the bedroom had significantly higher urinary MBzP (the BBzP metabolite).

references.authors: Carwile JL, Luu HT, Bassett LS, et al.
references.title: Polycarbonate bottle use and urinary bisphenol A concentrations
references.finding: A week of drinking cold beverages from polycarbonate bottles raised urinary BPA by 69%.

references.authors: Carwile JL, Ye X, Zhou X, et al.
references.title: Canned soup consumption and urinary bisphenol A: a randomized crossover trial
references.finding: One serving of canned soup a day for 5 days raised specific-gravity-adjusted urinary BPA to 20.8 ug/L vs 1.1 ug/L after fresh soup.

references.authors: den Braver-Sewradj SP, van Spronsen R, Hessel EVS
references.title: Substitution of bisphenol A: a review of the carcinogenicity, reproductive toxicity, and endocrine disruption potential of alternative substances
references.finding: Data for BPS, BPAF and to a lesser extent BPF indicate a reproductive-toxicity hazard with a possible endocrine mode of action; most other BPA alternatives have data gaps.

references.authors: Duty SM, Ackerman RM, Calafat AM, et al.
references.title: Personal care product use predicts urinary concentrations of some phthalate monoesters
references.finding: Men who used cologne or aftershave in the previous 48 h had about double urinary MEP (265 vs 108 ng/mL); each additional personal-care product raised MEP by 33%.

references.authors: EFSA Panel on Food Contact Materials, Enzymes and Processing Aids (CEP), Silano V, Barat Baviera JM, et al.
references.title: Update of the risk assessment of di-butylphthalate (DBP), butyl-benzyl-phthalate (BBP), bis(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate (DEHP), di-isononylphthalate (DINP) and di-isodecylphthalate (DIDP) for use in food contact materials
references.finding: EFSA set a group TDI of 50 ug/kg bw/day (as DEHP equivalents) for DBP, BBP, DEHP and DINP based on reduced fetal testosterone; aggregated dietary exposure was 0.9-7.2 (mean) to 1.6-11.7 (high) ug/kg/day, up to 23% of the group TDI; assessment called temporary.

references.authors: EFSA Panel on Food Contact Materials, Enzymes and Processing Aids (CEP), Lambré C, Barat Baviera JM, et al.
references.title: Re-evaluation of the risks to public health related to the presence of bisphenol A (BPA) in foodstuffs
references.finding: EFSA lowered the BPA tolerable daily intake from 4 ug/kg to 0.2 ng/kg body weight per day (20,000-fold) based on Th17 immune effects in mice and concluded average and high dietary exposure exceed it by two to three orders of magnitude.

references.authors: Ehrlich S, Calafat AM, Humblet O, et al.
references.title: Handling of thermal receipts as a source of exposure to bisphenol A
references.finding: Handling thermal receipts for 2 h without gloves raised urinary BPA from 1.8 to 5.8 ug/L, peaking at 8-12 h; nitrile gloves prevented a significant rise.

references.authors: European Commission
references.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/3190 of 19 December 2024 on the use of bisphenol A (BPA) and other bisphenols and bisphenol derivatives in materials and articles intended to come into contact with food
references.journal: Official Journal of the European Union
references.finding: Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/3190 bans BPA and its salts in food contact materials (plastics, coatings, varnishes, inks, adhesives, rubbers), with an 18-month transition to 20 July 2026 for most single-use items and 36 months (to 20 January 2028) for some uses; other hazardous bisphenols need authorization.

references.authors: Faber WD, Deyo JA, Stump DG, et al.
references.title: Developmental toxicity and uterotrophic studies with di-2-ethylhexyl terephthalate
references.journal: Birth Defects Res B Dev Reprod Toxicol
references.finding: Guideline developmental toxicity studies of DEHTP in rats (up to 747 mg/kg/day) and mice found no malformations or effects on implantation or fetal weight, and no estrogenic activity in a uterotrophic assay.

references.authors: Ferguson KK, Cantonwine DE, Rivera-González LO, et al.
references.title: Urinary phthalate metabolite associations with biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress across pregnancy in Puerto Rico
references.n: 54 women (oxidative stress) / 120 women (inflammation), PROTECT Puerto Rico
references.finding: Across repeated pregnancy samples, all phthalate metabolites were associated with higher urinary 8-isoprostane and 8-OHdG; IQR rises in MBP and MiBP went with about 49-50% higher 8-isoprostane.

references.authors: Ferguson KK, McElrath TF, Chen YH, et al.
references.title: Urinary phthalate metabolites and biomarkers of oxidative stress in pregnant women: a repeated measures analysis
references.n: 482 pregnant women (130 preterm cases, 352 controls; LIFECODES)
references.finding: Interquartile rises in urinary phthalate metabolites were associated with higher urinary 8-OHdG and 8-isoprostane across up to four samples per woman, more strongly for MBzP, MBP and MiBP than DEHP metabolites.

references.authors: Ferguson KK, Cantonwine DE, McElrath TF, et al.
references.title: Repeated measures analysis of associations between urinary bisphenol-A concentrations and biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress in pregnancy
references.finding: An interquartile rise in urinary BPA was associated with 5-9% higher 8-OHdG and 8-isoprostane and 9% higher plasma IL-6 across repeated pregnancy samples.

references.authors: Ferguson KK, Chen YH, VanderWeele TJ, et al.
references.title: Mediation of the Relationship between Maternal Phthalate Exposure and Preterm Birth by Oxidative Stress with Repeated Measurements across Pregnancy
references.n: 482 pregnant women (130 preterm cases, 352 controls; LIFECODES)
references.finding: Counterfactual mediation analysis: 8-isoprostane mediated an estimated 47-60% of the association between the DEHP metabolite MECPP and preterm birth (total OR 1.48-1.67).

references.authors: Foster PM
references.title: Disruption of reproductive development in male rat offspring following in utero exposure to phthalate esters
references.finding: Review of rat studies: in-utero DBP, DEHP and BBP lower fetal testicular testosterone and INSL3, causing the 'phthalate syndrome' of hypospadias, cryptorchidism, malformed accessory glands, retained nipples and shorter anogenital distance.

references.authors: Friedman A, Welch BM, Keil AP, et al.
references.title: Periods of susceptibility for associations between phthalate exposure and preterm birth: Results from a pooled analysis of 16 US cohorts
references.finding: In the same pooled data, DEHP-metabolite associations with preterm birth were strongest for first- and second-trimester exposure (MEHP OR 1.15 and 1.11 per IQR) and null in the third trimester.

references.authors: Galloway TS, Baglin N, Lee BP, et al.
references.title: An engaged research study to assess the effect of a 'real-world' dietary intervention on urinary bisphenol A (BPA) levels in teenagers
references.finding: A self-designed 7-day diet to avoid BPA did not lower urinary BPA overall (p=0.25); participants found BPA-free food hard to identify and unlikely to sustain.

references.authors: Gerofke A, Lange R, Vogel N, et al.
references.title: Phthalates and substitute plasticizers: Main achievements from the European human biomonitoring initiative HBM4EU
references.finding: Health-based biomonitoring guidance values were exceeded in up to 5% of participants; for about 17% of children and teens, a mixture risk from five reprotoxic phthalates could not be excluded; food and personal-care products were main sources.

references.authors: Hagobian T, Smouse A, Streeter M, et al.
references.title: Randomized Intervention Trial to Decrease Bisphenol A Urine Concentrations in Women: Pilot Study
references.finding: A 3-week intervention (BPA-free products, glass containers, weekly counselling) lowered creatinine-adjusted urinary BPA vs control (treatment x time p=0.04).

references.authors: Harley KG, Kogut K, Madrigal DS, et al.
references.title: Reducing Phthalate, Paraben, and Phenol Exposure from Personal Care Products in Adolescent Girls: Findings from the HERMOSA Intervention Study
references.finding: Three days of personal-care products free of phthalates, parabens, triclosan and BP-3 lowered urinary MEP by 27% and methyl/propyl paraben by about 44-45%; MnBP and MiBP did not change.

references.authors: Harray AJ, Lucas AD, Herrmann SE, et al.
references.title: Low-plastic diet and urinary levels of plastic-associated phthalates and bisphenols: the randomized controlled PERTH Trial
references.finding: A 7-day diet of food sourced to minimize plastic contact, with plastic-free kitchenware and personal-care products, cut urinary MnBP by 37.5%, MBzP by 53.5% and BPA by 59.7% vs no intervention; personal-care swaps alone lowered MnBP; Minderoo-funded.

references.authors: Hauser R, Duty S, Godfrey-Bailey L, et al.
references.title: Medications as a source of human exposure to phthalates
references.finding: A man taking enteric-coated mesalamine (Asacol) had urinary MBP of 16,868 ng/mL, more than two orders of magnitude above the NHANES 95th percentile.

references.authors: Heindel JJ, Belcher S, Flaws JA, et al.
references.title: Data integration, analysis, and interpretation of eight academic CLARITY-BPA studies
references.finding: Integration of eight academic CLARITY-BPA studies on the same animals: developmental BPA affected brain, prostate, urinary tract, ovary, mammary gland and heart, often at the lowest dose (2.5 ug/kg/day) and non-monotonically.

references.authors: Hernández-Díaz S, Mitchell AA, Kelley KE, et al.
references.title: Medications as a potential source of exposure to phthalates in the U.S. population
references.finding: Users of mesalamine formulations that may contain DBP had mean urinary MBP 50 times higher than non-users (2,257 vs 46 ug/L); some didanosine, omeprazole and theophylline products were linked to higher MEP.

references.authors: Hormann AM, Vom Saal FS, Nagel SC, et al.
references.title: Holding thermal receipt paper and eating food after using hand sanitizer results in high serum bioactive and urine total levels of bisphenol A (BPA)
references.finding: Holding thermal receipt paper right after using a hand sanitizer with penetration enhancers, then eating fries by hand, raised serum unconjugated BPA to about 7 ng/mL within 90 min.

references.authors: Hutter HP, Kundi M, Hohenblum P, et al.
references.title: Life without plastic: A family experiment and biomonitoring study
references.finding: After a family removed plastics from their home, urinary BPA was below quantification, but over two further months phthalate metabolites fell in some members and rose in the mother.

references.authors: Hyman S, Acevedo J, Giannarelli C, et al.
references.title: Phthalate exposure from plastics and cardiovascular disease: global estimates of attributable mortality and years life lost
references.finding: Burden model applying a US hazard ratio to regional DEHP exposure estimates: 356,238 cardiovascular deaths in 2018 (13.5% of CVD deaths at ages 55-64) attributed to DEHP; funded by Bloomberg Philanthropies, Beyond Petrochemicals and NIH.

references.authors: Hyman S, Acevedo J, Trasande L
references.title: Preterm birth attributable to exposure to chemicals used in plastic materials: a global estimate
references.finding: Burden model applying a hazard ratio from a previous cohort to global exposure estimates: 1.97 million preterm births in 2018 (8.7% of the global total) attributed to DEHP.

references.authors: Jensen TK, Frederiksen H, Kyhl HB, et al.
references.title: Prenatal Exposure to Phthalates and Anogenital Distance in Male Infants from a Low-Exposed Danish Cohort (2010-2012)
references.finding: In a low-exposed cohort, no consistent associations were seen between any third-trimester phthalate metabolite and anogenital distance or penile width at 3 months.

references.authors: Jiang Y, Xu Y, Xiao S, et al.
references.title: Phthalate and DINCH exposure and ovarian reserve markers among women seeking infertility care
references.finding: Most conventional phthalate metabolites were inversely associated with antral follicle count, DINCH metabolites with higher FSH; the phthalate+DINCH mixture went with 8.6% lower AFC.

references.authors: Johns LE, Cooper GS, Galizia A, et al.
references.title: Exposure assessment issues in epidemiology studies of phthalates
references.finding: Phthalate metabolite half-lives are 3-18 h; intraclass correlations of repeated urine samples are about 0.3-0.6 for DEP, DBP, DiBP and BBzP metabolites and 0.1-0.3 for DEHP, DiNP and DiDP; US and German exposures to DEP, BBzP, DBP and DEHP declined after 2001.

references.authors: Knox KE, Schwarzman MR, Rudel RA, et al.
references.title: Trends in NHANES Biomonitored Exposures in California and the United States following Enactment of California's Proposition 65
references.finding: Median BPA fell 15% after California's Prop 65 listing while unlisted BPS rose 20% over the same period, suggesting substitution.

references.authors: Koch HM, Bolt HM, Angerer J
references.title: Di(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate (DEHP) metabolites in human urine and serum after a single oral dose of deuterium-labelled DEHP
references.finding: After a labelled DEHP dose, urinary metabolites peaked at 2-4 h; first-phase excretion half-lives were about 2 h and second-phase 5-10 h.

references.authors: Kortenkamp A, Martin O, Iacovidou E, et al.
references.title: Drivers of divergent assessments of bisphenol-A hazards to semen quality by various European agencies, regulators and scientists
references.finding: Analysis of why EFSA and the German BfR diverge: BfR proposed an alternative TDI 1,000-fold higher than EFSA's, based on adult sperm-count effects, and rejected the immunotoxicity endpoint; both agencies discounted gestational-exposure studies.

references.authors: Lange R, Apel P, Rousselle C, et al.
references.title: The European Human Biomonitoring Initiative (HBM4EU): Human biomonitoring guidance values for selected phthalates and a substitute plasticizer
references.finding: HBM4EU human-biomonitoring guidance values for adults, e.g. 0.5 mg/L urine for the sum of 5-oxo- and 5-OH-MEHP, 0.19 mg/L MnBP, 3 mg/L MBzP, 4.5 mg/L for DINCH metabolites.

references.authors: Lehmler HJ, Liu B, Gadogbe M, et al.
references.title: Exposure to Bisphenol A, Bisphenol F, and Bisphenol S in U.S. Adults and Children: The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2013-2014
references.finding: BPA, BPS and BPF were detected in 95.7%, 89.4% and 66.5% of urine samples; median adult BPA 1.24 ug/L vs 0.35-0.37 ug/L for BPF and BPS.

references.authors: Lessmann F, Kolossa-Gehring M, Apel P, et al.
references.title: German Environmental Specimen Bank: 24-hour urine samples from 1999 to 2017 reveal rapid increase in exposure to the para-phthalate plasticizer di(2-ethylhexyl) terephthalate (DEHTP)
references.finding: The DEHP substitute DEHTP went from under 10% detection before 2009 to 100% in 2017 (median 3.35 ug/L metabolite), still far below German guidance values (median intake 0.74 ug/kg/day vs TDI 1,000).

references.authors: Liu C, Duan P, Chen YJ, et al.
references.title: Mediation of the relationship between phthalate exposure and semen quality by oxidative stress among 1034 reproductive-aged Chinese men
references.finding: Every phthalate metabolite rose with urinary 8-OHdG, 8-isoPGF2a and HNE-MA; 8-isoPGF2a suggestively mediated 12% of the MBP-sperm concentration link and 8-OHdG 32% of the MEP-morphology link (p<0.10).

references.authors: Machtinger R, Gaskins AJ, Racowsky C, et al.
references.title: Urinary concentrations of biomarkers of phthalates and phthalate alternatives and IVF outcomes
references.finding: Higher DEHP metabolites were linked to fewer total, mature and fertilized oocytes and top-quality embryos, but no phthalate metabolite was linked to implantation, clinical pregnancy or live birth; DINCH metabolites showed no associations.

references.authors: Martínez Steele E, Khandpur N, da Costa Louzada ML, et al.
references.title: Association between dietary contribution of ultra-processed foods and urinary concentrations of phthalates and bisphenol in a nationally representative sample of the US population aged 6 years and older
references.finding: Urinary DiNP, mCNP, mCPP, MBzP and BPF rose monotonically across quintiles of ultra-processed food intake.

references.authors: Mhaouty-Kodja S, Zalko D, Tait S, et al.
references.title: A critical review to identify data gaps and improve risk assessment of bisphenol A alternatives for human health
references.finding: BPS and BPF are now found in people worldwide and are being regulated for toxicity; newer BPA alternatives have large toxicology data gaps (regrettable substitution).

references.authors: Oh J, Choi JW, Ahn YA, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics of bisphenol S in humans after single oral administration
references.finding: Oral BPS was absorbed within about 1 h and excreted with a terminal half-life under 7 h (6.8 h).

references.authors: Oskar S, Mook J, Smith MK, et al.
references.title: Temporal trends in phthalate metabolite exposure of girls in the United States across sociodemographic factors and intersectional social identities: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2001-2018
references.finding: Low- and high-molecular-weight phthalate metabolites declined between 2001 and 2018, with persistent sociodemographic differences in low-molecular-weight phthalates.

references.authors: Peng CY, Tsai EM, Kao TH, et al.
references.title: Canned food intake and urinary bisphenol a concentrations: a randomized crossover intervention study
references.finding: A canned-food meal raised urinary BPA by up to 206% at 4 h, returning to baseline by 24 h.

references.authors: Plachetka L, Stanislas V, Bauer A, et al.
references.title: Urinary bisphenol levels and blood pressure after soda consumption from cans, PET and glass bottles
references.finding: Soda from cans raised urinary BPA by 22% vs PET bottles; BPS, BPF and BPE appeared regardless of packaging.

references.authors: Potts C, Harbolic A, Murphy M, et al.
references.title: A common phthalate replacement disrupts ovarian function in young adult mice
references.finding: In young adult mice, 10 days of oral DEHTP (from 10 ug/kg) altered ovarian follicle counts and gene expression, and DEHTP/MEHTP slowed follicle growth in vitro.

references.authors: Prueitt RL, Goodman JE
references.title: WITHDRAWN: Letter to editor: Evidence evaluated by EFSA does not support lowering the temporary tolerable daily intake for bisphenol A
references.finding: RETRACTED/WITHDRAWN letter arguing EFSA's evidence did not support lowering the BPA TDI; withdrawn at the request of the author(s) and/or editor. Cited only to flag it.

references.authors: Radke EG, Glenn BS, Braun JM, et al.
references.title: Phthalate exposure and female reproductive and developmental outcomes: a systematic review of the human epidemiological evidence
references.finding: EPA systematic review: moderate evidence linking DEHP, DBP and DEP to preterm birth; slight or indeterminate evidence for time to pregnancy, puberty and spontaneous abortion.

references.authors: Rochester JR, Bolden AL
references.title: Bisphenol S and F: A Systematic Review and Comparison of the Hormonal Activity of Bisphenol A Substitutes
references.finding: BPS and BPF have hormonal potency in the same order of magnitude as BPA (estrogenic, antiestrogenic, androgenic, antiandrogenic); authors employed by TEDX, an endocrine-disruption advocacy nonprofit.

references.authors: Rudel RA, Gray JM, Engel CL, et al.
references.title: Food packaging and bisphenol A and bis(2-ethyhexyl) phthalate exposure: findings from a dietary intervention
references.finding: Three days of fresh, unpackaged food cut urinary BPA by 66% and DEHP metabolites by 53-56% (geometric means).

references.authors: Sathyanarayana S, Alcedo G, Saelens BE, et al.
references.title: Unexpected results in a randomized dietary trial to reduce phthalate and bisphenol A exposures
references.finding: A 5-day catered 'low-exposure' diet unexpectedly raised urinary DEHP metabolites (to an estimated intake above EPA and EFSA limits for children) because ingredients such as ground coriander and milk were contaminated.

references.authors: Silva MJ, Wong LY, Samandar E, et al.
references.title: Exposure to di-2-ethylhexyl terephthalate in the U.S. general population from the 2015-2016 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
references.finding: DEHTP metabolites were detected in 96-99.9% of the US population; levels rose with household income and were higher in females and children.

references.authors: Stahlhut RW, Welshons WV, Swan SH
references.title: Bisphenol A data in NHANES suggest longer than expected half-life, substantial nonfood exposure, or both
references.finding: Urinary BPA barely fell with longer fasting (population-based half-life 43 h), suggesting substantial non-food exposure, storage, or both.

references.authors: Sturgeon SR, Flynn D, Kaiser AB, et al.
references.title: Urinary levels of phthalate metabolites and cardiovascular disease mortality (NHANES, 1999-2008)
references.finding: No urinary phthalate metabolite was associated with cardiovascular mortality (top vs bottom quartile HRs 0.73-1.4, all non-significant; 175 CVD deaths).

references.authors: Swan SH, Main KM, Liu F, et al.
references.title: Decrease in anogenital distance among male infants with prenatal phthalate exposure
